discussions.prompt: This record routes two independent paths to immune evasion -- complement-regulator binding by surface proteins, and effector delivery through the T3SS. In a given host, is either route sufficient on its own, or does established infection require both?
discussions.rationale: The graph draws both arrows into the same node without saying whether they are alternatives or partners. If either is sufficient, single-target antivirulence strategies are viable; if evasion needs both, only combination approaches will work, and the two edges should carry that dependency rather than reading as parallel routes.

label: bacterial cannibalism
definition: A predatory bacterial phenotype in which cells kill susceptible conspecific cells and obtain nutrients from the killed cells.

evidence.snippet: The sporulating cells feed on the nutrients thereby released, which allows them to keep growing rather than to complete morphogenesis.
evidence.notes: Gonzalez-Pastor et al. (2003), PMID:12817086, scientific abstract directly retrieved from Europe PMC. The author-posted main text at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/10699307_Cannibalism_by_Sporulating_Bacteria was also read. It reports sibling killing in the PY79 laboratory background, while the nutritional explanation is proposed from killing and sporulation phenotypes, not traced nutrient uptake. The snippet preserves the abstract's stronger wording without upgrading that inference. Actual figures and supplements were not inspected; no numerical or protein-resolved claim is imported.

evidence.snippet: Cannibal cells express the skf and sdp toxin systems to lyse a fraction of their sensitive siblings.
evidence.notes: Lopez et al. (2009), PMID:19775247, PMC2983100, scientific Summary, directly checked in NCBI BioC full text at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC2983100/unicode. Results, Discussion and Experimental Procedures were read. NCIB3610 is the wild-type background; prominent hypercannibal phenotypes concern engineered derivatives. Nutrient-mediated sporulation delay remains an interpretation, not a nutrient-flux measurement. Actual figures and supplements were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: our data challenge the established role of cannibalism-dependent killing as the mechanism behind this sporulation delay.
evidence.notes: Friebel et al. (2026), PMID:42294941, PMC13343845.1, published 2026-06-15, IMPORTANCE section, not the scientific Abstract. Directly checked against Europe PMC full-text XML and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13343845.1/. Results, Discussion and Methods were read; actual figures and supplements were not inspected. DK1042 is an NCIB3610-derived laboratory background. Biofilm differentiation and membrane-integrity readouts do not directly establish nutrient transfer. This is counterevidence to a universal killing-based explanation, not a new positive demonstration of the nutritional phenotype.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish nutritional cannibalism from broader developmental usage.
discussions.rationale: This class retains the classical killing-and-feeding sense. Friebel et al. 2026 also calls the wider toxin-dependent biofilm differentiation program cannibalism; that usage need not satisfy this narrower nutritional definition. The predatory bacterium parent traitmech:000054 fits this operational scope, not every phenotype assigned that name in the literature. Bacteriocin production traitmech:000183 requires neither conspecific killing nor feeding. Saprotrophy traitmech:000055 does not require killing the food source; natural competence traitmech:000087 concerns DNA uptake. Fratricide, programmed cell death, biofilm formation and sporulation delay are not exact synonyms. Resolve broader terminology and external mappings before adding xrefs; do not assume species-level disjointness.

discussions.prompt: Resolve direct feeding evidence and strain provenance before exemplar curation.
discussions.rationale: The cited studies support the term and sibling-killing biology but do not justify treating every toxin-positive population as a demonstrated nutritional cannibal. Obtain direct conspecific nutrient-use evidence, inspect the supplements and verify natural strain provenance before adding canonical examples. Gene presence, expression, inhibition zones, membrane damage and delayed sporulation alone are insufficient. Do not infer a protein-resolved causal graph from toxin names or sequence profiles. Mechanistic edges, protein accessions and canonical taxa are deliberately deferred.

label: bacterial mycophagy
definition: A trophic-ecology phenotype in which a bacterium actively obtains nutrients from living fungi or oomycetes and uses them for its own growth.

evidence.snippet: phenotypic behaviours that make available nutrients from living fungi and allow the conversion of living fungal biomass into bacterial biomass.
evidence.notes: Leveau and Preston 2008, PMID:18086226, section I, p. 860 (author PDF page 2), visually checked contiguous quotation. Definition authority, not experimental replication. Summary, section I, strategy overview and selected diagnostic passages in section III read; remaining review and referenced experiments not comprehensively assessed. Section I explicitly includes oomycetes while acknowledging they are not true fungi. Section III requires growth controls and distinguishes inferred nutrient acquisition from direct flux measurement. Author full text: https://leveau.faculty.ucdavis.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/220/2015/05/Leveau2008.pdf. DOI AND SRC:MED metadata matched PMID, title and DOI on 2026-10-11.

evidence.snippet: All Ter isolates proliferated in sand when hyphae of the fungi C. globosum, F. culmorum or M. hiemalis invaded.
evidence.notes: de Boer et al. 2004, PMID:15143036, Results, p. 860 (PDF page 4), visually checked quotation. Methods tested all isolates against intact living hyphae, using plate counts at three weeks corrected for uninoculated controls. Growth is indirect nutritional evidence, not isotope-traced transfer. Heat-fixed-hypha adhesion is a separate observation. Abstract, Introduction, Methods, relevant Results and taxonomic descriptions read; pages 4/7 visually inspected; supplement unread. Author full text: https://leveau.faculty.ucdavis.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/220/2015/05/deBoer2004.pdf. EXT_ID:15143036 AND SRC:MED matched source, ID, title and DOI on 2026-10-11.

evidence.snippet: The growth of collimonads did not cause a significant reduction in the Absidia biomass.
evidence.notes: Hoppener-Ogawa et al. 2009, PMID:18923455, scientific Abstract, directly matched. Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Table 1 and actual Figures 1/2 read; Figure 3 and supplement unread. Indigenous soil populations and a four-strain sand mixture grew with invading fungus; this is not individual strain proof or direct nutrient tracing. Nonsignificant biomass loss does not establish no fitness cost. Methods samples at three weeks, whereas Figure 2 caption names two and three; no time-specific quantitative claim adopted. Overlapping authors with 2004, not independent-group replication. Author full text: https://leveau.ucdavis.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/220/2015/05/HoppenerOgawa2009.pdf. EXT_ID:18923455 AND SRC:MED matched source, ID, title and DOI on 2026-10-11.

canonical_examples.note: Qualified to natural dune-soil isolate Ter6 (type strain, NCCB 100033 = LMG 21973), not every species member. Primary Methods establish provenance and hyphal-growth testing; species description on p. 863 identifies Ter6. Provenance: https://doi.org/10.1099/ijs.0.02920-0. NCBI species ID/name and Ter6 type material independently resolved on 2026-10-11: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=158899. discussions.prompt: Resolve exact mappings without conflating trophic endpoints.
discussions.rationale: Follow Leveau and Preston's active nutritional definition and explicit oomycete scope, without classifying oomycetes as true fungi or asserting experimentally demonstrated feeding on every target group. Merely consuming passive leaks or tissue dead through unrelated causes is excluded. Fungal inhibition, lysis, chitinase activity or a sequence annotation alone is insufficient. Killing and obligate fungal dependence are not required. Predatory bacterium traitmech:000054 requires bacterial prey; saprotrophy traitmech:000055 concerns dead material; parasitism traitmech:000043 requires host harm; phagotrophy traitmech:000628 requires particle ingestion. None is an established broader parent here. No organism-level disjointness is asserted. Unqualified mycophagy, fungivory and mycetophagy also cover nonbacterial organisms and are not exact synonyms. No exact xref or synonym assigned pending authority/scope reconciliation.

discussions.prompt: Resolve active nutrient acquisition and taxon-specific mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Causal graphs and protein examples are deferred, not claimed absent. Separate fungal damage, nutrient release and bacterial assimilation; require functional evidence and taxon-paired accessions before encoding protein mechanisms. CommunityMech CommunityMech:000364 led to DOI:10.1093/ismejo/wrag201 (PMID:42523014, PMC13615538). Its Abstract, antagonistic-assay Methods and mycophagy Results/Discussion passages were read: CFU after five days with sclerotia is compared with glass beads. This is a follow-up lead, not counted evidence of active feeding rather than released-nutrient consumption. Figures and supplement remain unread; no additional canonical taxon or independent replication is inferred from the assay name.

discussions.prompt: This record draws nitric oxide straight to biofilm dispersal with nothing in between, while c-di-GMP sits in the same graph wired only to the sessile state. Is the NO effect on dispersal mediated by lowering c-di-GMP, and should that intermediate be on the edge?
discussions.rationale: A bare `induces` edge from a diffusible signal to a community-scale outcome is a placeholder where a mechanism should be. The graph already carries c_di_gmp, but only as a promoter of sessile_state, so it cannot currently express the route most often proposed for this effect. The distinction is not academic: if dispersal runs through the c-di-GMP pool, then strains holding that pool high are intrinsically refractory to the NO-releasing antibiofilm agents now in development -- a resistance mechanism this graph has no way to represent while the edge stays bare.

discussions.prompt: BSL-2 requires a biosafety cabinet specifically for procedures with aerosol or splash potential, while other work may go on the open bench. Which procedures actually generate an infectious dose at the breathing zone, and does the current procedure list match them?
discussions.rationale: The bench/cabinet boundary is the single control that most BSL-2 work turns on, and it is drawn from procedure lists that long predate quantitative aerosol measurement. A procedure that is on the open bench but does generate respirable particles is an unrecognised exposure; one needlessly in the cabinet costs throughput. Either way the edge into biosafety_cabinet is asserting something measurable that has not been measured.

discussions.prompt: Every BSL-4 control this record requires assumes terrestrial gravity and somewhere to put contaminated air, water and waste -- suit overpressure, airlocks, chemical showers, specialized waste disposal. Which still contain an agent in a closed-loop habitat that recycles all three?
discussions.rationale: Sample-return and crewed-habitat missions need containment for agents with no countermeasure, which is exactly what BSL-4 is for. But every control edge runs outward from bsl4_trait to a piece of equipment -- `requires` an airlock, a decontamination shower, specialized waste disposal; `necessitates use of` a positive pressure suit -- so the controls are named as hardware rather than as the physics they rely on, and it is the physics that does or does not transfer. Sedimentation-dependent controls behave differently in microgravity, and a shower and a waste stream that both feed a recycling loop are not disposal. As written the record cannot distinguish a control that survives the move from one that does not, because it never says what any of them do.

label: collective bacterial predation
definition: A predatory bacterial phenotype in which cells act in coordinated multicellular groups to kill bacterial prey and obtain nutrients from the killed cells.

evidence.snippet: Myxococcus xanthus forages and moves collectively to prey and feed on other bacterial species.
evidence.notes: Rombouts et al. 2023, PMID:37696789, PMC10495355, scientific abstract, not the separate editor summary. Identity checked with EXT_ID:37696789 AND SRC:MED plus matching title and DOI. Results on cell-state transitions, A/S motility, trail following and prey lysis, Discussion and relevant Methods were read directly. Figure 5 and Supplementary Table 1 (p. 12) were visually inspected. The table identifies DZ2 laboratory material and engineered reporters or motility mutants; the paper's wild-type designation does not establish an untouched natural isolate. The prey is E. coli MG1655 with HU-mCherry for the lysis readout. Figure 5 measures prey fluorescence loss relative to an uninvaded zone, not direct nutrient assimilation or individual fitness benefits. Motility perturbations support contributions to efficient predation in this assay, not universal group obligacy. Raw movies and source data were not independently reanalyzed. MED and Crossref exposed a preprint relationship, not a linked correction/retraction; none was identified on the retrieved publisher page. Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-41193-x.

evidence.snippet: In addition to group hunting, individual M. xanthus cells are able to kill and lyse prey cells
evidence.notes: Zhang et al. 2020, PMID:31704687, PMC6974655, scientific ABSTRACT, not the separate IMPORTANCE text. Qualified MED identity and title/DOI checked. The PMC Results and Discussion subsections on post-killing behavior and conclusions, Methods strain table and tracking analysis were also read. This is primary counterevidence to obligate group-only killing: DK1622 cells can kill E. coli individually. Prey-fragment consumption inferences do not constitute a direct assimilation assay. The delta-aglZ analysis also included individuals in groups of two or three and is not uniformly a solitary-cell dataset. This paper is boundary evidence, not independent replication of the 2023 collective-motility experiment. MED and Crossref exposed no linked correction/retraction; publisher access returned HTTP 403, leaving publisher notice status unverified. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6974655/.

discussions.prompt: Keep coordinated group feeding distinct from claims of obligatory cooperation.
discussions.rationale: Predatory bacterium traitmech:000054 supplies killing and nutrition; coordinated multicellular predation supplies the differentia. Mere cell density, aggregation, motility or prey lysis without feeding is insufficient. This is a capability expressed by cells in a group context, not a claim that a lone cell displays a collective phenotype. It does not require every cell to attack one prey simultaneously or benefit equally. Solitary killing and collective feeding can coexist in the same organism; no obligate group dependence or disjointness is asserted. Cooperative predation and wolf-pack predation are not assigned exact synonym status: cooperation in an evolutionary fitness sense requires separate evidence. The 2023 scout/loner/swarm bins are analysis states, not distinct primary traits. Swarming motility traitmech:000062 is explicitly flagella-dependent; gliding METPO:1000706 and twitching traitmech:000061 do not require predation. Epibiotic, periplasmic and cytoplasmic predation classify predator location, not group organization. No exact xrefs or synonyms are assigned.

discussions.prompt: Resolve natural examples and mechanism breadth without inferring feeding from sequence.
discussions.rationale: The directly inspected collective-imaging evidence concerns DZ2 laboratory material, engineered reporters and motility perturbations. Canonical examples remain unset pending natural material provenance and independently checked taxon identity. A- and S-motility contribute to the studied M. xanthus assay, but their combination is not imposed on every possible bearer of this trophic phenotype. A causal graph and protein examples are deferred until taxon-scoped machinery and mechanism boundaries are grounded. Motility genes, secretion systems, hydrolases or other sequence features alone do not establish coordinated prey consumption. Direct nutrient assimilation and individual fitness benefits require evidence beyond the reported fluorescence-loss readout. These limits are not evidence that collective predation is absent.

label: cytoplasmic bacterial predation
definition: A predatory bacterial phenotype in which a bacterium enters the cytoplasm of a bacterial prey cell and grows and reproduces there by consuming and degrading the prey cytoplasm.

evidence.snippet: Daptobacter penetrates both membranes of the prey cell walls and reproduces in their degrading cytoplasm.
evidence.notes: Guerrero et al. 1986, PMID:11542073, PMC323246, Figure 2E caption continued on p. 2141. Full five-page primary paper read from the Europe PMC PDF, including Methods, Results and Discussion, Table 2 and the note added in proof; actual Figure 2E/F micrographs and continued caption visually inspected. Enrichment-culture thin sections support prey-cytoplasmic invasion, degradation and division; these are not live-cell time courses or nutrient-tracing experiments. Figure 3 is a schematic, not additional experimental imaging. The scientific abstract was independently retrieved with EXT_ID:11542073 AND SRC:MED and title/DOI checked. MED and Crossref exposed no linked correction/retraction; publisher notice access returned HTTP 403, so that status is unverified. Source: https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC323246?pdf=render.

evidence.snippet: invade their host cells and replicate in the cytoplasm, consuming their prey from the inside out
evidence.notes: LPSN genus Daptobacter, Notes, directly retrieved 2026-10-11. LPSN quotes this description from Madigan et al. 2019; that book was not independently read. Supports established terminology, not independent experimental replication of Guerrero et al. LPSN marks the genus name not validly published and preferred rather than correct. Its permanent record link is https://doi.org/10.83108/rn.684. The nomenclatural record is not evidence for a sequence-defined lineage or an NCBITaxon mapping.

discussions.prompt: Keep prey-cytoplasmic feeding distinct from generic intracellular residence.
discussions.rationale: Predatory bacterium traitmech:000054 supplies the broader trophic phenotype. Periplasmic bacterial predation traitmech:000699 has a different replication compartment; epibiotic bacterial predation traitmech:000697 keeps the predator cell body external. Generic endobiotic or intracellular predation, endoparasitism and endosymbiosis are not exact synonyms. Guerrero et al. discuss predator/parasite and primary-consumer terminology on pp. 2141-2142; the operational feeding/location definition here does not settle that broader ecological vocabulary. Entry alone or intracellular growth without destructive prey consumption is insufficient. No organism-level disjointness, fixed prey range or obligate prey dependence is asserted. Exact synonyms and authority-backed xrefs remain unassigned pending scope reconciliation.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the historical isolate and its mechanism before grounding examples.
discussions.rationale: The primary study describes Daptobacter in lake-derived enrichment cultures and reports axenic growth; it does not make cytoplasmic predation an obligate lifestyle. No exact NCBITaxon identity for the observed material has been established in this curation, so canonical_examples is intentionally omitted. LPSN nomenclature does not supply that missing mapping. The second evidence item is terminology support, not another experiment. Protein-resolved mechanism, modern replication and lineage breadth remain open; do not infer causal machinery from a taxon name, sequence prediction or the different Bdellovibrio model. No causal graph or protein examples are proposed.

discussions.prompt: Two edges reach genome reduction here: confined habitat through metabolic gene loss, and the trait itself, whose description bundles drift in as `with small Ne`. The nodes that would give drift a mechanism -- transmission bottleneck, limited recombination -- connect to neither. Should they feed the drift edge, and which mechanism dominates?
discussions.rationale: The record asserts both mechanisms but at different resolutions, which is what makes them impossible to weigh. Drift arrives bundled into a trait-level edge as a parenthetical -- `with small Ne` inside a description -- while selection is spelled out as a two-step path through metabolic_gene_loss. transmission_bottleneck and limited_recombination attach to each other and to nothing else, so the drift claim has no mechanism under it, and host_symbiont_aa_complementarity -> nutritional_compensation is likewise its own disconnected pair, so compensation is not wired into reduction either. The two predict opposite loss spectra -- drift removes genes roughly regardless of function, compensation removes exactly the genes whose products the host supplies -- so until they are stated at the same resolution the graph cannot say what a newly sequenced symbiont will have lost, which is most of what a reduction model is for.
discussions.notes: Scan provenance (#409). The kg-microbe-kgscan pass raised this discussion with the prompt 'Knowledge gap for endosymbiosis: Growth anomalies (GAs) are coral diseases characterised by tumour-like skeletal lesions reported globally, yet their causes remain poorly understood.', whose sentence came from PMID:42130304. That sentence is about growth anomalies in corals, not about this trait: the scan matched the hedging vocabulary of a gap statement without checking that the gap was about the trait it was filed under. The prompt above was authored instead from this record's own causal graph, and none of these references are carried as its evidence, because they support the scraped sentence rather than the question. The scan attached 3 further references whose snippets concern neither that sentence nor this trait; all 4 are reproduced here so nothing it produced is lost: PMID:42130304 'Growth anomalies (GAs) are coral diseases characterised by tumour-like skeletal lesions reported globally, yet their causes remain poorly understood.'; PMID:41612704 'Disrupting this obligate symbiosis represents a promising pest control strategy, yet the molecular mechanisms maintaining host-symbiont homeostasis remain poorly understood.'; PMID:40831140 'This review explores the origin and evolution of plastids, their protein-import machinery, compartmentalization, and interactions with other cellular compartments, and highlights key unanswered questions in these areas.'; PMID:41764142 'Detritivorous E. murphyi larvae can increase soil nitrogen levels by up to five times compared with similar uncolonized substrates, although the mechanisms involved remain unknown.'.

label: epibiotic bacterial predation
definition: A predatory bacterial phenotype in which a bacterium kills and obtains nutrients from bacterial prey while attached and growing externally, without its cell body entering the prey cell.

evidence.snippet: epibiotic, where they attach to the prey from outside.
evidence.notes: Pasternak et al. 2014, PMID:24088628, PMC3930308, Introduction; contiguous quotation defining the external predation strategy. Abstract, Introduction, culture/prey-range/electron-microscopy Methods, growth Results, Discussion and actual Figure 1 read. JSS and Micavibrio aeruginosavorus EPB observations support external feeding; genome comparisons are not functional proof. Do not make the paper's binary-division generalization defining: the 2024 JSS time-lapse study demonstrates nonbinary division. Other figures, genomic analyses and supplements not fully assessed. Full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3930308/.

evidence.snippet: No periplasmic growth stage was observed and no bdelloplast was formed.

JSS was isolated from sewage in London, Ontario, with Caulobacter crescentus prey; attached external predation left emptied cells. This supports natural strain provenance and noninvasive feeding, not its frequency in undisturbed sewage. Full text, figures and supplement unavailable to this review; no Methods claim imported. Publisher: https://doi.org/10.1099/ijs.0.039701-0.

evidence.snippet: Bdellovibrio exovorus is an obligate epibiotic predator that attaches on the prey cell surface, where it grows and proliferates.
evidence.notes: Santin et al. 2024, PMID:38678033, PMC11055950, scientific Abstract; direct contiguous match. Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, selected culture/killing/live-imaging/cryo-EM/statistics Methods and actual Figures 2-5 read; other Methods, actual Figures 1/6, supplements and movies not fully assessed. JSS time-lapse growth and prey-content loss support feeding, not direct molecular nutrient tracing. The 2025 correction DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-58758-7 (PMID:40234419, PMC12000597) was read: retain its qualified prey-range wording and removal of the S-layer-defense recommendation. It is not another independent experiment. Full corrected text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11055950/.

canonical_examples.note: Qualified to JSS (ATCC BAA-2330 = DSM 25223), not every species member. Studied as Bdellovibrio exovorus on C. crescentus; the predator's natural sewage-isolate provenance and type-strain identity are stated in the primary Abstract at https://doi.org/10.1099/ijs.0.039701-0. Some 2024 prey strains carry engineered labels or deletions; this natural-provenance qualification concerns the predator. NCBI species ID/name and JSS type material independently resolved on 2026-10-11: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=453816.

discussions.prompt: Keep external feeding distinct from general surface association.
discussions.rationale: Predatory bacterium traitmech:000054 supplies killing and nutrition; external attachment and growth supply the differentia. The broader METPO:1007093 epibiont phenotype does not require predation. Epibiosis, ectosymbiosis, ectoparasitism and vampirism are not asserted exact synonyms. The existing predation research report also calls wolf-pack Myxococcus feeding epibiotic; this record follows the attached-feeding sense of Pasternak et al., not every use of external killing. Attachment, prey lysis or sequence signatures alone are insufficient. Bacterial cannibalism traitmech:000626 concerns prey relatedness, an orthogonal axis. No organism-level disjointness is asserted. No exact xrefs or synonyms are assigned pending authority and scope reconciliation.

discussions.prompt: Resolve feeding machinery without generalizing model-specific observations.
discussions.rationale: Causal graphs and protein examples are deferred, not claimed absent. An external predator cell body does not exclude envelope-crossing feeding structures or secreted effectors. JSS imaging supports a feeding junction but does not identify its molecular machinery; fluorescence loss is not direct nutrient tracing. Comparative gene content is not functional causality. Do not require polar attachment, binary division, fixed progeny number, a universal prey range, or obligate dependence merely because particular models exhibit them. The corrected 2024 S-layer experiments concern tested prey backgrounds, not all predators or all S-layers. The 2013/2014 studies share authors and JSS material; three citations are not three independent laboratory replications.

edges.subject: trehalose_biosynthesis
edges.description: Trehalose accumulation through the OtsAB pathway is required for free-living osmotic stress tolerance: losing the pathway reduces viability under both nonionic and ionic hyperosmotic challenge, and supplying trehalose restores it.

evidence.snippet: the Δ(otsCB-otsA) mutant showed reduced viability under these stress conditions similar to the ΔecfG mutant
evidence.notes: Free-living hyperosmotic challenge in Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens USDA 110: 400 mM sorbitol, 27 mM NaCl, 50 mM MgCl2, 75 mM MgSO4. The nonionic sorbitol condition is what separates osmotic pressure from salt-specific ion toxicity. Causality is pinned by two further controls: expressing a cytoplasmic trehalase (strain TreF-1) phenocopies the deletion, and exogenous trehalose rescues the otsA deletion but not the transporter-deficient otsCB-otsA or otsCB deletions, so the phenotype tracks intracellular trehalose rather than the locus.

evidence.snippet: the single, double, and triple mutant strains lacking the OtsAB pathway (the ΔotsA, ΔotsA ΔtreS or ΔotsA ΔtreY, and ΔotsA ΔtreS ΔtreY mutants) were inhibited for growth on 60 mM NaCl
evidence.notes: Independently constructed mutants in the same strain background (published as B. japonicum), so the phenotype does not depend on one construct. Mutants lacking both the OtsAB and TreYZ routes failed to grow on salt-containing medium. The same study found the low-trehalose otsA and otsA treY mutants were NOT worse than wild type under desiccation at 50% relative humidity, which is why this edge is scoped to osmotic tolerance rather than to environmental stress generally.

discussions.prompt: Ectoine and glycine betaine both enable osmotic stress tolerance here, but trehalose is wired instead to environmental stress tolerance -- a node with no outgoing edge. Is that split a real distinction, or does trehalose belong on the osmotic route too?
discussions.rationale: Because environmental_stress_tolerance has no outgoing edge, nothing downstream depends on trehalose at all: this record currently predicts the trait's osmotolerance from two systems and leaves the third dangling. Either reading has a consequence. If trehalose does serve osmotic tolerance, a genome carrying only trehalose scores as non-osmotolerant when it is not, which is exactly the inference anything reading habitat range off gene content would make. If the split is real -- trehalose for desiccation and thermal stress rather than osmolarity -- then the dangling node needs its own edge onward to the trait. The second question, whether the two routes that do converge are redundant or condition-partitioned, rides along on the same experiment: their costs differ sharply, since de novo ectoine synthesis is carbon-expensive where betaine uptake is cheap given a precursor.
discussions.notes: Scan provenance (#409). The kg-microbe-kgscan pass raised this discussion with the prompt 'Knowledge gap for free-living: Interactions between parasites and the gut microbiota play a key role in immune responses and susceptibility to zoonotic diseases; however, many aspects of how protozoan infections alter microbial diversity and how these changes influence parasite pathogenicity and host defense remain poorly understood.', whose sentence came from PMID:41989588. That sentence is about protozoan infection and gut microbial diversity, not about this trait: the scan matched the hedging vocabulary of a gap statement without checking that the gap was about the trait it was filed under. The prompt above was authored instead from this record's own causal graph, and none of these references are carried as its evidence, because they support the scraped sentence rather than the question. The scan attached 3 further references whose snippets concern neither that sentence nor this trait; all 4 are reproduced here so nothing it produced is lost: PMID:41989588 'Interactions between parasites and the gut microbiota play a key role in immune responses and susceptibility to zoonotic diseases; however, many aspects of how protozoan infections alter microbial diversity and how these changes influence parasite pathogenicity and host defense remain poorly understood.'; PMID:42039802 'Engineered microbial assemblies tailored to specific host plants and environmental conditions have shown potential in stabilizing crop performance during drought, salinity, and nutrient limitations.'; PMID:41943163 'OBJECTIVES: Oxo-polyethylene (oxo-PE) is marketed as a biodegradable plastic, yet its environmental degradation remains poorly understood, particularly in marine contexts.'; PMID:42125129 "However, contradictions persist regarding pH's effect on microbial diversity, with unresolved questions about how specific environmental conditions regulate microbial taxa.".

proposed_experiments.name: Combinatorial solute-pathway knockouts across an environmental matrix
proposed_experiments.approach: combinatorial knockout panel with matrix growth phenotyping
model_systems: a free-living halotolerant isolate carrying all three systems
single, double, and triple pathway knockouts
perturbations: an osmolarity gradient spanning the growth range
low and high temperature at each osmolarity
carbon-replete versus carbon-limited medium
betaine precursor present or absent
readouts: growth rate and final yield across the matrix
intracellular solute pools by NMR or LC-MS
the osmolarity limit for each genotype
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: whether the trehalose knockout loses growth at high osmolarity specifically, with temperature and water activity held constant
proposed_experiments.would_support: trehalose loss costs nothing osmotically and only shows under desiccation or heat -- the split in the graph is real and environmental_stress_tolerance needs its own edge onward
proposed_experiments.would_refute: the trehalose knockout is osmotically impaired -- it belongs on the osmotic route with the other two

discussions.resolution_note: Refuted. The record's own would_refute criterion was 'the trehalose knockout is osmotically impaired', and it is: in Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens USDA 110 the otsCB-otsA deletion loses viability at 400 mM sorbitol, a nonionic challenge that separates osmotic pressure from ion toxicity, as well as at 27 mM NaCl, 50 mM MgCl2 and 75 mM MgSO4 (DOI:10.1128/mBio.00390-21). A cytoplasmic trehalase phenocopies the deletion and exogenous trehalose rescues the otsA deletion but not the transporter-deficient strains, so the phenotype tracks intracellular trehalose. Independently constructed mutants in the same background are inhibited on 60 mM NaCl (DOI:10.1128/AEM.02483-09). The split was therefore not real, and trehalose_biosynthesis now enables osmotic_stress_tolerance alongside ectoine and glycine betaine. Two things were deliberately NOT decided here and are tracked in issue 614: the weaker pre-existing trehalose_biosynthesis to environmental_stress_tolerance edge was retained rather than deleted, and the observation that the same AEM study found no desiccation defect for low-trehalose otsA mutants argues trehalose's role is specifically osmotic.

label: fungal nematode egg parasitism
definition: An animal-pathogenic phenotype in which a fungus infects nematode eggs by penetrating their eggshells and colonizing their interiors.

evidence.snippet: The egg-pathogenic fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum parasitizes on nematode eggs
evidence.notes: Xu et al. 2021, PMID:33897634, PMCID:PMC8058359, scientific Abstract; direct JATS match and native VERIFIED. Own JZD02 experiment, Methods and actual Figure 1 A-C support infection of Meloidogyne incognita eggs. Supplementary Table 1 defines infection by hyphal penetration through an individual egg, not mere surface contact. Its 30-hour printed mean disagrees with the replicate counts; no numerical infection rates are adopted. The 6-hour control and 42-hour infected transcriptomes differ in time and include mixed infection stages. Expression associations are not causal protein evidence.

evidence.snippet: Infected eggs by P. lilacinum 36-1.
evidence.notes: Xie et al. 2016, PMID:27486440, PMCID:PMC4949223, Figure 5 caption, panel B; actual panels A-C and Methods/Results inspected. P. lilacinum denotes Purpureocillium lilacinum. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT is retained. This is its own 36-1 infection experiment, not a repetition of Xu's citation. Eggs were supplied as the only nourishment for the reported 24-hour comparison, but microscopy does not quantify nutrient assimilation. RNA-seq replicates were pooled; gene homology and expression do not demonstrate a required effector.

evidence.snippet: Infection defined by Purpureocillium lilacinum mycelium penetrating through the whole individual Meloidogyne incognita egg
evidence.notes: Xu et al. 2021, Supplementary Table 1 footnote, Table_1.DOCX from the PMC8058359 Europe PMC supplementaryFiles archive. Direct DOCX text match and complete rendered page inspected; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT is retained. This operational scoring criterion supports individual-egg penetration, not another independent experiment or a direct nutrient-flux measurement. The two Xu excerpts total 23 words. The printed 30-hour mean discrepancy remains unresolved; no infection rate is imported.

discussions.prompt: Refine the egg-infection hierarchy without conflating infection, feeding and hatching endpoints.
discussions.rationale: The fungal bearer penetrates eggshells and colonizes egg interiors. Surface attachment, egg-hatching inhibition, killing, trapping or a gene annotation alone is insufficient. Animal pathogen METPO:1004002 is active below pathogenic to host METPO:1004000 and phenotype METPO:1000059. Its pinned organism-like wording is clarified as a phenotype in current upstream METPO; the local parent is not rewritten. Nematode egg infection does not entail mammalian pathogenicity. Xie describes this fungus as nematophagous, but the operational infection endpoint does not quantify feeding: fungal nematophagy traitmech:000719 requires consumption and also includes dead prey. It is related, not an asserted parent here. Local parasitism traitmech:000043 inherits persistent symbiosis, which is not required. No organism-level disjointness, obligacy, exclusive host stage or universal host range is asserted. Bare egg parasitism does not specify the fungal actor and is not an exact synonym.

discussions.prompt: Review the proposed class without reviving the obsolete parasitism identifier.
discussions.rationale: No exact active counterpart was identified in the inspected pinned/current releases, editor and template owners. Historical METPO:1000227 obsolete parasitism is broader, deprecated, under ObsoleteClass with OMO:0001000 reason and no replacement or consider annotation in those releases. METPO issue 521 disputes mechanically assigned reasons; the code neither invalidates the biology nor authorizes reuse. The historical ID is not revived or placed in xrefs. Fried-egg colony is unrelated. The ontology pin remains unchanged; v602 proposes this narrower infection phenotype with PROPOSED status and no equivalent external xref.

discussions.prompt: Resolve source inconsistencies and strain provenance before adding rates, examples or causal mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Xu Supplementary Table 1 reports a 30-hour mean of 38% for replicates 38%, 33% and 33%, whose arithmetic mean is about 34.7%. This discrepancy is preserved, not silently corrected. Its main Methods sample-level wording is less precise than the supplement's individual-egg penetration criterion. No rates or infection threshold are curated. Xie's conserved appressorium genes also occur in fungi lacking that structure; neither gene inventory nor differential expression establishes this trait or a protein-resolved mechanism. No causal graph, protein example or canonical taxon is asserted without further authority and strain-provenance checks. Microscopy and source-designated infection are not tracer measurements of nutrient flux. No field efficacy or safety claim follows. Source hashes, inspected figures/supplement, actual snippet verdicts and bounded notice checks are retained in the verification sidecar; no comprehensive correction/retraction clearance is claimed. Both counted primary experiments concern Purpureocillium lilacinum (JZD02 and 36-1). The fungal actor class is not evidence that this phenotype was experimentally demonstrated across fungal species; additional species require their own evidence.

label: fungal nematode endoparasitism
definition: An animal-pathogenic phenotype in which a fungus uses spores attached to or ingested by a vermiform nematode to initiate infection and then grows inside the host.

evidence.snippet: Drechmeria coniospora is an obligate fungal pathogen that infects nematodes via the adhesion of specialized spores to the host cuticle.
evidence.notes: Lebrigand et al. 2016, PMID:27153332, PMCID:PMC4859500, scientific Abstract. Direct JATS match and native VERIFIED. Author Summary and Discussion distinguish spore-initiated endoparasitism from hyphal traps and egg infection. Actual Figures 8 and 9 show recombinant fungal growth in C. elegans, not unmodified natural exemplars. S1 Text was fully read and visually checked: the laboratory line was serially passaged for about 15 years; its source isolate and ARSEF 6962 share provenance. Obligate is the authors' species description, not a universal class requirement or inability to grow on their artificial medium. Predicted genes and expression are not a universal mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Then, the fungal hyphae penetrate into the nematode body cavity and grow in the nematode body
evidence.notes: Sun et al. 2024, PMID:38248977, PMCID:PMC10820206, Results 3.2. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. Methods 2.5 and actual Figure 2c,d concern GFP-engineered HR-eGFP1 on Bursaphelenchus xylophilus; Figure 2 distinguishes attachment, entry, internal growth and emergence. The entire two-page supplement, including S1-S3, was inspected. Methods 2.6 scores attached spores or colonization as parasitism; no rate is imported as an internal-infection rate. Main-text intestinal infection after swallowing is tentative; do not silently strengthen it using the supplement caption. No field efficacy or safety is inferred.

evidence.snippet: The infection method for Harposporium cycloides was shown to be by spore ingestion.
evidence.notes: Glockling and Shimazu 1997, publisher scientific Abstract. Direct contiguous HTML match; DOI/title confirmed by Crossref and Europe PMC AGR:IND20619532. The native abstract resolver returned UNRESOLVED because it returned no abstract; this is not a missing-index claim. The primary abstract reports spore-ingestion infection in Harposporium cycloides and infectivity testing after pure culture. Full Methods, figures and host/strain provenance were not accessed; no canonical taxon, dose, route universality or pure-culture obligacy is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Refine the infection-strategy hierarchy without conflating infection, trapping and feeding.
discussions.rationale: The fungal bearer has the established spore-infection-strategy phenotype, not merely an anatomical location inside a nematode. The host-contacting or ingested spore is the infectious unit; spore germination into an external hyphal trap is not this route. Adhesion or ingestion alone, killing alone, internal occupancy without the specified route and sequence annotation are insufficient. Vermiform stages distinguish the selected strategy from eggshell penetration in fungal nematode egg parasitism traitmech:000726. Fungal nematophagy traitmech:000719 requires feeding and includes dead prey; fungal nematode trap formation traitmech:000718 concerns hyphal differentiation. Neither is asserted as a parent. Local parasitism traitmech:000043 inherits persistent symbiosis, not required here. Animal pathogen METPO:1004002 is active below pathogenic to host METPO:1004000 and phenotype METPO:1000059. Current upstream clarifies its pinned organism-like wording as a phenotype; the local parent remains unchanged. No organism-level disjointness, exclusive host stage, universal host range or obligacy is asserted. Bare endoparasitism does not specify the fungal actor, host or infection route and is not an exact synonym.

discussions.prompt: Review the proposed infection class without reviving the obsolete parasitism identifier.
discussions.rationale: No exact active counterpart was identified in inspected pinned/current releases, editor and six template owners. Historical METPO:1000227 obsolete parasitism is broader, deprecated, under ObsoleteClass with OMO:0001000 reason and no replacement or consider annotation in those releases. METPO issue 521 disputes mechanically assigned reasons; the code neither invalidates the biology nor authorizes reuse. The historical ID is not revived or placed in xrefs. The ontology pin remains unchanged; v603 proposes this narrower infection phenotype with PROPOSED status and no equivalent external xref. Existing bacterial endoparasitic predation is not this fungal spore-infection strategy.

discussions.prompt: Resolve assay endpoints and strain provenance before adding rates, canonical taxa or causal proteins.
discussions.rationale: Sun's Methods 2.6 counts attached spores or colonization; reported parasitism percentages are not curated as internal infection rates. Its imaged HR-eGFP1 is engineered, and morphological similarity to the wild type does not establish unchanged virulence. Its intestinal-route suggestion remains tentative; the distinct 1997 primary abstract supports ingestion in Harposporium cycloides. Lebrigand's S1 Text reports long laboratory passage and related isolate provenance, so these are not independent natural-strain exemplars. Predicted genes, expression and disputed assembly or mating-type interpretations are not required causal effectors. No canonical taxa, proteins or causal graph are asserted without further authority and strain-provenance work. Microscopy does not measure nutrient flux; no quantitative threshold, field efficacy or safety is inferred. The verification sidecar retains actual source locators, hashes and native verdicts; direct matching does not upgrade NOT_IN_ABSTRACT or UNRESOLVED. Full Glockling Methods and all raw experimental data were not accessed, and bounded notice checks are not comprehensive correction/retraction clearance.

No rates, canonical taxa or sequence-derived mechanism imported. label: fungal nematophagy
definition: A nutritional phenotype in which a fungus consumes nematodes as food.

evidence.snippet: Nematophagy implies the consumption of nematodes.
evidence.notes: Marlin et al. 2019, Introduction, PDF page 1: directly read terminology, not an independent experiment. The fungal actor qualifies the term; consumption, not paralysis alone, defines the endpoint. Publisher PDF visually checked. Native DOI abstract verifier: UNRESOLVED, retained separately from the direct match. Crossref and USDA identify the same DOI/title.

evidence.snippet: Susceptible rhabditid species (Poikilolaimus oxycercus) being consumed by Pleurotus ostreatus hyphae.
evidence.notes: Figure 2a caption, actual PDF page 6 and panel inspected, with Methods 2.1-2.3 and Results 3.2. This is a source-named feeding observation, not measured nutrient flux. Native verifier: UNRESOLVED. Host susceptibility is differential; neither all nematodes nor all Pleurotus isolates are asserted. The two excerpts from this paper total 17 words.

evidence.snippet: The saprophytic and predacious ability appeared not to be mutually exclusive.
evidence.notes: den Belder and Jansen 1994, Summary, PDF page 1, directly and visually matched. Selected Methods, Results and Discussion, including actual pages 6-8, describe Arthrobotrys oligospora CBS 289.82 feeding on living and previously killed Meloidogyne hapla juveniles. Internal hyphal occupancy is not a tracer assimilation assay. The excerpt supports nonexclusive feeding modes, not an exact rate. URL evidence is not run by the native DOI/PMID abstract verifier.

evidence.snippet: At mid to late time points, we observed hyphal growth inside nematodes following penetration of the cuticle, corresponding to digestion.
evidence.notes: Lin et al. 2023, PMID:37988381; Results subsection on late-time protease induction, publisher XML sec018. Native verifier: NOT_IN_ABSTRACT; exact full-text match. Actual Figure 5, Table 1 and S7 inspected. GFP-labeled reference TWF3407 is engineered, not an unmodified natural exemplar. Protease inhibition delays internal growth at 12 h without proving complete feeding loss or quantifying assimilation. Remaining figures and raw S1 spreadsheet were not fully audited.

canonical_examples.note: Qualified Figure 2a example: unnamed culture isolated from grocery-store mushrooms and identified morphologically, per Methods 2.1 at https://doi.org/10.3390/f10050404. The water-agar assay used 20 mixed-age nematodes and assessed this fungus after one week. No strain deposit, molecular identification or genetic provenance is inferred. NCBI EFetch resolved the species on 2026-10-13.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the broader feeding hierarchy without imposing a capture mechanism or carbon-specific endpoint.
discussions.rationale: Feeding on living or previously dead nematodes is included; fungal killing, obligacy and starvation are not universal requirements. Mere contact, paralysis, killing, trap formation or a sequence annotation alone is insufficient. Fungal nematode-trap formation (traitmech:000718) is structural, neither necessary nor sufficient for feeding. Mycoparasitism (traitmech:000717) has fungal prey; predatory bacterium (traitmech:000054) has a bacterial actor and prey. Phagotrophy (traitmech:000628), myzocytosis (traitmech:000631) and pallium feeding (traitmech:000632) impose different uptake modes. Saprotrophy (traitmech:000055) can overlap, without organism-level disjointness. Local parasitism (traitmech:000043) inherits persistent association, not required here. Keep phenotype METPO:1000059 pending a closer feeding hierarchy; no universal carbon, nitrogen or energy contribution is specified. Bare nematophagy includes nonfungal actors and is not an exact synonym. No unverified synonyms or xrefs are asserted.

discussions.prompt: Review upstream placement without reviving deprecated identifiers.
discussions.rationale: Pinned and current METPO lack an exact active counterpart in the inspected scope. Historical METPO:0000005 and METPO:000005 are deprecated and replace to active METPO:1000631 trophic type, a carbon/energy axis rather than this prey-defined feeding phenotype. METPO:1000644 is organic-carbon heterotrophy and METPO:1000731 concerns nutrient-availability adaptation. Deprecated METPO:0000261, METPO:000262 and METPO:1000125 concern fungal spores; METPO:1000227 is parasitism. No replacement or consider annotation was observed for those four. Their OMO:0001000 reasons neither invalidate biology nor authorize reuse. Historical IDs are not exact xrefs. The pinned ontology remains unchanged; v595 proposes the new class.

discussions.prompt: Resolve source inconsistencies and taxon-paired effectors before adding a causal graph.
discussions.rationale: Marlin's Table 2 conflicts with its Introduction on two host responses; Table 3 and Results differ for P. artyukhovskii. Those disputed host ranges are not imported. den Belder's Figure 2 panel labels/caption, Table 3 direction and significance notation disagree with prose; no numerical rates are adopted. Lin's Results uses mep1 where Table 1 and Figure 5 use mcp1; no protein identity is silently reconciled. Its linked DOI:10.1371/journal.pbio.3003178 is a later Update Article, not a correction or independent laboratory replication. Capture and digestion have distinct assays; expression associations do not establish universal effectors. No causal graph, protein example or chemical mechanism is asserted. Source-status checks are bounded: MDPI's notice page returned 403, and no comprehensive notice clearance is claimed. Source hashes, inspected sections and actual native verdicts are retained in the verification sidecar.

No exact active METPO counterpart identified. Other records unchanged. Timestamp is observed post-audit acceptance.

label: gut-associated
definition: A host association in which an organism is a persistent member of the gastrointestinal microbiota of an animal host, often contributing to host nutrition and physiology.

evidence.notes: Bäckhed et al. characterize the distal intestine as a dense microbial habitat whose residents provide metabolic capabilities to the host.
McFall-Ngai et al. support the gut as a major site of host-associated microbial communities across animals.

canonical_examples.note: Canonical human-gut-symbiont model (polysaccharide utilisation loci).

causal_graphs.title: Gut-associated lifestyle in the gastrointestinal microbiota
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This broad ecological, host-relationship, habitat, or hazard classification spans multiple taxa and mechanisms; contextual protein nodes do not receive token UniProt examples.
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed causal sketch linking gastrointestinal habitat to persistent gut-microbiota membership and host nutritional contributions.

nodes.description: Persistent retention/colonization in the duodenum and proximal small intestine.

edges.subject: gastrointestinal_habitat
edges.description: The intestinal environment supports persistent residency.

evidence.notes: Bäckhed et al. characterize the distal intestine as a dense microbial habitat.

edges.subject: gut_associated_trait
edges.description: Gut microbiota provide metabolic capabilities to the host.

evidence.notes: McFall-Ngai et al. support the gut microbiota as a metabolically consequential host-associated community.

edges.subject: adhesins
edges.description: Bacterial adhesins bind host receptors to enable adhesion.

evidence.notes: Adhesion primarily relies on adhesins; binding of bacterial adhesins to host receptors is a prerequisite for long-term colonization (Lin et al., 2024).

edges.subject: mucosal_adhesion
edges.description: Adhesion to mucus/epithelium is a prerequisite for long-term gut colonization.

evidence.notes: Adhesion emphasized as the prerequisite for persistence (adhesion -> growth -> reproduction) (Lin et al., 2024).

edges.subject: bile_acids
edges.description: Bile acids shape gut community via antimicrobial and detergent-like properties.

evidence.notes: Bile acids shape the gut microbiome composition due to antimicrobial and detergent-like properties, creating a harsh gut environment (McMillan et al., 2024).

edges.subject: bile_acids
edges.description: Small-intestinal bile salts inhibit growth of many bacteria.

evidence.notes: Bile salts and Paneth-cell antimicrobial peptides inhibit growth of many bacteria in the small intestine (Muramatsu & Winter, 2024).

edges.subject: antimicrobial_peptides
edges.description: Paneth-cell antimicrobial peptides inhibit growth of many small-intestinal bacteria.

evidence.notes: Antimicrobial peptides released by Paneth cells inhibit growth of many bacteria in the small intestine (Muramatsu & Winter, 2024).

edges.subject: peristalsis
edges.description: Strong peristalsis (plus bile/antimicrobials) makes the duodenum hostile to retention.

evidence.notes: The duodenum is hostile to retention due to bile, antimicrobials, and strong peristalsis (Lin et al., 2024).

edges.subject: luminal_oxygen_limitation
edges.description: Host limitation of luminal oxygen shelters a primary-fermenter-dominated community.

evidence.notes: During homeostasis, host functions that limit oxygen diffusion into the colonic lumen shelter a community dominated by primary fermenters (Lee et al., 2024).

edges.subject: primary_fermenter_community
edges.description: The anaerobic primary-fermenter community is the source of luminal butyrate; depleting it collapses butyrate and reconstituting it restores butyrate.

evidence.snippet: While inoculation with a community of 17 human Clostridia isolates resulted in a significant (P < 0.05) increase in butyrate levels
evidence.notes: The recolonisation arm of the discussion's decision rule. The converse was shown in the same study: streptomycin depletion of butyrate-producing Clostridia lowered cecal butyrate.

edges.subject: butyrate
edges.description: Butyrate is sensed by epithelial PPAR-gamma and drives colonocyte energy metabolism toward beta-oxidation, raising epithelial oxygen consumption.

evidence.snippet: Bacteria-derived butyrate affects epithelial O2 consumption and results in stabilization of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF), a transcription factor coordinating barrier protection
evidence.notes: Cell-culture work in the same study shows the effect is direct: epithelial metabolism of butyrate depletes local oxygen.

evidence.snippet: the depletion of butyrate-producing microbes by antibiotic treatment reduced epithelial signaling through the intracellular butyrate sensor peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPAR-γ)
evidence.notes: Identifies PPAR-gamma as the epithelial butyrate sensor.

edges.subject: colonocyte_oxidative_metabolism
edges.description: Colonocyte beta-oxidation consumes oxygen at the mucosa and so limits the oxygen reaching the lumen. SCOPE: this is a claim about mucosal-to-luminal oxygen flux and bioavailability, NOT about bulk centre-lumen anoxia.

evidence.snippet: Microbiota-induced PPAR-γ signaling also limits the luminal bioavailability of oxygen by driving the energy metabolism of colonic epithelial cells (colonocytes) toward β-oxidation
evidence.notes: States the closing step directly, and in terms of BIOAVAILABILITY rather than bulk concentration.

evidence.snippet: tributyrin supplementation restored epithelial hypoxia in streptomycin-treated mice
evidence.notes: Metabolite rescue: the oxygen change tracks butyrate, not the antibiotic, which is what makes the return arm causal rather than correlational.

evidence.snippet: Remarkably, measurements of luminal oxygen levels show nearly identical pO2 (partial pressure of oxygen) profiles in conventional and germ-free mice, pointing to the existence of oxygen consumption mechanisms other than microbial respiration
evidence.notes: BOUNDING EVIDENCE, attached deliberately so this edge cannot drift into claiming the microbiota creates the anaerobic gut. Direct pO2 measurement shows chemistry alone is sufficient to hold the lumen anaerobic: germ-free luminal contents consume oxygen via lipid oxidation, though more slowly than conventional contents. The source does NOT say microbes are irrelevant to bulk anoxia -- it concludes that 'both the microbes and the oxidative chemical reactions regulate luminal oxygen levels', and credits increased microbial biomass with the proximal-to-distal oxygen gradient. The bound is therefore about SOLE causation: this edge asserts a contribution to limiting mucosal-to-luminal oxygen flux, which is how the target node is defined, and must not be strengthened into sole responsibility for bulk centre-lumen anoxia.

discussions.prompt: This record commits to luminal oxygen limitation contributing to the primary fermenter community. Does the reverse arm hold too -- do the fermenters and the epithelium maintain the anoxia -- making this a feedback loop rather than the one-way edge drawn?
discussions.rationale: The existing edge is not wrong so much as half: it says the anoxic lumen permits the fermenters, and stops. If the return arm also holds, the two nodes are a self-reinforcing loop, and losing the fermenters raises luminal oxygen and admits facultative pathogens -- the collapse that follows antibiotic depletion. That is the clinically load-bearing half, and a graph of one-way edges can only carry it if someone draws it.
discussions.notes: Scan provenance (#409). The kg-microbe-kgscan pass raised this discussion with the prompt 'Knowledge gap for gut-associated: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small, noncoding RNAs involved in posttranscriptional gene regulation in both animal and plant. miRNAs derived from edible plants, referred to as xenomiRs, are proposed to cross-kingdom barriers and to modulate mammalian gene expression.', whose sentence came from PMID:40945860. That sentence is about plant-derived xenomiRs crossing kingdom barriers, not about this trait: the scan matched the hedging vocabulary of a gap statement without checking that the gap was about the trait it was filed under. The prompt above was authored instead from this record's own causal graph, and none of these references are carried as its evidence, because they support the scraped sentence rather than the question. proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: whether luminal oxygen rises when an established fermenter community is depleted, with colonisation order held constant
proposed_experiments.would_support: oxygen rises on depletion and falls again on re-colonisation -- the return arm is real and the pair is a loop
proposed_experiments.would_refute: oxygen is unchanged by depletion -- the habitat sets the anoxia and the single existing edge is the whole story

discussions.resolution_note: Supported, with two bounds. The would_support criterion was 'oxygen rises on depletion and falls again on re-colonisation', and both arms hold: streptomycin depletion of butyrate-producing Clostridia lowers cecal butyrate and raises epithelial oxygenation, tributyrin supplementation reverses it, and recolonisation with 17 human Clostridia isolates raises butyrate and restores colonocyte hypoxia (DOI:10.1016/j.chom.2016.03.004), replicated independently by DOI:10.1016/j.chom.2015.03.005. The pair is therefore a feedback loop, now modelled as such. Bound 1: the return arm is HOST-MEDIATED, running through butyrate and colonocyte beta-oxidation rather than direct microbial oxygen consumption (DOI:10.1126/science.aam9949), so the graph routes it through the new butyrate and colonocyte_oxidative_metabolism nodes rather than drawing a direct reverse edge. Bound 2: the community is NOT responsible for bulk centre-lumen anoxia -- direct phosphorescent-probe measurement finds germ-free and conventional mice nearly indistinguishable (DOI:10.1073/pnas.1718635115) -- so the closing edge is scoped to mucosal-to-luminal oxygen flux and carries that source as bounding evidence. Left open and tracked in issue 617: whether abiotic luminal oxygen consumption deserves its own node, and whether this component should attach to the trait node, which no current source supports.

definition: A trophic-ecology phenotype in which filamentous bacteria capture microbial prey on their cell surface and kill the captured cells to obtain prey-derived nutrients.

evidence.snippet: Single-cell analyses with stable isotope-labeled prey revealed that prey components are taken up by the attacker.
evidence.notes: Lien et al. 2024, PMID:39418385, scientific Abstract, not the separate article summary; directly matched source-qualified MED text. Introduction and contact/capture Results support the surface-trapping differentia. Nutrient-uptake Results, culture, killing, imaging and Raman Methods, Discussion and actual Figures 1, 5 and 6 read. label: kin discrimination
definition: An ecological phenotype in which microbial cells preferentially associate with kin or exclude nonkin through differential interactions according to genetic similarity or relatedness.

evidence.snippet: Our findings demonstrate that D. discoideum cells co-aggregate more with genetically similar than dissimilar individuals
evidence.notes: Ostrowski et al. 2008, PMID:19067487; scientific abstract, publisher PDF page 1, contiguous span visually checked. Mixtures with AX4-GFP and natural-isolate dye controls support partial sorting during aggregation, not complete clonal exclusion. The measured endpoint is variation in fluorescent spore proportions among fruiting bodies; genetic distance uses 12 microsatellite loci, not genome-wide identity. Main text and all four figures were inspected; Figure 1 is hypothetical. Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 were read by text extraction. Main Methods names QS45, absent from the retrieved S1 strain table; no strain alias is inferred. Kin-selected benefit is an interpretation, not a measured fitness endpoint here. Natural provenance of every laboratory derivative and a molecular recognition mechanism remain unresolved. Native abstract verifier: VERIFIED.

evidence.snippet: Some swarms did merge, and most interestingly, this behavior was only seen in the most highly related strain pairs.
evidence.notes: Stefanic et al. 2015, PMID:26438858, PMC4653157; directly retrieved scientific abstract from Europe PMC with the namespace-qualified query EXT_ID:26438858 AND SRC:MED. Title, PMID and DOI were checked together. The authors define a conspecific scope and report relatedness-associated swarm merging versus boundary formation among sympatric Bacillus subtilis isolates. The separately reported root-colonization outcome is not a direct killing measurement. Full text, figures and supplements were inaccessible and are not claimed as inspected; indexed search passages were not used as excerpts or quantitative evidence. Native abstract verifier: VERIFIED. Linked PMID:26512099 is commentary, not a correction or experimental replication.

evidence.snippet: The effects of kin discrimination extend to nearby species, as the other subtilis clade species were treated with the same antagonism as nonkin.
evidence.notes: Lyons and Kolter 2017, PMID:28679746, PMC5573675; scientific abstract, NLM version 1 PDF page 1 and JATS article-meta abstract without abstract-type. This is not the separate IMPORTANCE summary. Introduction distinguishes preferential kin association from nonkin exclusion and supports the definition's two modes; the paper's own experiments support the nearby-species extension. The comparison concerns interactions with B. subtilis NCIB3610: nearby species can be antagonized, while more distant lineages show varied outcomes. This is not a universal monotonic relation between distance and antagonism. Relatedness uses type-strain 16S, not whole-genome identity of every isolate. Swarm, biofilm and halo assays differ in medium and endpoint. Figure 2A and 2C assign WNC032 to different species; Data Set S1 identifies it as B. megaterium. No silent panel correction or taxon anchor is inferred. Actual Figures 2 and 4 and selected spreadsheet rows/totals were inspected, not all figures or raw assays. Native abstract verifier: VERIFIED. Shares an investigator with 2015; not an independent-laboratory replication.

discussions.prompt: Preserve relational phenotype scope without equating all recognition or cooperation.
discussions.rationale: Stefanic 2015 defines conspecific discrimination, whereas Lyons 2017 explicitly extends exclusion to nearby species. The record retains that attributed extension without a universal kin threshold, obligate killing, cognition or monotonic distance-response rule. Kin recognition, allorecognition and self/nonself discrimination are not asserted as exact synonyms. An interaction phenotype is required; a recognition locus, allele match, isolated pairing or spatial assortment alone is insufficient. Recognition-allele specificity, measured relatedness proxies and genome-wide relatedness must not be conflated. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent. Mutualism (traitmech:000041) requires reciprocal benefit; biofilm formation (traitmech:000053) is neither necessary nor sufficient. Contact-dependent outer membrane exchange (traitmech:000650) is material transfer, and its existing negative kin-discrimination evidence remains a boundary, not a parent gap. Heterokaryon incompatibility (traitmech:000606) concerns postfusion restriction and is not automatically equivalent or reparented. Predation requires trophic benefit; DNA self/nonself defense has a different target and endpoint. No organism-level disjointness is implied.

discussions.prompt: Resolve strain, assay and source gaps before assigning canonical taxa or molecular mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: The QS45 strain-table gap and WNC032 figure-label conflict remain unresolved. The 2015 scientific abstract was read directly, but full text was not. The 2017 scientific abstract and IMPORTANCE summary were distinguished; the corrected excerpt is from the scientific abstract, not IMPORTANCE. Selected supplemental spreadsheet checks are not raw-image reanalysis or a statistical replication; supplementary EPS figures remain unread. Bounded MED, PLOS and NLM metadata checks are not exhaustive clearance of corrections or retractions; some publisher routes were inaccessible. No canonical taxa, exact external mappings, protein examples or causal graph are asserted. Allele-specific adhesion in engineered systems requires separate provenance and mechanism review, not inference of natural species-wide possession. Source URLs, hashes, access limits and native snippet outcomes are retained in the source-verification sidecar.

label: nutritional fungal mycoparasitism
definition: An ecological phenotype in which a fungus obtains nutrients at the expense of another fungus, either from the living host or after killing it.

evidence.snippet: The term mycoparasitism applies strictly to those relationships in which one living fungus acts as a nutrient source for another
evidence.notes: Jeffries 1995 review; scientific abstract directly retrieved from https://kar.kent.ac.uk/19621/. This strict sense contrasts with broader fungicolous usage in the same abstract. Selected main text and actual PDF pages 1 and 3 support detrimental nutrition with either a living host or killing before use. The record restricts actor and host to fungi, excluding historically grouped oomycetes. The review supplies terminology, not an independent experiment. Not every figure or table was inspected. Native abstract verifier: UNRESOLVED; the direct institutional excerpt was separately matched, not relabeled VERIFIED.

evidence.snippet: In dual-culture the mycelia of T. atroviride which remained in direct contact with labeled A. mellea showed an increased δ(13)C value
evidence.notes: Pellegrini et al. 2012, PMID:22302490; directly retrieved scientific abstract, Results, using DOI and SRC:MED together. Title, DOI and PMID agree. After 29 days in contact, the reported carbon isotope value was 66.4 per mille versus -26.6 per mille with unlabeled host. This supports host-derived carbon assimilation, not by itself host killing, a penetration mechanism or exclusion of all alternative transfer routes. The journal full text was not retrieved; the restricted institutional deposit was not bypassed. The bacterial comparator is not an example of this fungal-actor trait. Native abstract verifier: VERIFIED.

evidence.snippet: Only T. harzianum maintained mycoparasitic activity in the soil microcosm
evidence.notes: Pellegrini et al. 2013; scientific abstract directly read at https://iris.unipv.it/handle/11571/604013?mode=complete. Native verifier: VERIFIED via AGR:IND500606635, not PubMed. The author-deposited Corneo thesis chapter identifies this DOI; its version is not presumed identical to the unread journal full text. Its experiment selects three microorganisms: the positive soil result concerns a sterile microcosm at 20 C after 29 days, followed by three-day culture-out before isotope measurement, not direct field flux or all 158 isolates. Dual-culture enrichment accompanies growth inhibition; the host viability endpoint comes from a separate broth assay. Washing and host-specific PCR address contamination without excluding every route of carbon transfer. Leakage versus direct parasitism remains partly interpretive. Shares all six authors with 2012, not independent-laboratory replication.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the broader hierarchy without importing persistent association or broad fungicolous usage.
discussions.rationale: Nutrition at host expense is required; mere co-occurrence, fungicolous association, antagonism or utilization of already dead material does not establish it. Killing, penetration, obligacy and a single mechanism are not universal requirements. The unqualified mycoparasitism label is not an exact synonym. Local parasitism (traitmech:000043) inherits persistent physical association from symbiosis (traitmech:000040); that narrower local umbrella is not automatically applicable to destructive encounters included by Jeffries. METPO:1000059 phenotype is retained pending hierarchy review. Bacterial mycophagy (traitmech:000696) has a bacterial actor; microbial haustorium formation (traitmech:000663) is a structural phenotype, neither necessary nor sufficient for this nutrition. Saprotrophy (traitmech:000055) alone does not establish attack on a living host; no organism-level disjointness is implied. Pinned and current METPO broad lexical matches (0000261, 000262, 1000125, 1000197, 1000198, 1000227) are deprecated, with no replacement or consider annotation observed. Their OMO:0001000 reason does not disprove the biology or license identifier reuse. None is an exact active counterpart; historical IDs are not xrefs.

discussions.prompt: Resolve source discrepancies and isolate provenance before assigning canonical taxa or a causal mechanism.
discussions.rationale: The 2013 abstract reports inhibition of 80 +/- 0.19%; thesis Results gives 88 +/- 0.24% and Table 1 gives 80 +/- 0.29%. Fluorogenic-assay sampling days differ between Methods and Figure 2; soil-control isotope values differ between Results and Table 3. A no-difference statement is paired with P < 0.05, and abstract versus Results pathogen exclusions differ. These are unresolved, not silently harmonized. Selected thesis Methods, Results, Discussion and actual pages 69, 73, 75, 86 and 89 were inspected, not all figures, tables or raw data. Ground inoculum may include nonviable material; no killed-host control was inspected, which is not proof none exists. Table accessions identify BLAST reference strains, not experimental isolate deposits. No canonical taxa, exact external mappings, protein examples or causal graph are asserted. The measured enzyme activity is not a molecular effector identification. Metadata and notice checks were bounded; some publisher endpoints failed. Source URLs, hashes, version distinctions and native verification results are retained in the sidecar.

label: periplasmic bacterial predation
definition: A predatory bacterial phenotype in which a bacterium enters the periplasm of a bacterial prey cell and grows and reproduces there using nutrients obtained by killing and consuming the prey.

evidence.snippet: establishes itself in the prey periplasm, feeding on the prey’s cytoplasmic contents as a main nutrient source.
evidence.notes: Lai et al. 2025, PMID:41125861, PMC12546842, Introduction, second paragraph; the subject is B. bacteriovorus. Direct publisher HTML and Europe PMC full-text XML match. Scientific Abstract, Introduction, selected growth/exit Results and culture, sampling, time-lapse and statistics Methods, Discussion and actual Figures 1 and 4 read. Figure 1a is a lifecycle schematic, not direct imaging; Figure 4a includes WT exit measurements. Other figures and supplements not fully assessed. Publisher and MED showed no linked notice; MED linked the earlier preprint, not a correction. Published source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-025-09010-x.

evidence.snippet: Nutrients for the replication of Bdellovibrio bacteria come entirely from the digestion of the single invaded bacterium
evidence.notes: Fenton et al. 2010, PMID:20935099, scientific Abstract retrieved from source-qualified MED metadata. Supports prey-derived nutrition during intrabacterial replication; do not generalize its single-prey wording to a fixed predator occupancy or universal prey dependence. Full-text delivery failed; Methods, actual figures and supplement remain unread. MED links a commentary, not a correction/retraction; publisher notice check was inaccessible. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20935099/.

evidence.snippet: Although partial disruption of the cytoplasmic membrane was always apparent, the parasite did not appear to actively penetrate through this barrier.
evidence.notes: Burnham et al. 1968, PMID:4879563, scientific Abstract directly read at PubMed and matched source-qualified MED metadata. Electron microscopy supports entry without observed active penetration of the prey cytoplasmic membrane, not an intact membrane throughout predation or direct nutrient tracing. Full text and actual figures were unavailable; no strain-level example inferred. MED/PubMed exposed no linked notice, but publisher notice status was not verified. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4879563/.

canonical_examples.note: Qualified to wild-type HD100, not deletion, complemented or host-independent derivatives. Lai et al. used E. coli laboratory prey; this is not direct field observation. DSM 50701 is HD100 and is recorded as a soil isolate at https://webshop.dsmz.de/en/bacteria/Bdellovibrio-bacteriovorus.html; this establishes natural provenance, not another predation assay. NCBI strain identifier, scientific name and DSM 50701 synonym independently checked on 2026-10-11: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=264462.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish periplasmic feeding from invasion alone.
discussions.rationale: Predatory bacterium traitmech:000054 is broader; its intraperiplasmic_growth node denotes a lifecycle stage, not this whole feeding phenotype, and must not be equated to it. Epibiotic bacterial predation traitmech:000697 keeps the predator cell body external. Generic intracellular predation, endoparasitism and endosymbiosis are not exact synonyms of periplasmic predation. Attachment, killing without entry, or residence without nutritional growth are insufficient. Exact synonyms and xrefs remain unassigned pending authority and scope reconciliation. No organism-level disjointness, universal prey range, division pattern, progeny number or obligate dependence is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Ground model-specific machinery before adding causal edges.
discussions.rationale: A protein-resolved graph and protein examples are deferred, not claimed absent. The 2025 proteome and perturbation experiments provide leads, but protein abundance, gene presence and predicted sequence function do not establish the complete feeding mechanism. Heterologous prey lysis does not establish predator invasion or nutrient uptake. Verify exact accessions, taxon pairing and relevant supplements before curating machinery; do not transfer the HD100 mechanism to every periplasmic predator.
