evidence.notes: Panne et al. identify McrBC from Escherichia coli K-12 as a restriction enzyme that attacks modified-cytosine DNA.

evidence.snippet: McrB(L) binds specifically to the methylated recognition site and is, therefore, the DNA-binding moiety of the McrBC endonuclease.
evidence.notes: Panne et al. support methylated-site DNA binding by McrB(L), one of the products of the E. coli K-12 mcrB gene.

label: Metis system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Metis locus that senses phage-mediated host-genome degradation through N6-methyl-deoxyadenosine monophosphate and activates a type-specific toxic effector.

evidence.snippet: In this work, we describe Metis, a bacterial defense system that directly senses phage-mediated host genome degradation.
evidence.notes: Osterman et al. directly name Metis as a bacterial system sensing host-genome degradation during phage infection.

evidence.snippet: Metis aborts phage infection once it detects the modified mononucleotide N6-methyl-deoxyadenosine monophosphate (m6dAMP).
evidence.notes: Osterman et al. identify m6dAMP as the modified mononucleotide cue detected by Metis.

evidence.snippet: As methylation of deoxyadenosines usually occurs on the DNA polymer, accumulation of m6dAMP signals that the host genome has been degraded.
evidence.notes: Osterman et al. explain why free m6dAMP reports host-genome degradation.

evidence.snippet: In type I Metis, sensing of m6dAMP activates a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) diphosphatase, leading to NAD+ depletion and cessation of the infection process, whereas the effector in type II Metis is a membrane-spanning protein whose toxicity is triggered in response to the modified mononucleotide.
evidence.notes: Osterman et al. distinguish type I and type II Metis effectors without resolving a DefenseFinder rule-level model in the pinned registry.

evidence.snippet: We further show that Metis defense depends on endogenous DNA methylases and that phages can escape Metis through mutations that inactivate host genome degradation.
evidence.notes: Osterman et al. link Metis immunity to endogenous DNA methylases and to phage genome-degradation activity.

evidence.snippet: | Metis | 10\.1101/2025\.11\.05\.686725 | Bacteria sense virus-induced genome degradation via methylated mononucleotides |
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder article registry maps the named Metis system to the Osterman et al. preprint.

label: MMB gp29-gp30 system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an MMB gp29-gp30 locus that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.

evidence.snippet: at least five distinct prophage-expressed viral defense systems that interfere with infection
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. places the Cluster N MMB gp29-gp30 system in a cohort of prophage-expressed defenses against lytic and temperate mycobacteriophages.

evidence.snippet: Tweety (F1) is targeted by Xerxes, MMB, Phrann and Panchino
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. identifies Tweety as one phage targeted by the MichelleMyBell prophage defense profile.

evidence.snippet: Phages MMB, Xerxes, and Pipsqueaks are closely-related in the lysis-immunity region (Fig. 4a) and MMB and Xerxes have almost identical patterns of defense against eleven individual phages
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. connects the MichelleMyBell and Xerxes defense spectra to their shared lysis-immunity-region context.

evidence.snippet: we constructed a MMB mutant in which genes 29 and 30 are removed (deletions of individual genes appear to generate non-viable mutants; Supplementary Table 3) and showed that prophage-mediated defense is lost
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. deletes the MMB 29-30 interval when testing whether gp29 and gp30 contribute to MMB defense.

evidence.snippet: expressing MMB 29 and 30 confers the same pattern of defense as the MMB lysogen
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. shows that recombinant MMB genes 29 and 30 reproduce the MMB prophage-mediated defense pattern.

evidence.snippet: MMB 29-30 and Phrann 29-30 also confer survival to infection by a lytic Tweety derivative
evidence.notes: The PMC author manuscript for Dedrick et al. shows that the MMB gp29-gp30 system can protect bacteria from a lytic Tweety derivative in addition to wild-type Tweety.

label: Mok-Hok-Sok system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a hok/sok toxin-antitoxin locus represented by DefenseFinder as the two-profile Mok_Hok_Sok model and experimentally linked to bacteriophage T4 exclusion by the plasmid R1 hok/sok locus.

evidence.snippet: To investigate whether the hok/sok locus evolved as a phage-exclusion mechanism, Escherichia coli cells that contain hok/sok on a pBR322-based plasmid were challenged with T1, T4, T5, T7, and lambda phage.
evidence.notes: Pecota and Wood tested whether a plasmid-carried hok/sok locus can act as a phage-exclusion mechanism (PMID:8606182 / DOI:10.1128/jb.178.7.2044-2050.1996).

evidence.snippet: The presence of hok/sok reduced the efficiency of plating of T4 by 42% and decreased the plaque size by approximately 85%.
evidence.notes: Pecota and Wood show that hok/sok reduced bacteriophage T4 plating efficiency and plaque size.

evidence.snippet: Single-step growth experiments demonstrated that hok/sok decreased the T4 burst size by 40%, increased the time to form mature phage (eclipse time) from 22 to 30 min, and increased the time to cell lysis (latent period) from 30 to 60 min.
evidence.notes: Pecota and Wood support delayed T4 development and a lower T4 burst size in the presence of hok/sok.

label: MspJI system
definition: A type IV modification-dependent restriction system in which an organism possesses an MspJI-family Mrr-like locus encoding a restriction endonuclease that recognizes methylcytosine- or hydroxymethylcytosine-modified DNA and cleaves both strands at a fixed distance from the modified cytosine.

evidence.snippet: MspJI is a novel modification-dependent restriction endonuclease that cleaves at a fixed distance away from the modification site.
evidence.notes: Cohen-Karni et al. support MspJI as a modification-dependent restriction endonuclease with distance-defined cleavage relative to its modified target.

evidence.snippet: All of the enzymes specifically recognize cytosine C5 modification (methylation or hydroxymethylation) in DNA and cleave at a constant distance (N(12)/N(16)) away from the modified cytosine.
evidence.notes: Cohen-Karni et al. biochemically characterized MspJI homologs and support the MspJI family as C5-modified-cytosine-dependent restriction endonucleases.

evidence.snippet: Besides 5-methylcytosine, MspJI also recognizes 5-hydroxymethylcytosine but is blocked by 5-glucosylhydroxymethylcytosine.
evidence.notes: Zheng et al. support MspJI restriction of both methylcytosine- and hydroxymethylcytosine-containing DNA while leaving glucosylated hydroxymethylcytosine DNA uncleaved.

evidence.snippet: The new class of modification-dependent restriction enzymes was named Type IV, as distinct from the familiar modification-blocked Types I-III.
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh define the Type IV class as modification-dependent restriction enzymes.

label: Nhi system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an Nhi-family locus represented by the DefenseFinder Nhi__Nhi profile and exemplified by a single enzyme with nuclease and helicase activities that protects against diverse staphylococcal phages, prevents phage DNA accumulation, and is inferred to target and degrade phage-specific replication intermediates.

evidence.snippet: Here, we describe a unique mode of nucleic acid immunity mediated by a single enzyme with nuclease and helicase activities, herein referred to as Nhi (nuclease-helicase immunity)
evidence.notes: Bari et al. define Nhi as nuclease-helicase immunity mediated by one enzyme with nuclease and helicase activities.

evidence.snippet: This enzyme provides robust protection against diverse staphylococcal phages and prevents phage DNA accumulation in cells stripped of all other known defenses
evidence.notes: Bari et al. support Nhi as a system that protects against diverse staphylococcal phages and prevents phage DNA accumulation even without other known defenses.

evidence.snippet: Our observations support a model in which Nhi targets and degrades phage-specific replication intermediates

evidence.snippet: Nhi homologs are distributed in diverse bacteria and exhibit functional conservation
evidence.notes: Bari et al. support functional conservation of Nhi homologs across diverse bacteria.

label: NixI system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a NixI-family phage-satellite locus represented by the DefenseFinder NixI__NixI profile and exemplified by a PLE-encoded nicking endonuclease that cleaves ICP1 bacteriophage DNA, inhibits ICP1 genome replication, and reduces progeny production in Vibrio cholerae.

evidence.snippet: Here, we characterize a PLE-encoded nuclease, NixI, that blocks phage development likely by nicking ICP1’s genome as it transitions to RCR
evidence.notes: LeGault et al. characterize NixI as a PLE-encoded nuclease that likely blocks ICP1 development by nicking the ICP1 genome as it transitions to rolling-circle replication.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data show that PLE encodes a nicking endonuclease, NixI, that is necessary for cleavage of ICP1’s genome in vivo and that shows in vitro specificity for sequences found in ICP1’s genome
evidence.notes: LeGault et al. show that NixI is a PLE-encoded nicking endonuclease necessary for in vivo ICP1 cleavage and specific for ICP1-derived sequences in vitro.

evidence.snippet: NixI, however, is sufficient to limit ICP1 progeny production in a single round of infection
evidence.notes: LeGault et al. support NixI as a PLE-encoded product sufficient to limit ICP1 progeny production in a single infection round.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data demonstrate that nixI is a potent inhibitor of ICP1 replication, resulting in decreased virion production.
evidence.notes: LeGault et al. support NixI as a potent inhibitor of ICP1 genome replication, resulting in decreased virion production.

evidence.snippet: Phage parasites can be considered host defense systems, as the parasite inhibits production of its viral host, benefiting the bacterial population
evidence.notes: LeGault et al. explicitly frame PLE-like phage parasites as host defense systems because they inhibit production of their viral hosts.

label: NLR-like bNACHT system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an NLR-related bacterial NACHT locus represented by DefenseFinder as an NLR_like_bNACHT01 or NLR_like_bNACHT09 single-profile model, encoding a NACHT-module STAND-family protein that can restrict bacteriophage production.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that proteins containing a NACHT module, the central feature of the animal nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeat-containing gene family (NLRs), are found in bacteria and defend against phages.
evidence.notes: Kibby et al. support NACHT-module proteins as bacterial NLR-related proteins that defend against phages.

evidence.snippet: Genome context of bNACHT01, which is located near a CBASS system in Klebsiella pneumoniae MGH 35.
evidence.notes: Kibby et al. identified a NACHT-module gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae MGH 35 before naming it bNACHT01.

evidence.snippet: We named this gene bacterial NACHT module-containing protein 1 (bNACHT01), and it did not appear to be in an operon with any other genes.
evidence.notes: Kibby et al. named the selected NACHT-module gene bNACHT01.

evidence.snippet: bNACHT01 conferred over a 100-fold increase in protection against phage T4 and over a 1000-fold increase in protection against phages T5 and T6
evidence.notes: bNACHT01 protected against phages T4, T5, and T6 in the E. coli heterologous assay.

evidence.snippet: bacteria expressing bNACHT01 restricted phage virion production and continued growing
evidence.notes: Kibby et al. observed restricted phage virion production in bacteria expressing bNACHT01.

evidence.snippet: Mutation of R214 to alanine maintained expression of the protein but abrogated phage defense
evidence.notes: An R214A mutation preserved bNACHT01 expression but abrogated defense, supporting a NACHT-dependent output.

evidence.snippet: Diverse bacterial NACHT proteins from different clades exhibited robust antiphage activity across a wide range of phages
evidence.notes: Kibby et al. observed antiphage activity across diverse bacterial NACHT proteins.

label: Old exonuclease system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses an Old exonuclease locus represented by DefenseFinder as a single-profile model, Old_exonuclease__Old_exonuclease, and experimentally linked to interference with phage lambda by the bacteriophage P2 Old protein.

evidence.snippet: The Old protein of bacteriophage P2 is responsible for interference with the growth of phage lambda and for killing of recBC mutant Escherichia coli.
evidence.notes: The 1995 Old nuclease study identifies the P2 Old protein as responsible for phage-lambda interference.

evidence.snippet: The Old protein fused to maltose-binding protein has exonuclease activity on double-stranded DNA as well as nuclease activity on single-stranded DNA and RNA.
evidence.notes: The 1995 biochemical study shows Old has nuclease activity on double-stranded DNA, single-stranded DNA, and RNA.

evidence.snippet: It's been shown to protect against phage lambda :ref{doi=10.1128/jb.177.3.497-501.1995}, and when cloned with the P2 Tin accessory gene, it was shown to protect against other *E. coli* phages :ref{doi=10.1016/j.chom.2022.02.018}.
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page links Old_exonuclease to lambda protection and to broader P2 Old plus Tin protection.

evidence.snippet: The old_exonuclease is dsDNA exonuclease that digests in the 5' to 3' direction :ref{doi=10.1128/jb.177.3.497-501.1995}. To our knowledge, other aspects of the molecular mechanisms remain unknown.
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page supports Old dsDNA exonuclease activity while leaving the remaining molecular mechanism unresolved.

evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page describes Old_exonuclease as a one-protein system.

label: Ophion system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a three-gene Ophion locus encoding OpnA, OpnB, and OpnC components that can block jumbo-phage infection before phage-nucleus formation.

evidence.snippet: From over 500 candidate defense systems, we selected nine for experimental testing and validated three: Dionysus, a TerB-encoding system that disrupts early phage infection vesicle formation by Jumbo phages; Ophion, a Radical SAM-containing system that prevents the formation of the Jumbo phage nucleus; and Ambrosia, a tightly regulated RM-like system.
evidence.notes: Keesman et al. named Ophion among three modular phage-defense candidates validated experimentally from an initial pool of more than 500 candidates.

evidence.snippet: Ophion, named after a primordial serpent from Greek mythology, is a three gene system encoding a radical S-adenosyl-L-methionine (rSAM) enzyme (OpnA), a polymerase-and histidinol-phosphatase (PHP, OpnB), and a phosphoribosyl transferase (PRTase, OpnC)
evidence.notes: Keesman et al. support Ophion as a three-gene system encoding OpnA, OpnB, and OpnC components with Radical SAM, PHP, and phosphoribosyl-transferase domains.

evidence.snippet: Ophion shows strong protection against jumbo phages
evidence.notes: Keesman et al. support Ophion as a system that strongly protects against jumbo phages.

evidence.snippet: Mutating conserved residues of the rSAM and PRTase domains revealed these to be essential for protection, with partial dependence on the PHP domain
evidence.notes: Keesman et al. support the OpnA Radical SAM and OpnC phosphoribosyl-transferase domains as essential in the tested Ophion system, with partial dependence on OpnB PHP.

evidence.snippet: Ophion provides potent and specific defense against jumbo phages by blocking progression from the EPI vesicle to the nucleus stage, possibly by halting the transcription of the nucleus forming genes
evidence.notes: Keesman et al. connect Ophion-mediated defense to arrest of jumbo phages as they progress from the early phage infection vesicle stage to nucleus formation.

evidence.snippet: Ophion | 10\.1101/2025\.09\.30\.679545 | Discovery of phage defense systems through component modularity networks
evidence.notes: The DefenseFinder article registry maps the named Ophion system to the Keesman et al. modular phage-defense discovery preprint; the pinned DefenseFinder HMM inventory and rules table do not list Ophion, so this row is name-to-paper evidence rather than model-component evidence.

causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph captures Ophion as a named three-gene anti-jumbo-phage system while leaving its direct phage trigger, the OpnA/OpnB/OpnC interaction sequence, the nucleotide-modification product, the natural locus breadth, and the absence of pinned DefenseFinder HMM or rule rows unresolved.

label: pangenome openness
definition: A genomics trait describing the structure of a species' pangenome — the balance of core versus accessory genes and whether the pangenome is open (continually acquiring new genes across genomes) or closed.

evidence.notes: Tettelin et al. introduced the microbial pan-genome concept, distinguishing core and dispensable genes and open versus closed pangenomes.
McInerney, McNally & O'Connell review why prokaryotes have pangenomes and what drives their openness.

canonical_examples.note: Textbook open pan-genome: enormous accessory-genome diversity across strains relative to the core genome.

label: Panoptes system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a two-gene optSE locus encoding an OptS protein that constitutively produces cyclic dinucleotides and an OptE transmembrane effector that is released from cyclic-dinucleotide repression when phage Acb2-like proteins sequester those signals, leading to inner-membrane disruption.

evidence.snippet: Panoptes is a two-gene operon, optSE, wherein OptS is predicted to synthesize a nucleotide-derived second messenger and OptE is predicted to bind that signal and drive effector-mediated defence.
evidence.notes: Sullivan et al. define Panoptes as the two-gene optSE system encoding OptS and OptE.

evidence.snippet: We named OptSE the Panoptes antiphage system for Argus Panoptes, the all-seeing, many-eyed giant in Greek mythology who was a faithful watchman to Hera.

evidence.snippet: OptS orthologues from two distinct Panoptes systems generated cyclic dinucleotide products, including 2′,3′-cyclic diadenosine monophosphate (2′,3′-c-di-AMP), which we showed were able to bind the soluble domain of the OptE transmembrane effector.
evidence.notes: OptS orthologues produce cyclic dinucleotides, including 2′,3′-c-di-AMP, that can bind the soluble domain of the OptE transmembrane effector.

evidence.snippet: Panoptes potently restricted phage replication, but phages that had loss-of-function mutations in anti-cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signalling system (CBASS) protein 2 (Acb2) escaped defence.
evidence.notes: Phage replication was restricted by Panoptes, while Acb2 loss-of-function mutations escaped defense.

evidence.snippet: Our data support the idea that cyclic nucleotide sequestration by Acb2 releases OptE toxicity, thereby initiating inner membrane disruption, leading to phage defence.
evidence.notes: Acb2 cyclic-nucleotide sequestration releases OptE toxicity and leads to inner-membrane disruption.

evidence.snippet: We investigated a candidate two-gene Panoptes operon from Vibrio navarrensis.

label: PARIS system
definition: An abortive infection system in which an organism possesses a phage anti-restriction-induced system locus encoding an AriA ABC ATPase sensor and an AriB TOPRIM-family nuclease whose activation by phage anti-restriction or other foreign proteins releases AriB to inhibit translation through lysine tRNA cleavage and block bacteriophage propagation.

evidence.snippet: We validate the activity of diverse systems and describe PARIS, an abortive infection system triggered by a phage-encoded anti-restriction protein
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. support PARIS as a named abortive infection system activated by a phage anti-restriction protein.

evidence.snippet: phage anti-restriction-induced system (PARIS), an abortive infection system that triggers growth arrest upon sensing an anti-restriction protein
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. support the PARIS long-form name and the growth-arrest output of the system.

evidence.snippet: operates as a toxin-antitoxin system, in which the antitoxin AriA sequesters and inactivates the toxin AriB until triggered by the T7 phage counterdefence protein Ocr
evidence.notes: Deep et al. support defining the Ocr-triggered PARIS mechanism around the AriA antitoxin and AriB toxin.

evidence.snippet: AriB is a toprim/OLD-family nuclease, the activation of which arrests cell growth and inhibits phage propagation by globally inhibiting protein translation through specific cleavage of a lysine tRNA
evidence.notes: Deep et al. support the AriB nuclease, lysine-tRNA cleavage, translational-inhibition, growth-arrest, and phage-propagation outputs.

evidence.snippet: The phage antirestriction induced system (PARIS) is a defence system, often encoded in viral genomes, that is composed of a 55 kDa ABC ATPase (AriA) and a 35 kDa TOPRIM nuclease (AriB)
evidence.notes: Burman et al. independently support the AriA ABC ATPase and AriB TOPRIM nuclease components.

evidence.snippet: ATP-dependent detection of foreign proteins triggers the release of AriB, which assembles into a homodimeric nuclease that blocks infection by cleaving host lysine transfer RNA
evidence.notes: Burman et al. support an activation model in which foreign-protein detection releases AriB to cleave host lysine tRNA.

evidence.snippet: Phage T5 subverts PARIS immunity through expression of a lysine transfer RNA variant that is not cleaved by PARIS, thereby restoring viral infection
evidence.notes: Burman et al. support recording T5 lysine tRNA anti-defense as a reviewed counter-defense gap before minting narrower PARIS subtype children.

evidence.snippet: While the system from E. coli B185 provided robust defense when expressed from its natural promoter
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. support E. coli as a canonical organism by cloning the E. coli B185 PARIS system with its native promoter and observing robust antiphage defense.

canonical_examples.note: Rousset et al. cloned the native-promoter PARIS locus from E. coli B185 and showed that it provided robust defense.

causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph stays at the PARIS-family level and uses characterized E. coli B185 AriA/AriB examples without asserting one universal phage trigger, Ocr response, Ptr1/Ptr2 response, T5 lysine tRNA suppressor, exact AriA/AriB stoichiometry, or anti-anti-restriction context across all PARIS loci.

discussions.rationale: Rousset et al. discovered PARIS as an abortive infection system triggered by T7 Ocr; Deep et al. resolved Ocr-dependent AriA release of AriB for the E. coli B185 system; and Burman et al. showed that T5 Ptr1 and Ptr2 can activate PARIS while a phage T5 lysine tRNA variant can evade AriB cleavage. label: PD-T2-1 system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a two-gene PD-T2-1 operon whose expression was experimentally linked to protection against T2, T6, Bas18, T4, and T5 phages.

evidence.snippet: Two phage proteins were further investigated, revealing T7 gp17 and additional tail fiber proteins activated the undescribed antiphage system PD-T2–1 and identifying λ gpE major capsid protein activated the antiphage system Avs8.
evidence.notes: Goedecke et al. report that T7 gp17 and additional tail fiber proteins activated the previously undescribed PD-T2-1 antiphage system.

evidence.snippet: Sequencing the transposon insertion site of mutants that did grow revealed 28 out of 48 mutants contained transposons that disrupted a two-gene operon of unknown function
evidence.notes: ECOR03 transposon mutants that escaped T7 gp17-mediated growth inhibition were enriched for insertions disrupting the same unknown two-gene operon.

evidence.snippet: Operon structure of phage defense against T2 system 1 (PD-T2–1). Transposon insertions identified in mutant ECOR03 expressing T7 gp17 are indicated with triangles. A predicted transmembrane domain (TM) for PD-T2–1A, accession numbers, and the length of each protein in amino acids (aa) are shown.
evidence.notes: The PD-T2-1 operon figure identifies transposon insertions, the predicted transmembrane domain in PD-T2-1A, and the protein accessions used in the study.

evidence.snippet: GeneAB conferred >100-fold protection against phages T2, T6, and Bas18, and approximately 10-fold protection against phages T4 and T5
evidence.notes: Expression of the operon in MG1655 protected against T2, T6, Bas18, T4, and T5 in phage-challenge assays.

evidence.snippet: These findings led us to rename the geneAB operon phage defense against T2 system 1 (PD-T2–1)
evidence.notes: Goedecke et al. renamed the placeholder geneAB operon phage defense against T2 system 1.

evidence.snippet: Transformation efficiency assays revealed that PD-T2–1 also selectively inhibited bacterial growth when T2 gp37, T2 gp34, and T2 gp12 were co-expressed
evidence.notes: PD-T2-1 also selectively inhibited growth when the T2 tail-fiber genes gp37, gp34, and gp12 were expressed.

evidence.snippet: These results indicate PD-T2–1 does not function as a canonical toxin-antitoxin system.
evidence.notes: Single-gene expression experiments argue against PD-T2-1 as a canonical toxin-antitoxin system.
The Methods section reports the ECOR03 PD-T2-1A RefSeq and nonredundant protein accessions used in the article.

label: PD-T4-10 system
definition: An abortive infection system in which an organism possesses a PD-T4-10 locus represented by DefenseFinder as a two-profile model, PD-T4-10__PD-T4-10_A and PD-T4-10__PD-T4-10_B, and experimentally linked to T2, T4, T6, T5, and SECphi27 protection when expressed in E. coli.

evidence.snippet: Here we developed an experimental selection scheme agnostic to genomic context to identify defence systems in 71 diverse E. coli strains. Our results unveil 21 conserved defence systems, none of which were previously detected as enriched in defence islands.
evidence.notes: Vassallo et al. developed the agnostic E. coli pangenome selection that uncovered PD-T4-10 and related conserved phage-defense systems.

evidence.snippet: The PD-T4-10 system is composed of 2 proteins: PD-T4-10_B and, PD-T4-10_A. These ORFs are overlapping and PD-T4-10_B is toxic while PD-T4-10_A neutralizes its toxicity, hinting at a toxin-antitoxin (TA) mechanism. It confers resitance to T2, T4, T6 and SECphi27 through an Abi defense mechanism :ref{doi=10.1038/s41564-022-01219-4}.
evidence.notes: The DefenseFinder wiki describes PD-T4-10 as a two-protein Abi system whose overlapping ORFs include a toxic PD-T4-10_B and neutralizing PD-T4-10_A.

label: PfiAT system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Pf4 prophage-encoded PfiAT toxin-antitoxin locus represented by DefenseFinder as a two-profile model requiring PfiAT__PfiA and PfiAT__PfiT.

evidence.snippet: we provided experimental evidence to demonstrate that PA0729 and the upstream ORF Rorf0727 near the right attachment site of Pf4 form a type II toxin/antitoxin (TA) pair.
evidence.notes: Li et al. experimentally identify PA0729 and Rorf0727 in the Pf4 prophage as a PfiT/PfiA type II toxin-antitoxin pair (PMID:32246813 / DOI:10.1111/1751-7915.13570).

evidence.snippet: Importantly, we found that the deletion of the toxin gene PA0729 greatly increased Pf4 phage production.
evidence.notes: Li et al. show that deleting pfiT increases Pf4 phage production.

evidence.snippet: We thus suggest the toxin PA0729 be named PfiT for Pf4 inhibition toxin and Rorf0727 be named PfiA for PfiT antitoxin.
evidence.notes: Li et al. name PA0729 as PfiT and Rorf0727 as PfiA.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, this study reveals that the TA systems in Pf prophages can regulate phage production and phage immunity, providing new insights into the function of TAs in mobile genetic elements.
evidence.notes: Li et al. frame Pf prophage toxin-antitoxin systems as regulators of phage production and phage immunity.

evidence.snippet: Importantly, we found that the deletion of the toxin gene PA0729 greatly increased Pf4 phage production.
evidence.notes: Li et al. show that pfiT inhibits Pf4 phage production.

label: phage defense system
definition: A genomics trait describing possession of one or more bacterial or archaeal immune systems that inhibit bacteriophage infection.

evidence.snippet: Viruses and their hosts are engaged in a constant arms race leading to the evolution of antiviral defence mechanisms
evidence.notes: Bernheim and Sorek define the bacterial bacteriophage-defense context and review the pan-genomic diversity and cost of antiviral defense systems.

evidence.snippet: individual microorganisms often encode multiple distinct defence systems
evidence.notes: The pan-immune-system model supports treating possession of one or more defense systems as a strain-level genomics trait rather than a single protein, locus, or pathway.

evidence.snippet: Bacteria have evolved numerous immune mechanisms, both innate and adaptive
evidence.notes: Hampton et al. review innate and adaptive anti-phage systems and the phage counter-defense mechanisms that evade them.

evidence.snippet: Here we review the spectrum of anti-phage systems and highlight their evasion by bacteriophages
evidence.notes: This supports the umbrella scope spanning diverse CRISPR-Cas, restriction-modification, BREX, DISARM, abortive-infection, and related anti-phage defenses.

evidence.snippet: Candidate immune systems were then experimentally validated for their activities
evidence.notes: The Science article summary for Doron et al. supports genomic discovery and experimental validation of antiphage defense systems from microbial pangenomes.

canonical_examples.note: S. thermophilus is the organism in which CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity was experimentally shown to provide phage resistance.

causal_graphs.title: Antiphage defense systems resist viral challenge
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed ontology sketch linking phage pressure to the umbrella phage-defense-system trait and its reviewed CRISPR-Cas and restriction-modification children.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This parent trait groups independently reviewed genome-level anti-phage defense systems without claiming that CRISPR-Cas, restriction-modification, BREX, DISARM, abortive infection, or other defense families share one universal molecular mechanism.

label: phosphorothioate defense system
definition: A genomics trait describing possession of a DNA phosphorothioation-dependent antiviral locus in which host DNA phosphorothioate modification is paired with a Dnd-, Ssp-, or Pbe-family effector module to restrict invading viral DNA.

evidence.snippet: We previously identified the Dnd system, which uses DndABCDE to insert sulfur into the DNA backbone as a double-stranded phosphorothioate (PT) modification, and DndFGH, a restriction component
evidence.notes: Xiong et al. summarize the Dnd modification and restriction modules as a DNA phosphorothioation defense system.

evidence.snippet: SspABCD coupled with SspE provides protection against phages
evidence.notes: Xiong et al. support SspABCD-SspE as a bacterial phosphorothioation-sensing antiphage defense system.

evidence.snippet: Usually, this modification gene cluster is paired with a restriction module consisting of DndF, DndG, and DndH
evidence.notes: Jiang et al. support the paired modification-plus-restriction architecture of Dnd-related phosphorothioate R-M systems.

evidence.snippet: the host could benefit from the protection provided by Dnd-related R-M systems against infection by various lytic phages as well as temperate phages
evidence.notes: Jiang et al. experimentally demonstrated broad antiphage protection by Dnd-related phosphorothioate R-M systems.

evidence.snippet: DndCDEA-specific DNA phosphorothioate (PT) modification and the PbeABCD-mediated halt of virus propagation
evidence.notes: Xiong et al. support DndCDEA-PbeABCD as an archaeal phosphorothioation-dependent antiviral branch distinct from bacterial DndFGH and Ssp systems.

canonical_examples.note: Jiang et al. cloned the native E. coli B7A dndBCDE-FGH module into E. coli DH10B and measured strong DndB7A R-M protection against multiple lytic phages.

causal_graphs.title: Phosphorothioate restriction modules target invading viral DNA
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed process sketch linking host DNA phosphorothioate modification to PT-dependent self/non-self discrimination, restriction of invading viral DNA, and impaired viral DNA replication.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph captures system-level logic shared by phosphorothioate-based Dnd, Ssp, and Pbe antiviral systems without claiming that DndFGH, SspE, SspFGH, and PbeABCD sense PT marks, damage foreign DNA, or inhibit viral replication by one exact protein mechanism.

label: Phrann gp29-gp30 system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Phrann gp29-gp30 locus that can protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection.

evidence.snippet: at least five distinct prophage-expressed viral defense systems that interfere with infection
evidence.notes: Dedrick et al. place the Cluster N Phrann gp29-gp30 system in a cohort of prophage-expressed defenses against lytic and temperate mycobacteriophages.

evidence.snippet: Phrann genes 29 and/or 30 are involved in defense against Tweety and Gaia, as a mutant lysogen lacking Phrann 29 loses defense against these phages
evidence.notes: Dedrick et al. localize part of the Phrann prophage-mediated heterotypic defense phenotype to genes 29 and 30.

evidence.snippet: expressing Phrann genes 29 and 30 reproduce the Phrann defense against Tweety and Gaia
evidence.notes: Dedrick et al. show that recombinant Phrann genes 29 and 30 are sufficient to reproduce Phrann defense against Tweety and Gaia.

evidence.snippet: Phrann prophage-mediated defense is strictly heterotypic, and Phrann gp29/gp30 does not defend against Phrann or other Cluster N phages
evidence.notes: Dedrick et al. delimit the Phrann gp29-gp30 defense profile as heterotypic rather than Cluster N superinfection exclusion.

evidence.snippet: Prophage-mediated defense by (p)ppGpp synthetases is a new and intriguing system for defense against viral attack
evidence.notes: Dedrick et al. interpret Phrann gp29 as a putative (p)ppGpp synthetase in a prophage-mediated viral-defense system.

label: Pif system
definition: An abortive infection system in which an organism possesses an F-plasmid pif-family locus represented by the DefenseFinder Pif__PifA and Pif__PifC profiles and exemplified by the pif region that specifies abortive infection of T7 phage.

evidence.snippet: Molecular analysis of F plasmid pif region specifying abortive infection of T7 phage.
evidence.notes: Cram et al. title the paper around F-plasmid pif-region specification of the T7 abortive-infection phenotype.

evidence.snippet: We report the molecular cloning of the pif region of the F plasmid and its physical dissection by subcloning and deletion analysis.
evidence.notes: Cram et al. cloned and deletion-mapped the F-plasmid pif region.

evidence.snippet: Examination of the polypeptide products synthesized in maxicells by plasmids carrying defined pif sequences has shown that the region specifies at least two proteins of molecular weights 80,000 and 40,000, the genes for which appear to lie in the same transcriptional unit.
evidence.notes: Cram et al. support a multigene pif region without resolving a direct PifA or PifC molecular function.

The previous predicates are transitively rdfs:subPropertyOf METPO:2000001, whose rdfs:domain is METPO:1000525 (microbe), so a causal-graph subject entailed that the subject IS a microbe; CausalNodeTypeEnum has no organism member, so no such edge could ever satisfy the domain. Relabelled 1 causal edge from `reduces` to `decreases` and re-grounded it from METPO:2007802 to RO:0002212 (negatively regulates), issue 330. The corpus wrote two senses under the single label `reduces` - genuine electron donation, and a lessens/decreases sense - and METPO:2007802 is defined as donating electrons to the object and lowering its oxidation state, which this edge does not assert. The two senses could not be separated mechanically because the label was identical, so they migrated together in issue 329 and were split here by reading each edge. RO:0002212 declares no rdfs:domain or rdfs:range, so this introduces no entailment of the kind issue 301 removed.

Separated the protein sense from the activity sense so one node_id means one thing (issue 356): retyped plasmid_methylase: MOLECULAR_FUNCTION -> GENE_OR_PROTEIN. The exception in this tranche. Both occurrences describe the ENZYME -- 'Methyltransferase encoded by a mobile element that pre-methylates its DNA' (GENE_OR_PROTEIN) and 'Plasmid-borne methyltransferase shielding plasmid DNA from restriction' (MOLECULAR_FUNCTION). Neither names an activity, so there is one concept here and it is a protein. A rename would have invented a distinction the corpus does not draw.

label: PrrC system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a PrrC locus represented by DefenseFinder as a two-profile model requiring PrrC__EcoprrI and PrrC__PrrC, with type I restriction-modification components accepted as accessory markers.

evidence.snippet: phage exclusion systems that involve T4-mediated activation of a latent endoribonuclease (PrrC) and cofactor-assisted activation of EF-Tu proteolysis (Gol-Lit)
evidence.notes: Uzan et al. name PrrC as a T4-mediated phage-exclusion system that activates a latent endoribonuclease (PMID:21129205 / DOI:10.1186/1743-422X-7-360).

evidence.snippet: The tRNA(Lys) anticodon nuclease PrrC is associated in latent form with the type Ic DNA restriction endonuclease EcoprrI and activated by a phage T4-encoded inhibitor of EcoprrI.
evidence.notes: Blanga-Kanfi et al. support latent PrrC association with the EcoprrI restriction endonuclease and activation by a T4-encoded EcoprrI inhibitor.

evidence.snippet: This triad exists in all the known PrrC homologs but only some of them feature residues needed for tRNA(Lys) recognition by the Escherichia coli prototype.
evidence.notes: Blanga-Kanfi et al. support a family of PrrC homologs whose substrate-recognition residues can differ from the Escherichia coli prototype.

evidence.snippet: The differential conservation and consistent genetic linkage of the PrrC proteins with EcoprrI homologs portray them as a family of restriction RNases of diverse substrate specificities that are mobilized when an associated DNA restriction nuclease is compromised.
evidence.notes: Blanga-Kanfi et al. support genetic linkage between PrrC proteins and EcoprrI homologs as a restriction-RNase family mobilized when an associated restriction nuclease is compromised.

label: PvuRts1I system
definition: A type IV modification-dependent restriction system in which an organism possesses a PvuRts1I-family locus encoding a restriction endonuclease that recognizes 5-hydroxymethylcytosine or 5-glucosylhydroxymethylcytosine in double-stranded DNA and cleaves both strands on the 3'-side away from the recognized modified cytosine.

evidence.snippet: Using PvuRts1I as the founding member, we define a family of homologous proteins with similar DNA modification-dependent recognition properties.
evidence.notes: Wang et al. support PvuRts1I as the founding member of a family of modification-dependent restriction enzymes.

evidence.snippet: PvuRts1I is a modification-dependent restriction endonuclease that recognizes 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) as well as 5-glucosylhydroxymethylcytosine (5ghmC) in double-stranded DNA.
evidence.notes: Wang et al. support PvuRts1I recognition of 5hmC- and 5ghmC-containing double-stranded DNA.

evidence.snippet: We show that these enzymes introduce a double-stranded cleavage at the 3'-side away from the recognized modified cytosine.
evidence.notes: Wang et al. support PvuRts1I-family enzymes as modification-dependent restriction endonucleases that cleave both DNA strands at a defined offset from the modified cytosine.

evidence.snippet: The new class of modification-dependent restriction enzymes was named Type IV, as distinct from the familiar modification-blocked Types I-III.
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh define the Type IV class as modification-dependent restriction enzymes.

evidence.snippet: | PvuRts1I | 10\.1093/nar/gkr607 | Comparative characterization of the PvuRts1I family of restriction enzymes and their application in mapping genomic 5-hydroxymethylcytosine |
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder article registry maps the PvuRts1I source key to the Wang et al. PvuRts1I-family paper.

label: Pycsar system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Pycsar locus encoding a PycC pyrimidine cyclase and a cognate cyclic-pyrimidine receptor effector whose phage-induced cyclic CMP or cyclic UMP signaling activates antiviral effector outputs that inhibit bacteriophage propagation.

synonyms.synonym_text: Pyrimidine Cyclase System for Antiphage Resistance
pyrimidine cyclase system for anti-phage resistance

evidence.snippet: We discovered a family of bacterial pyrimidine cyclase enzymes that specifically synthesize cCMP and cUMP following phage infection
evidence.notes: Tal et al. support Pycsar-associated pyrimidine cyclases as phage-induced producers of cyclic CMP and cyclic UMP.

evidence.snippet: The cCMP and cUMP molecules then activate effector proteins
evidence.notes: Tal et al. connect cyclic pyrimidine second messengers to activation of Pycsar effector proteins.

evidence.snippet: The predicted cyclase genes are usually found in an operon together with an additional gene, and we therefore cloned such two-gene operons, one from Escherichia coli 303145 and the other from E. coli E831, into the laboratory E. coli strain MG1655. Challenging the transformed bacteria with a panel of 12 phages showed that both operons provided substantial defense against multiple phages
evidence.notes: Tal et al. support a canonical Escherichia coli example by showing that two E. coli Pycsar loci conferred antiphage defense after cloning into E. coli MG1655.

evidence.snippet: Mutation in the predicted active site of the cyclase domain abolished defense
evidence.notes: Tal et al. support the functional importance of the PycC cyclase domain for the antiphage phenotype.

evidence.snippet: This system consists of a pyrimidine cyclase and a cyclic pyrimidine receptor protein
evidence.notes: Hou et al. support defining Pycsar systems around a pyrimidine cyclase plus a cognate cyclic-pyrimidine receptor rather than a bare pycC gene.

evidence.snippet: a distinct zinc-finger motif of the uridylate cyclase is identified to confer substantial resistance against phage infections
evidence.notes: Hou et al. support the uridylate-cyclase branch while the broad TraitRecord leaves cCMP-producing and cUMP-producing Pycsar clades unresolved as children.

evidence.snippet: structural characterization of cUMP receptor protein PycTIR provides clear picture of specific cUMP recognition and identifies a conserved N-terminal extension that mediates PycTIR oligomerization and activation
evidence.notes: Hou et al. support cyclic UMP recognition by the PycTIR cyclic-pyrimidine receptor as one resolved Pycsar effector-activation mechanism.

canonical_examples.note: Tal et al. cloned native Pycsar two-gene operons from E. coli 303145 and E. coli E831 into E. coli MG1655 and showed that both operons provided substantial defense against multiple phages.

causal_graphs.title: Pycsar loci couple cyclic-pyrimidine signaling to phage defense
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed process sketch linking a complete Pycsar locus to phage-induced PycC pyrimidine cyclase activity, cyclic CMP or cyclic UMP signaling, cyclic-pyrimidine receptor activation, antiviral effector output, and inhibition of phage propagation.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph stays at the Pycsar-family level and uses characterized cytidylate-cyclase and uridylate-cyclase examples without asserting one universal cyclase clade, cCMP-versus-cUMP product, PycTIR-versus-PycTM effector fold, AGS-C role, zinc-finger role, activating phage trigger, membrane impairment, or NAD-depletion output across all Pycsar antiphage loci.

label: RADAR system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a restriction by an adenosine deaminase acting on RNA locus encoding an RdrA AAA+ ATPase and an RdrB adenosine deaminase that assemble into a supramolecular defense complex to modify adenosine-containing substrates and inhibit bacteriophage replication.

synonyms.synonym_text: restriction by an adenosine deaminase acting on RNA

evidence.snippet: RADAR is a two-protein bacterial defense system that was reported to defend against phage
evidence.notes: Duncan-Lowey et al. support RADAR as a named bacterial phage-defense system.

evidence.snippet: revealing RdrA as a heptameric, two-layered AAA+ ATPase and RdrB as a dodecameric, hollow complex with twelve surface-exposed deaminase active sites
evidence.notes: Duncan-Lowey et al. support the RdrA AAA+ ATPase and RdrB adenosine-deaminase complex components.

evidence.snippet: RdrB catalyzes ATP-to-ITP conversion in vitro and induces the massive accumulation of inosine mononucleotides during phage infection in vivo, limiting phage replication
evidence.notes: Duncan-Lowey et al. support ATP-to-ITP deamination and inosine-mononucleotide accumulation as RADAR antiphage outputs.

evidence.snippet: When heterologously expressed in E. coli MG1655, all RADAR systems conferred defense against the closely related T-even phages T2, T4, and T6
evidence.notes: Duncan-Lowey et al. support the E. coli P0304799.3 RADAR locus as experimentally investigated and antiphage-active when cloned into E. coli MG1655.

evidence.snippet: RADAR contains an adenosine triphosphatase (RdrA) and an adenosine deaminase (RdrB)
evidence.notes: Gao et al. independently support defining RADAR around the RdrA ATPase and RdrB deaminase components.

evidence.snippet: up to twelve RdrA rings can dock one RdrB cage with precise alignments between deaminase catalytic pockets and RNA-translocation channels
evidence.notes: Gao et al. independently resolve RADAR RdrA/RdrB supramolecular assemblies while supporting an RNA-translocation interpretation of the deaminase substrate.

canonical_examples.note: Duncan-Lowey et al. selected the RADAR system from E. coli P0304799.3 for experimental investigation and reported that it conferred defense against T-even phages when heterologously expressed in E. coli MG1655.

causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph stays at the RADAR-family level and uses the mononucleotide-deamination mechanism from Duncan-Lowey et al. without asserting that the exact RdrA activation trigger, ATP-versus-RNA substrate, inosine toxicity route, or abortive-infection output is resolved across all RADAR loci.

label: Retron system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a retron locus encoding a reverse transcriptase, an msr/msd non-coding RNA that yields multicopy single-stranded DNA, and an associated effector whose activation can inhibit bacteriophage propagation through abortive infection.

evidence.snippet: We report that retrons function as anti-phage defense systems
evidence.notes: Millman et al. support retrons as experimentally observed antiphage defense systems rather than only retroelement sequence features.

evidence.snippet: The defensive unit is composed of three components: the RT, the ncRNA, and an effector protein
evidence.notes: Millman et al. support defining the broad record around a reverse transcriptase, non-coding RNA, and associated effector rather than a bare reverse-transcriptase gene.

evidence.snippet: We examined multiple retron systems and show that they confer defense against a broad range of phages via abortive infection
evidence.notes: Millman et al. support treating Retron system as a family of organism-level antiphage traits, with abortive infection as a shared defense output.

evidence.snippet: retrons, functioning together with their associated effector genes, form anti-phage defense systems
evidence.notes: Millman et al. connect associated effector genes to Retron antiphage function.

evidence.snippet: RcaT is neutralized by the reverse transcriptase–msDNA antitoxin complex, and becomes active upon perturbation of msDNA biosynthesis
evidence.notes: Bobonis et al. support an RcaT-containing Retron-Sen2 example in which the reverse-transcriptase-msDNA complex controls effector activity.

evidence.snippet: we identified multiple trigger and blocker proteins of phage origin
evidence.notes: Bobonis et al. support phage-encoded trigger and blocker logic for the characterized Retron-Sen2 RcaT system.

evidence.snippet: phage-related triggers directly modify the msDNA, thereby activating RcaT and inhibiting bacterial growth
evidence.notes: Bobonis et al. connect phage-triggered msDNA modification to RcaT activation in Retron-Sen2 without making that trigger universal across all retrons.

evidence.snippet: retron toxin–antitoxin systems act as abortive infection anti-phage defence systems
evidence.notes: Bobonis et al. support retron toxin-antitoxin systems as abortive-infection antiphage systems.

canonical_examples.note: Millman et al. cloned E. coli Ec48 and Ec73 retrons with their predicted effector genes into E. coli MG1655 and showed that both engineered E. coli systems had broad antiphage activity that depended on reverse-transcriptase catalytic-site residues.

causal_graphs.title: Retrons couple msDNA complexes to effector activation
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed process sketch linking a complete retron locus to RT/ncRNA-dependent msDNA biosynthesis, control of associated effectors, abortive-infection outputs, and inhibition of phage growth.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph stays at the retron family level and uses the Ec48 RecBCD-guarding and Retron-Sen2 RcaT mechanisms as characterized examples without asserting one universal effector fold, phage trigger, direct msDNA-modification event, guarded host target, or Retron-Septu release architecture across all retron antiphage loci.

label: RloC system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a genome-encoded RloC locus represented by DefenseFinder as a one-profile model requiring RloC__RloC.

evidence.snippet: The conserved bacterial protein RloC, a distant homologue of the tRNA(Lys) anticodon nuclease (ACNase) PrrC, is shown here to act as a wobble nucleotide-excising and Zn(++)-responsive tRNase.
evidence.notes: Davidov and Kaufmann identify RloC as a conserved bacterial wobble nucleotide-excising, zinc-responsive tRNase related to PrrC (PMID:18681940 / DOI:10.1111/j.1365-2958.2008.06387.x).

evidence.snippet: Geobacillus kaustophilus RloC expressed in Escherichia coli exhibited ACNase activity that differed from PrrC's in substrate preference and ability to excise the wobble nucleotide.
evidence.notes: Davidov and Kaufmann support wobble nucleotide excision by Geobacillus kaustophilus RloC expressed in Escherichia coli.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, RloC is rarely linked to an RM protein, and its ACNase is regulated by an internal switch responsive to double-stranded DNA breaks.
evidence.notes: Bitton et al. describe RloC ACNase regulation by an internal switch that responds to double-stranded DNA breaks.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with these predictions we show that Acinetobacter baylyi RloC expressed in Escherichia coli is activated by wild-type phage T4 but not by a mutant impaired in host DNA degradation.
evidence.notes: Bitton et al. show that Acinetobacter baylyi RloC expressed in Escherichia coli is activated by wild-type phage T4, but not by a host-DNA-degradation mutant.

evidence.snippet: Nonetheless, T4's plating efficiency was inefficiently impaired by AbaRloC, presumably due to a decoy function of the phage encoded tRNA target, the absence of which exacerbated the restriction.
evidence.notes: Bitton et al. report that Acinetobacter baylyi RloC inefficiently impairs wild-type T4 plating and more strongly restricts a phage mutant lacking the decoy tRNA target.

label: RnlAB system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a genome-encoded RnlAB toxin-antitoxin locus represented by DefenseFinder as a two-profile model requiring RnlAB__RnlA and RnlAB__RnlB.

evidence.snippet: RNase LS was originally identified as a potential antagonist of bacteriophage T4 infection. When T4 dmd is defective, RNase LS activity rapidly increases after T4 infection and cleaves T4 mRNAs to antagonize T4 reproduction.
evidence.notes: Koga et al. frame RnlA-dependent RNase LS activity as a potential antagonist of bacteriophage T4 dmd mutants (PMID:20980243 / DOI:10.1534/genetics.110.121798).

evidence.snippet: Here we show that rnlA, a structural gene of RNase LS, encodes a novel toxin, and that rnlB (formally yfjO), located immediately downstream of rnlA, encodes an antitoxin against RnlA.
evidence.notes: Koga et al. identify rnlA as the RNase LS toxin gene and rnlB as the neighboring cognate antitoxin gene.

evidence.snippet: Pull-down analysis showed a specific interaction between RnlA and RnlB.
evidence.notes: Koga et al. support direct RnlA/RnlB interaction by pull-down analysis.

evidence.snippet: All of these results suggested that rnlA-rnlB define a new toxin-antitoxin (TA) system.
evidence.notes: Koga et al. define rnlA-rnlB as a new toxin-antitoxin system.

evidence.snippet: Predicted proteins encoded by these two ORFs were found to share a weak homology with RnlA and RnlB, respectively, a toxin–antitoxin system encoded on the E. coli K-12 chromosome.
evidence.notes: Otsuka and Yonesaki describe RnlA/RnlB as a toxin-antitoxin system encoded on the Escherichia coli K-12 chromosome.

evidence.snippet: T4 phage Dmd suppressed the toxicities of both RnlA and LsoA by direct interaction, the first example of a phage with an antitoxin against multiple toxins.
evidence.notes: Otsuka and Yonesaki support T4 Dmd as a phage antitoxin that suppresses RnlA toxicity by direct interaction.

Tranche 5 of issue 356 settles the process/quality families and merges ids that meant the same sense: maximal_growth_rate is QUALITY. A maximal growth rate is a measured upper bound or peak specific rate. Its edges associate, enable, or manifest that value; none describe the process of cell growth itself. An edge cannot enable a QUALITY under RO:0002327's biological-process range, so edges that causally support the rate use promotes (RO:0002213) instead.

label: Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a three-protein Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR locus represented by DefenseFinder as a three-profile model requiring Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR__Rst_1TM_TIR, Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR__Rst_2TM_TIR, and Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR__Rst_TIR_tm and experimentally linked to multi-phage protection when expressed in Escherichia coli C.

evidence.snippet: Phage resistance heatmaps of the validated defense systems show the median fold resistance of three independent replicates against a panel of eight phages
evidence.notes: The Figure 5 legend frames the cloned Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR hit as one of the validated defense systems in a replicated phage-resistance heatmap.

evidence.snippet: The Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR system is carried by the P2-like phage AC1 and protects *Escherichia coli* C against lambda, LF82_P8 and P2 phages. This system is composed of three proteins, Rst_TIR_tm, which contains a TIR (Toll/interleukin-1 receptor) domain, Rst_1TM_TIR, which contains a transmembrane helix (TM) and Rst_2TM_TIR, that contains two TMs :ref{doi=10.1016/j.chom.2022.02.018}.
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page names Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR as a three-protein system and links the AC1 locus to lambda, LF82_P8, and P2 protection in Escherichia coli C.

evidence.snippet: Rousset et al. suggested that the TIR-containing protein could generate a nucleotide messenger that in turn could activate the associated transmembrane proteins.
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page records the unresolved Rousset et al. hypothesis that the TIR-containing protein could produce a nucleotide messenger that activates the transmembrane proteins.

evidence.snippet: As far as we are aware, the molecular mechanism is unknown.
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder wiki page leaves the Rst_2TM_1TM_TIR molecular mechanism unresolved.

label: Rst gop-beta-cII system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a P4-like gop-beta-cII locus represented by DefenseFinder as the Rst_gop_beta_cll model and experimentally linked to lambda and P1 phage restriction.

evidence.notes: Rousset et al. describe the canonical P4 satellite gop, beta, and cII locus before testing it for anti-phage activity.

evidence.snippet: We report that gop-β-cII forms an anti-phage system that protects against λ and P1.
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. directly identify gop-beta-cII as an anti-phage system that protects against lambda and P1.

evidence.snippet: When compared with a control vector encoding a green fluorescent protein (GFP), seven systems provided robust and reproducible resistance to at least one phage
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. cloned P4/P2 hotspot systems under native promoters and measured reproducible phage resistance against their coliphage panel.

label: Rst TIR-NLR system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a P4-like TIR-NLR locus represented by DefenseFinder as the Rst_TIR-NLR single-profile model and experimentally linked to broad virulent-phage and P2-like phage restriction.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that hotspots of genetic diversity within the P2-like phage and P4-like satellite families constitute large reservoirs of anti-phage systems.
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. establish that P2-like phage and P4-like satellite hotspots are large reservoirs of anti-phage systems.

evidence.snippet: Validated systems also include a single-gene system with a TIR (toll/interleukin-1-receptor-like) domain protein.
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. describe one validated P4 hotspot system as a single-gene TIR-domain system.

evidence.snippet: Out of the 18 tested systems, only the TIR-NLR system provided protection
evidence.notes: Rousset et al. report that TIR-NLR was the only P4 system in their tested cohort that protected against P2-like phages.

label: SanaTA system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a sanaTA toxin-antitoxin locus represented by DefenseFinder as a SanaA/SanaT two-profile model and experimentally linked to resistance against T7 phage mutants lacking gene 4.5 anti-defense activity.

evidence.snippet: In all six tested pairs, induction of toxin expression inhibited bacterial growth, while co-induction of the toxin and antitoxin resulted in bacterial survival
evidence.notes: Sberro et al. experimentally validated the sanaTA family as one of six new toxin-antitoxin systems.

evidence.snippet: One of the tested systems, sanaTA, was found to provide E. coli with resistance against T7Δ4.5 and T7Δ4.3Δ4.5Δ4.7, reducing sensitivity to these phage strains by about 3 orders of magnitude
evidence.notes: Sberro et al. connect the sanaTA system to lower sensitivity to T7 phages lacking gene 4.5.

evidence.snippet: Since the sanaTA system provides resistance to the T7Δ4.5 mutant phage but not to the WT T7 phage, we hypothesized that the 4.5 gene codes for an anti-defense mechanism that overcomes the abortive infection imposed by the TA system.
evidence.notes: Sberro et al. show that SanaTA resists a T7 gene 4.5 mutant and leave the phage-encoded anti-Abi interaction as part of the system context.

evidence.snippet: Infection experiments with T7 phage showed that two of the new modules can provide resistance against phage.
evidence.notes: Sberro et al. summarize that infection experiments found phage resistance in two of the newly identified modules.

nodes.grounding_notes: No family-level term covers SduA. A bounded search of all InterPro member databases and of GO via OLS4 for 'Shedu' on 2026-10-08 returned only two domain entries plus their InterPro integrations: IPR025359 (Shedu protein SduA, C-terminal; Pfam PF14082, whose InterPro name history is DUF4263 then SduA_C) and IPR048396 (Shedu protein SduA, N-terminal; Pfam PF21407). Neither denotes the whole protein: InterPro reports PF14082 in 1304 UniProt proteins across 2464 taxa with 18 domain architectures, so grounding this whole-protein node to the C-terminal domain would sweep in carriers whose partner domains differ from SduA's. UniProt lists no NCBIfam cross-reference for B7HFR2, and OLS4 returns no GO term for Shedu. The node therefore stays reviewed label-only rather than taking a domain term as a family grounding.

discussions.prompt: Resolve family-wide mechanisms and classify borderline loci.
discussions.rationale: Short denotes the phylogenetic and structural LmuB family, not an arbitrary amino-acid cutoff or an isolated short protein. LmuC-loss clade S and effector-domain-loss clade O preclude requiring one universal three-component effector architecture. Type I/II component classifications and effector names are not exact synonyms for this family. HNH's explicitly short-form definition supports its new parent; SMEK's unresolved long-profile call prevents the same inference. Other table-defined subtypes require their own scope review before reparenting. The Vc-Cap4 mechanism already described on the Lamassu parent is not assumed universal across short-family effectors, so no duplicate or universal mechanism graph is asserted here. A registry Hypothetical label must not be equated with clade O's effector-domain loss without explicit evidence. The LmuC-loss architecture is now represented separately by traitmech:000573 Lamassu type I system. The paper identifies clade S as type I; clade O's effector-domain loss remains a distinct question. The new component class is not treated as a synonym for this whole length family, and its broader phylogenetic distribution is left open rather than inferred from one clade. Existing hierarchy and mechanism scope are unchanged.

label: SPARTA system
definition: A genomics trait describing possession of a short prokaryotic Argonaute TIR-APAZ (SPARTA) locus whose short pAgo and TIR-APAZ proteins form heterodimeric complexes that oligomerize after guide RNA-mediated target DNA binding and unleash TIR domain-mediated NAD(P)ase activity that depletes NAD(P)+ to remove plasmid-invaded cells.

evidence.snippet: short prokaryotic Argonaute and the associated TIR-APAZ (SPARTA) proteins form heterodimeric complexes

evidence.snippet: Upon guide RNA-mediated target DNA binding, four SPARTA heterodimers form oligomers in which TIR domain-mediated NAD(P)ase activity is unleashed
evidence.notes: Koopal et al. support the guide RNA and target DNA-triggered oligomerization mechanism that activates SPARTA NAD(P)ase activity.

evidence.snippet: SPARTA is activated in the presence of highly transcribed multicopy plasmid DNA, which causes cell death through NAD(P)+ depletion
evidence.notes: Koopal et al. support plasmid-challenge activation and NAD(P)+ depletion as experimentally demonstrated SPARTA outcomes.

evidence.snippet: cryo-EM structure of the SPARTA oligomer (tetramer of heterodimers) bound to guide-RNA/target-ssDNA

label: TagI system
definition: A type IV modification-dependent restriction system in which an organism possesses a TagI-family locus encoding an SRA-HNH restriction endonuclease that recognizes 5-methylcytosine- or 5-hydroxymethylcytosine-modified DNA.

evidence.snippet: TagI belongs to the recently characterized SRA-HNH family of modification-dependent restriction endonucleases (REases) that also includes ScoA3IV (Sco5333) and TbiR51I (Tbis1).
evidence.notes: Kisiala et al. support TagI as a member of an SRA-HNH modification-dependent restriction endonuclease family (PMID:30202937 / DOI:10.1093/nar/gky781).

evidence.snippet: Here, we present a crystal structure of dimeric TagI, which exhibits a DNA binding site formed jointly by the nuclease domains, and separate binding sites for modified DNA bases in the two protomers.
evidence.notes: Kisiala et al. support dimeric TagI structure with nuclease and modified-base-binding sites.

evidence.snippet: Their pockets for the flipped bases are spacious enough to accommodate 5-methylcytosine (5mC) or 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), but not glucosyl-5-hydroxymethylcytosine (g5hmC).
evidence.notes: Kisiala et al. support TagI recognition of flipped 5mC and 5hmC bases.

evidence.snippet: Such preference is in agreement with the biochemical determination of the TagI modification dependence and the results of phage restriction assays.
evidence.notes: Kisiala et al. support TagI modification dependence and phage restriction activity.

evidence.snippet: The ability of TagI to digest plasmids methylated by Dcm (C5mCWGG), M.Fnu4HI (G5mCNGC) or M.HpyCH4IV (A5mCGT) suggests that the SRA domains of the enzyme are tolerant to different sequence contexts of the modified base.
evidence.notes: Kisiala et al. support TagI digestion of multiple 5mC-modified plasmid sequence contexts.

evidence.snippet: The new class of modification-dependent restriction enzymes was named Type IV, as distinct from the familiar modification-blocked Types I-III.
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh define the Type IV class as modification-dependent restriction enzymes.

evidence.snippet: | TagI | 10\.1093/nar/gky781 | Crystal structure of the modification-dependent SRA-HNH endonuclease TagI |
evidence.notes: The pinned DefenseFinder article registry maps the TagI source key to the Kisiala et al. structural paper.

label: Thoeris system
definition: A genomics trait describing possession of a Thoeris antiphage defense locus in which phage-triggered TIR-domain proteins generate a cyclic-ADP-ribose-like signal that activates a ThsA NADase effector to deplete NAD and inhibit bacteriophage replication.

evidence.snippet: One such system is the Thoeris defense system, which consists of two genes, thsA and thsB
evidence.notes: Ka et al. support the two-component B. cereus Thoeris system architecture and its standard US-English name.

evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis suggests that NAD+ cleavage is linked to the antiphage function of Thoeris
evidence.notes: Ka et al. support the relationship between ThsA NADase activity and Thoeris antiphage function.

evidence.snippet: phage infection triggers Thoeris TIR-domain proteins to produce an isomer of cyclic ADP-ribose
evidence.notes: Ofir et al. support the phage-triggered TIR-domain signal production that activates the ThsA effector.

evidence.snippet: This molecular signal activates a second protein, ThsA, which then depletes the cell of the essential molecule nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD)
evidence.notes: Ofir et al. connect the Thoeris TIR-domain signal to ThsA NAD depletion.

evidence.snippet: One is from Bacillus cereus MSX-D12. The thsA gene and its downstream thsB gene conferred resistance against myophage infection when engineered into the model bacterium Bacillus subtilis BEST7003
evidence.notes: Ka et al. summarize experimental validation of the native Bacillus cereus MSX-D12 Thoeris thsA-thsB locus.

canonical_examples.note: Ka et al. describe the Bacillus cereus MSX-D12 thsA-thsB Thoeris system that conferred resistance to myophage infection when engineered into a Thoeris-lacking Bacillus subtilis host.

label: ToxIN system
definition: An abortive infection system in which an organism possesses a toxIN type III protein-RNA toxin-antitoxin locus whose ToxN toxin and tandem ToxI RNA antitoxins constitute a two-component Abi module that inhibits bacterial growth and restricts phage propagation.

evidence.snippet: A highly effective 2-gene Abi system from the phytopathogen Erwinia carotovora subspecies atroseptica, designated ToxIN, is described
evidence.notes: Fineran et al. define ToxIN as a two-gene abortive infection system from the native pECA1039 plasmid.

evidence.snippet: ToxN inhibiting bacterial growth and the tandemly repeated ToxI RNA antitoxin counteracting the toxicity
evidence.notes: Fineran et al. connect the ToxN protein toxin and tandem ToxI RNA repeats to the toxin-antitoxin behavior of ToxIN.

evidence.snippet: ToxIN defines an entirely new TA class that functions via a novel protein-RNA mechanism
evidence.notes: Fineran et al. support ToxIN as the defining member of the type III protein-RNA toxin-antitoxin class.

evidence.snippet: All of our data are consistent with ToxIN functioning as a phage Abi system
evidence.notes: Fineran et al. ruled out adsorption blockade and a restriction-modification explanation before classifying ToxIN as abortive infection.

evidence.snippet: ToxN functions through a reversible growth-inhibiting (bacteriostatic) mechanism
evidence.notes: Fineran et al. support host growth inhibition as the ToxN toxin output.

evidence.snippet: Designated ToxIN, this two-component abortive infection system acts as a toxin-antitoxin module
evidence.notes: Blower et al. place the two-component ToxIN module in the abortive infection class.

evidence.snippet: We determined the minimal ToxI RNA sequence in the native operon that is both necessary and sufficient for abortive infection and to counteract the toxicity of ToxN
evidence.notes: Blower et al. connect ToxI RNA repeat dosage to both ToxN neutralization and the native abortive-infection phenotype.

evidence.snippet: this two-component Abi system operates as a novel protein-RNA toxin-antitoxin (TA) system to abort phage infection in multiple gram-negative bacteria
evidence.notes: Blower et al. support the ToxIN system as an Abi trait that can operate beyond the source Erwinia strain.

canonical_examples.note: Fineran et al. isolated pECA1039 from Erwinia carotovora subsp. atroseptica 1039, designated its two-gene Abi system ToxIN, and showed that the native toxIN locus conferred phage resistance in strain SCRI 1043.

label: type II restriction-modification system
definition: A restriction-modification system in which an organism possesses a Type II restriction endonuclease activity paired with cognate methyltransferase self-protection, including conventional RM_Type_II loci represented by DefenseFinder.

evidence.snippet: The action of Type II restriction-modification (RM) systems depends on restriction endonuclease (REase), which cleaves foreign DNA at specific sites, and methyltransferase (MTase), which protects host genome from restriction by methylating the same sites.
evidence.notes: Kirillov et al. describe Type II restriction-modification systems as requiring a restriction endonuclease that cleaves foreign DNA and a methyltransferase that protects host DNA by methylating the same sites.

evidence.snippet: Type II REases are produced by prokaryotes to combat bacteriophages. With extreme accuracy, each recognizes a particular sequence in double-stranded DNA and cleaves at a fixed position within or nearby.
evidence.notes: Pingoud et al. review Type II restriction endonucleases as prokaryotic phage-defense enzymes that recognize specific double-stranded DNA sequences and cleave at fixed positions within or near those sequences.

evidence.snippet: REBASE (rebase.neb.com/rebase/rebase.html), the definitive source for information on REases and their companion proteins
evidence.notes: Pingoud et al. point to REBASE as the source for restriction endonucleases and companion proteins; DefenseFinder links its RM_Type_II model namespace to the 2023 REBASE update.

evidence.snippet: Type IIG (symmetric or asymmetric target sites; endonuclease activity affected by AdoMet (SAM))
evidence.notes: Zhu et al. place Type IIG enzymes in the Type II restriction enzyme classification, supporting the Type IIG child record's reparenting beneath this Type II R-M parent.

evidence.snippet: The action of Type II restriction-modification (RM) systems depends on restriction endonuclease (REase), which cleaves foreign DNA at specific sites, and methyltransferase (MTase), which protects host genome from restriction by methylating the same sites.
evidence.notes: Kirillov et al. describe Type II restriction-modification systems as requiring a restriction endonuclease that cleaves foreign DNA and a methyltransferase that protects host DNA by methylating the same sites.

label: type IIG restriction-modification system
definition: A restriction-modification system in which an organism possesses a Type IIG locus centered on a restriction-methyltransferase-specificity fusion gene represented by DefenseFinder as the RM_Type_IIG subsystem.

evidence.snippet: Type IIG R–M systems also follow this general strategy for target recognition, but instead of encoding separate REase, MTase and specificity subunits, they have evolved to combine them within a single uninterrupted protein chain.
evidence.notes: Shen et al. define Type IIG restriction-modification systems as systems that combine restriction, methyltransferase, and specificity subunits in one uninterrupted protein chain.

evidence.snippet: The entire BpuSI R–M system consists of two MTase genes (M1 and M2) and the R–M fusion gene.
evidence.notes: The characterized BpuSI Type IIG example carries two companion methyltransferase genes and an R-M fusion gene, supporting a locus-level system trait rather than a single protein trait.

evidence.snippet: Type IIG (symmetric or asymmetric target sites; endonuclease activity affected by AdoMet (SAM))
evidence.notes: Zhu et al. place Type IIG in the Type II restriction enzyme classification and describe variable target symmetry plus AdoMet/SAM-sensitive endonuclease activity.

evidence.snippet: Tth111II contains both endonuclease (R) and methylase (M) domains and a shared specificity domain (S).
evidence.notes: The cloned Tth111II Type IIGS enzyme has endonuclease, methylase, and specificity domains in one polypeptide.

evidence.snippet: The biological function of restriction-modification systems is to restrict/cleave foreign invading DNA
evidence.notes: Zhu et al. frame the Type IIGS decision between cleaving and modifying unmodified DNA in the broader restriction-modification role of cleaving foreign invading DNA.

label: type III restriction-modification system
definition: A restriction-modification system in which an organism possesses a Type III R-M locus encoding Mod-like DNA methyltransferase and Res-like ATP-dependent restriction subunits, including RM_Type_III loci represented by DefenseFinder.

evidence.snippet: The Type III REs are hetero-oligomeric assemblies, comprising polypeptides encoded by the res (restriction) and mod (modification) genes (4).
evidence.notes: Butterer et al. describe Type III restriction endonucleases as hetero-oligomeric assemblies encoded by res restriction and mod modification genes.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we present a series of results obtained by native mass spectrometry and size exclusion chromatography with multi-angle light scattering consistent with a 1:2 ratio of Res to Mod subunits in the EcoP15I, EcoPI and PstII complexes as the main holoenzyme species and a 1:1 stoichiometry of specific DNA (sDNA) binding by EcoP15I and EcoPI.
evidence.notes: Butterer et al. support a Type III R-M holoenzyme model with one Res subunit and two Mod subunits for characterized EcoP15I, EcoPI, and PstII complexes.

label: type IV modification-dependent restriction system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Type IV modification-dependent restriction locus, including DefenseFinder RM_Type_IV loci, whose restriction-enzyme activity cleaves foreign DNA carrying recognized base or backbone modifications rather than the unmodified targets of canonical Type I-III restriction-modification systems.

evidence.snippet: The new class of modification-dependent restriction enzymes was named Type IV, as distinct from the familiar modification-blocked Types I–III.
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh define Type IV as modification-dependent restriction, distinct from modification-blocked Types I-III.

evidence.snippet: Type IV enzymes recognize modified DNA with low sequence selectivity and have emerged many times independently during evolution.
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh support the broad Type IV class as enzymes that recognize modified DNA with limited sequence specificity.

evidence.snippet: there are enzymes that attack DNA only when the modification is present
evidence.notes: Loenen and Raleigh contrast modification-dependent restriction with protective modification by describing enzymes that attack DNA only when a modification is present.

evidence.snippet: The Escherichia coli CT596 prophage exclusion genes gmrS and gmrD were found to encode a novel type IV modification-dependent restriction nuclease that targets and digests glucosylated (glc)-hydroxymethylcytosine (HMC) DNAs.
evidence.notes: Bair and Black experimentally support GmrSD as a Type IV modification-dependent restriction nuclease targeting glucosylated hydroxymethylcytosine DNA.

evidence.snippet: Overall activities of the purified GmrSD enzyme are in good agreement with the properties of the cloned gmr genes in vivo and suggest a restriction enzyme specific for sugar modified HMC DNAs.
evidence.notes: Bair and Black verify purified GmrSD restriction activity against sugar-modified hydroxymethylcytosine DNA, one concrete activity within the Type IV branch.

label: Ukko system

evidence.snippet: Among the remaining eight systems, six demonstrated increased resistance to at least one phage with more than 100 fold reduction in plaque forming units (PFU) (Figure 3a, Supplementary Figure 5). As Streptomyces are mostly soil dwelling bacteria, we named these systems after deities of the soil and earth (Ceres, Geb, Veles, Prithvi, Ukko and Oshun).
evidence.notes: Mordret et al. directly name Ukko among six Streptomyces systems that increased resistance to at least one phage.
