label: bacterial polar flagellar ejection
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a bacterium actively ejects previously assembled axial structures of a polar flagellum by separation at its base.

evidence.snippet: Plesiomonas cells consistently lose their flagella at the base of the hook
evidence.notes: Ferreira et al. 2019, PMID:30889173, PMC6424402. Results, Shed hook-filament structures accumulate in P. shigelloides supernatant, sole paragraph (HTML anchor article1.body1.sec2.sec4.p1; PDF pp. 4-5); Figure 1G. Direct publisher full-text match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT. Hook-bearing released structures, population counts and relic/assembly comparisons support ejection rather than daughter-cell dilution or passive midfilament breakage. Nutrient-depletion conditions vary among assays; minimal medium containing glucose is not complete carbon starvation. All 25 main PDF pages and six figures were inspected, not raw supplementary data. Energy conservation and leakage prevention are interpretations.

evidence.snippet: bacteria can actively abandon flagella after prolonged stationary culturing
evidence.notes: Zhuang et al. 2020, PMID:32259388, scientific abstract, sentence beginning Interestingly. Direct MED/publisher match and native VERIFIED. Main publisher text and six figure captions were subsequently read, not the actual figures or supplement. Sections 2.4-2.7 separate daughter-cell dilution from stationary-phase shedding. OD times flagellated fraction is a population proxy, not a direct cell count. VIO5 and engineered EGFP-FliG strain NMB344 are distinct; red/green panels in Figure 3 are not the same cells. Two-color experiments in Figures 5-6 support basal release, but rod breakage is inferred, not a directly imaged cut. Surface immobilization and medium exchanges constrain the assay.

evidence.snippet: Nutrient depletion significantly increases the frequency of flagellar shedding and the accumulation of closed FOMCs
evidence.notes: Guo et al. 2026, PMID:42660870, PMC13521929.1, Results, Two distinct in situ architectures of the flagellar motor in V. cholerae, and Supplementary Figure 4. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT. FOMC denotes the flagellar outer membrane complex. The quoted experiment uses wild-type V. cholerae; delta-flhG structural samples are distinct. All 12 main PDF pages and six main figures were inspected, plus the actual supplementary Figure 4 and supplementary tables. Its 81/273 observations are cells in the figure caption and tomograms in Methods/Table 4, not biological replicates or ejection rates. The main-text Table 3 pointer instead corresponds to Table 4. Other supplements remain incompletely read.

discussions.prompt: Review active basal release separately from possession, loss and resorption.
discussions.rationale: This qualified phenotype requires active basal release of previously assembled polar flagellar axial structures. Hook-filament release is an observed endpoint, not a universal component-completeness requirement. Flagellar possession or arrangement, assembly failure, motor arrest, reduced motility, a decreasing flagellated fraction or passive filament breakage alone do not establish it. Periplasmic resorption and microbial-eukaryotic axonemal autotomy are distinct. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is a definition-based parent inference; locomotory possession is not a required parent. The definition does not require every flagellum to be lost, nonmotility, a particular stimulus, exact severing site, relic morphology or universal behavior among polar-flagellated bacteria. No bare shedding or deflagellation exact synonym is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Review the phenotype hierarchy without reviving retired flagellar identifiers.
discussions.rationale: Pinned and current METPO release annotations distinguish motility, locomotory flagellar possession and polar arrangement from ejection. Historical METPO:0000089 and METPO:000090 are deprecated with OMO:0001000; METPO:1000381 is deprecated with IAO:0000226. Their replacement METPO:1000704 denotes possession, not shedding. Deprecated flagellum METPO:1000123 has OMO:0001000 and no observed replacement or consider annotation. These are not exact mappings and are not reactivated. The current editor is an import stub, not a full release. The ontology pin remains unchanged. Proposal v608 reserves METPO:1068500 within 1068500-1068599; the local identifier is traitmech:000732. No upstream release or human sign-off is implied.

discussions.prompt: Keep organismal ejection separate from universal molecular and sequence claims.
discussions.rationale: The 2026 structures assign closure to FlgI conformational changes in V. cholerae; the 2019 interpretation of an unidentified added plug is not imposed as a universal mechanism. Assembly defects in gate-deletion mutants do not by themselves demonstrate failure of ejection. Cryo-ET states are not a longitudinal trajectory of the same motor. A protein-resolved causal graph needs taxon-paired authority-checked accessions and edge-specific evidence. Gene, motif and domain presence alone do not establish this organism-level phenotype. Mechanisms are deferred, not claimed absent.

discussions.prompt: Resolve assay-specific strain provenance before asserting canonical taxa.
discussions.rationale: Source organism names remain qualified observations, not independently resolved canonical taxon assertions. Engineered structural samples and source-designated wild-type nutrient assays must not be conflated. MED metadata and accessible publisher text were checked; unavailable publisher or PubMed pages are access limits, not evidence that no notice exists. This is not comprehensive correction/retraction clearance, raw-data reanalysis, independent replication, paid research or human sign-off.

label: ballistospore discharge
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a fungus forcibly discharges spores through coalescence of Buller's drop with liquid on the spore surface.

evidence.snippet: At the moment of fusion, Buller's drop snaps from the hilar appendix onto the adjacent spore surface.
evidence.notes: Stolze-Rybczynski et al. (2009), PMID:19129912, PMC2612744; Introduction, first paragraph, directly retrieved as publisher HTML and Europe PMC full-text XML. Abstract, Introduction, Results and Discussion, Table 1 and Methods were read. Seven basidiomycete species were analyzed by high-speed video; the yeast Sporobolomyces salmonicolor NPM01 had a measured mean launch speed of 1.42 +/- 0.12 m/s (s.e.m., six launches). Its 0.54 +/- 0.04 mm flight range is calculated, not a directly measured range. Drop geometry and flight range vary; a prominent lens-shaped adaxial drop is not universal. Figure captions were read, but image retrieval failed; actual figures, videos and supplements were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: Ballistospores can be produced either asexually (ballistoconidia) or sexually (basidiospores).
evidence.notes: Ianiri et al. (2014), PMID:25148260, PMC4141788; Introduction directly retrieved as full-text XML. This quotation supports terminology, not a new comparison of sexual and asexual development. Scientific abstract, strain table, mirror-assay Methods, initial mutant-screen Results and Discussion were also read. Of 18 mirror mutants, 17 had absent or reduced spore production; GI277 still formed abundant ballistospores but failed to release them. A failed mirror assay alone thus does not distinguish formation from discharge. PHS1 results concern delayed formation and broader cellular defects, not a demonstrated universal release motor. Actual figures, supplements and independent IAM 13481 provenance were not inspected; no canonical example is inferred from these mutants.

evidence.snippet: The fusion of the droplet onto the spore creates a momentum that propels the spore forward.
evidence.notes: Noblin, Yang and Dumais (2009), PMID:19684219; scientific abstract retrieved directly through Europe PMC. The study reports high-speed observations in Auricularia auricula and Sporobolomyces yeasts, mechanical analysis and calibrated microcantilever measurements of detachment work. The artificial validation system is not a fungal exemplar. Predicted and observed velocities are distinct quantities. Full text, figures, supplements and strain provenance were not inspected; the abstract is not a complete mechanistic audit.

canonical_examples.note: Strain NPM01. Table 1 reports high-speed-video launch measurements from six spores, with mean initial speed 1.42 +/- 0.12 m/s (s.e.m.); the listed flight distance is modeled, not directly measured. Organisms and culture methods at https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0004163 identify NPM01 as isolated from a contaminated manufacturing facility and report spore formation on potato dextrose agar within 24 h. That primary provenance passage was read directly; no engineered-strain origin is inferred. NCBI Taxonomy resolves the species ID and label. This example concerns NPM01 under the reported conditions, not every strain or life stage.

discussions.prompt: Review dispersal hierarchy without equating formation and discharge.
discussions.rationale: Use phenotype METPO:1000059. The sporulation and spore-forming records METPO:1000870 and METPO:1000871 concern endospores. Fungal conidiation traitmech:000657 concerns production of asexual propagules, whereas ballistospores include sexual and asexual forms and formation can persist without release. Discharge is also distinct from passive shedding, later wind transport and pressure-driven ascospore or sporangium ejection. Motility METPO:1000701 emphasizes independent locomotion; a closer dispersal parent and process-versus-phenotype mappings need review. Ballistospore and ballistoconidium name cells, not exact synonyms of this disposition; no exact synonyms or xrefs are asserted. Do not require a particular speed, distance, fruiting body or asexual developmental mode.

label: behavioral habituation
definition: A physiological phenotype in which repeated stimulation produces an experience-dependent decrease in a microbial organism's behavioral response that is not attributable solely to sensory adaptation or motor fatigue.

evidence.snippet: The Q and CAF slime moulds crossing a bridge containing quinine or caffeine for the sixth time showed reduced aversive behaviour.
evidence.notes: Boisseau et al. 2016, PMID:27122563, PMC4855389; page 4, Results (b), Test phase 1. Q and CAF denote cultured Physarum polycephalum plasmodia repeatedly exposed to quinine or caffeine bridges. Five daily exposures precede same/alternate-repellent tests; two plain-agar days precede retesting. Contact latency, crossing time and shape are different readouts. Caffeine does not show every quinine effect: initial crossing time was not slower than control, and recovery was incomplete. Residual aversiveness remains. Alternate-repellent responses support stimulus specificity, not universal exclusion of every confound. Main Methods, Results, Discussion and all five figures were inspected in a public publisher-formatted PDF bearing a 2016 download stamp, not verified as the current corrected VoR. Supplementary statistics and raw data were not assessed. The contiguous quote crosses PDF columns; direct text and visual checks agree. Native abstract lookup: NOT_IN_ABSTRACT.

evidence.snippet: the response to the low force stimuli shows extensive habituation even though the response to the alternating high force stimuli does not.
evidence.notes: Rajan and Marshall 2025, PMID:40562036, PMC13499368; Figure 4F caption, concluding result clause in retained PMC author-manuscript HTML. Figure 4F is an experimental contraction response in cultured Stentor coeruleus, not the adjacent model panel. Preserved stronger-stimulus responses argue against general motor exhaustion. The caption describes identical control timing, while Methods describes one low-force control tap per minute versus alternating forces at one total tap per minute; exact cadence equivalence remains unresolved. Figure 4I uses intervening low-force stimulation, not a stimulus-free rest; Figure 5 separately tests recovery after training. Anchored healthy nondividing cells were selected from Ward's cultures; field-of-view denominators vary. Experimental Results, relevant Methods and actual Figures 4-7 were inspected. Receptor internalization is modeled, not an identified molecular mechanism. Supplements and simulations were not reanalyzed. Native abstract lookup: NOT_IN_ABSTRACT; the exact full-text caption match is a separate check.

evidence.snippet: For cells treated with either cycloheximide or puromycin, the primary effect on learning was accelerating habituation (Figure 1C, 1E).
evidence.notes: Rajan et al. 2026, PMID:42025171, PMC13192338; Results S3, retained PMC author manuscript. Stentor contraction assays compare drug-treated and vehicle cultures under repeated mechanical stimulation. Figure 1C uses puromycin with two-hour pretreatment; Figure 1E describes 12-hour cycloheximide pretreatment, unlike general short-term Methods prose. Dose, stimulus strength and cadence differ; conditions are not interchangeable. Drug effects do not prove universally protein-synthesis-independent learning. Relevant Results and Methods and actual Figures 1, 3, 4 and 6 were inspected, not all omics analyses or supplements. RNAi and pharmacology retain off-target, anchoring, feeding and subculture limitations. SteCoe_6763 recovery differences were not significant. Figure 6 follows division during continuing stimuli, not retention after withdrawal. Results and Methods point to different supplementary electrical-control panels. This follow-up shares a laboratory with the 2025 study, not an independent replication. Native abstract lookup: NOT_IN_ABSTRACT; directly matched Results quote.

evidence.snippet: Habituation is defined as a behavioral response decrement that results from repeated stimulation and that does not involve sensory adaptation/sensory fatigue or motor fatigue.
evidence.notes: Rankin et al. 2009, PMID:18854219, PMC2754195; section 2, page 136 (PDF page 2), complete opening definition. This consensus review supports operational terminology, not a microbial experiment or independent replication. Its nervous-system framing is not imposed on non-neural microbes. The public institutional PDF was directly read and pages 2-4 visually inspected. PDF ligatures are expanded and whitespace folded for matching; no paraphrase is substituted. Partial recovery is allowed. Responding to a novel stimulus is not itself dishabituation, which restores the original response. The behavioral criteria are not a demonstrated common molecular mechanism. Source-qualified MED identity was checked; its absent commentCorrectionList is not exhaustive notice clearance.

discussions.prompt: Retain a behavioral endpoint and distinguish neighboring uses of adaptation.
discussions.rationale: Repeated-stimulus decrement alone is insufficient: evaluate sensory adaptation, motor fatigue, injury/toxicity, selection and depletion alternatives in the actual assay. Specificity and recovery provide operational support without identifying all underlying mechanisms. Rankin 2009 frames habituation in neural behavioral terms; Rajan 2025 distinguishes that usage from cellular adaptation while modeling related receptor dynamics. This record concerns microbial behavior, not a categorical ban on shared molecular machinery. No fixed time, curve, complete recovery, dishabituation or all ten hallmarks are required in every experiment. Response to a stronger stimulus is not itself dishabituation. Carbon-source memory (traitmech:000706), acquired stress-resistance memory (traitmech:000712), enhanced transcriptional reactivation memory (traitmech:000713), anticipation, bet hedging and nutrient adaptation have distinct endpoints. Chemotaxis is not a parent of every behavioral assay. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent; generic learning, memory and adaptation are not asserted as exact synonyms.

discussions.prompt: Resolve source discrepancies and culture provenance before adding taxa or mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Different taxa and assays support the phenotype, not independent replication of each experiment. Laboratory culture provenance has not been independently resolved for natural canonical taxa; no species-wide assignment follows. Unread supplements, raw data and statistical reanalysis remain gaps. The 2025 control cadence, 2026 cycloheximide timing and electrical-control locators remain unresolved source discrepancies. Retained public PDFs and author manuscripts are not verified equivalent to current corrected publisher versions. Bounded MED/Crossref checks are not proof of notice absence. Modeled receptor internalization, exploratory omics and drug/RNAi effects do not justify a universal protein-resolved mechanism. No causal graph, protein examples, canonical taxa or exact external mappings are asserted. Access failures, source hashes and actual snippet-verifier results are in the sidecar.

discussions.rationale: Pinned and inspected current METPO graphs mark METPO:1000004 adaptation, METPO:1000005 adaptive trait, METPO:0000248 and METPO:000249 Microbial Adaptation deprecated below ObsoleteClass, with OMO:0001000 and no inspected replacement or consider annotations. METPO issue 521 disputes the mechanically assigned reasons. Original historical scopes remain unresolved; labels do not prove equivalence or nonequivalence. This operational behavioral phenotype is accepted independently from primary evidence, not by reviving an obsolete term or inferring biological invalidity. Available ignored/hidden files, retained tracked history, pending changes, ontology graphs and live corpus semantics revealed no exact active record in the inspected scope. No historical exact mapping is asserted. The pinned ontology and existing records remain unchanged; discovery is not exhausted.

label: bioluminescence
definition: A physiological capability to emit visible light through a luciferase-catalyzed reaction, frequently regulated by quorum sensing in marine bacteria such as Aliivibrio and Photobacterium.

evidence.notes: Brodl, Winkler & Macheroux review the molecular mechanisms of bacterial bioluminescence and the luciferase reaction.
Waters & Bassler support quorum-sensing regulation of light production in luminous bacteria.

canonical_examples.note: Model bioluminescent bacterium (lux operon); Euprymna squid light-organ symbiont and quorum-sensing paradigm.

causal_graphs.title: Luciferase-catalyzed light emission
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed causal sketch linking luciferase to oxygen-dependent light emission, often under quorum-sensing control.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph describes the A. fischeri Lux system. LuxAB is a heterodimer, LuxCDE is a three-component fatty-acid reductase system, and LuxI/LuxR regulation is not universal to all bioluminescent organisms. The taxon-paired example anchors the LuxI quorum-sensing branch.

label: biomineralization
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbe mediates the formation of mineral phases.

evidence.snippet: Microorganisms can mediate the formation of minerals by a process called biomineralization.
evidence.notes: Benzerara et al. 2011, scientific Abstract, directly checked in publisher HTML on 2026-10-10. Definition terminology, not an independent experimental replication: this is a review. Its Introduction and section 2 distinguish controlled, induced and biologically influenced formation, including organic-matrix effects. TraitMech represents the microbial phenotype rather than equating it with a process or material entity. The source cautions that association with pre-existing minerals does not establish formation. The remainder and actual figures were not audited for this record.

evidence.snippet: All bacteria tested induce the precipitation of a significant amount of calcium carbonate when cultured in M-3P medium.
evidence.notes: Rodriguez-Navarro et al. 2012, PMID:22447589, PMC3346411, Discussion, Bacterial carbonatogenesis. Publisher scientific Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results and relevant Discussion directly read on 2026-10-10; actual Figures 1 and 6 inspected, other figures not visually audited. Inoculated assays produced carbonates whereas uninoculated substrate controls did not. Tested M. xanthus strain 422, B. diminuta SJ 63 and a stone bacterial community are assay labels, not verified canonical taxa here. Polymorph selection depends on the stated substrate/medium conditions, not a universal strain rule. The proposed amorphous precursor is not established by morphology alone. No universal urease requirement or functional protein mechanism is inferred.

evidence.snippet: Coccoliths are calcitic particles produced inside the cells of unicellular marine algae known as coccolithophores.
evidence.notes: Sviben et al. 2016, PMID:27075521, PMC4834641. Scientific Abstract directly checked in Europe PMC full-text XML on 2026-10-10; Introduction, calcite-resupply Results and Discussion also inspected. This supports controlled mineral production and the coccolith child's placement. Historical E. huxleyi AWI1516 observations do not establish every strain's current phenotype. A separate calcium-rich compartment is not proven to be a necessary direct precursor or bulk-transfer route. No new figure or supplement audit is claimed for this parent; the child's more detailed provenance is retained.

evidence.snippet: Scales were formed one by one in silica deposition vesicles (SDVs)
evidence.notes: Nomura and Ishida 2016, PMID:27348459. Scientific abstract directly read on 2026-10-10 at https://rrc.nbrp.jp/references/56432?lang=en. Scale formation and silicon detection in immature-scale vesicles support mineral production beyond carbonates and the siliceous-scale child's placement. Historical Paulinella chromatophora naming does not establish current strain taxonomy. Full Methods and figures remain unread; proposed microtubule involvement is not molecular necessity. Scale production is distinct from subsequent shell assembly.

discussions.prompt: Keep mineral formation distinct from association and process-level mappings.
discussions.rationale: The definition includes controlled, induced and matrix-mediated formation when microbial mediation is demonstrated; it is not restricted to carbonate, intracellular deposition or a crystalline end product. Benzerara et al. DOI:10.1016/j.crte.2010.09.002 section 2 includes passive organic-matter effects under biologically influenced biomineralization. This broad terminology is retained, but precipitation near a cell, isolated nonliving-matrix activity, mineral adhesion, uptake of preformed particles or ion adsorption alone does not establish that organism's formation phenotype. Organic-substrate mineralization, mineral dissolution, metal tolerance and mineral use as an electron donor are not equivalent. Coccolith and siliceous-scale production are narrower endpoints. Magnetosome and ferrosome organelle records retain their structural parents; no automatic cross-axis reparenting or disjointness is asserted. The magnetosome graph's similarly named node has narrower scope and is not exactly grounded to this umbrella. No synonyms or xrefs are asserted pending authority-backed phenotype mapping.

discussions.prompt: Resolve assay-specific exemplars and distinct mineral-forming mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: No canonical examples are assigned before strain provenance and current taxonomy are reconciled with the original assays. A community precipitation assay cannot be assigned wholesale to each community member. Substrate, medium, mineral phase, location and life stage qualify observations. No universal benefit, growth dependence, genetic control, obligatory enzyme or shared protein pathway follows from this umbrella. Separate controlled deposition from metabolically induced precipitation and organic-matrix effects when adding mechanisms. Functional evidence and taxon-paired accessions are required for protein edges; sequence features or mineral co-localization alone are insufficient. Mechanism is deferred, not claimed absent.

label: bipolar mating system
definition: A fungal mating phenotype in which compatibility between partners is governed by a single segregating mating-type factor.

evidence.snippet: A bipolar system is defined by a single genetic locus (MAT) that can have two or multiple alleles.
evidence.notes: Bakkeren and Kronstad (1994), PMID:7913746, PMC44343. Exact scientific-abstract sentence directly retrieved from Europe PMC core metadata. The abstract reports cloning of Ustilago hordei a1 and physical linkage of a and b into a complex MAT region, contrasted with genetically unlinked loci in U. maydis. The compatibility factor is not necessarily one gene. This supports definition and a reported linkage architecture, not a fresh verification of native crossing assays. Full text, figures, methods, supplements and natural strain provenance remain uninspected; no canonical strain is inferred.

evidence.snippet: All of the 24 collections displayed a bipolar mating system with only two mating types among all progeny of a collection.
evidence.notes: James et al. (2006), PMID:16461425, PMC1456265. Exact sentence in the first Results subsection on p. 1881, visually checked in the published PDF at https://public.websites.umich.edu/~mycology/resources/Publications/james2006.genetics.pdf; not an abstract quote. Native Coprinellus disseminatus single-spore crosses support the compatibility phenotype. Two types per collection does not mean only two across the species. Methods score clamps and dikaryotization, not automatically completed fertile sex; poor-mating progeny were excluded when choosing population testers. Table 3 shows segregation in 13 TJ00/38 progeny: MIP tracks mating type, whereas CDSTE3.1-.3 do not. Its plus/minus states are PCR-RFLP genotypes, not gene presence or absence; CDSTE3.4 lacks segregation data. The abstract reports heterologous sexual responses, not loss of all pheromone-receptor function. PDF pp. 1877-1882 and actual Tables 1-3 were read; pp. 1883-1884 were text-extracted only. Actual figures, later Results/Discussion and supplements remain uninspected. Natural North Carolina fruit-body provenance is described in Methods, but active taxon authority and the intersterile Japanese group remain unresolved; no canonical taxon assertion is made.

discussions.prompt: Keep genetic compatibility distinct from locus inventory and partner dependence.
discussions.rationale: A single segregating compatibility factor need not be one gene, exactly two specificities across a species, or fused pheromone/receptor and homeodomain loci. Bakkeren describes recognition in heterothallic basidiomycetes, but its examples do not establish universal separate-partner dependence under the organism-level definition of traitmech:000610. The functional compatibility axis differs from self-fertility and from tetrapolar mating (traitmech:000615), which requires differences at two independently segregating factors. Use released phenotype METPO:1000059 in record and proposal; do not assert disjointness with homothallism, universal self-sterility or a sufficient guarantee of fertility. Resolve unifactorial terminology and external equivalences before adding synonyms or xrefs. PHYSIOLOGY is a filesystem category, not a narrower ontology parent.

discussions.prompt: Resolve native mechanisms and taxon authority before adding graphs or examples.
discussions.rationale: Complete unread source sections and inspect actual figures and supplements before extending mechanistic claims. Loss of mating-type specificity is not absence of receptor genes or loss of every cellular function. Keep native compatibility assays, genetic segregation, heterologous responses and completed fertile reproduction distinct. Resolve NCBI taxon authority and strain scope before canonical examples, and native protein accessions plus tested dependencies before causal edges. No NONMECHANISTIC graph bypasses grounding. Manual full-text checks do not replace the abstract resolver's actual verdict.

label: carbon-source memory
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a non-genetic cellular state established by prior carbon-source conditions persists after those conditions change and alters subsequent induction or growth responses to carbon sources.

evidence.snippet: Cells grown under cyclical glucose/lactose conditions thus displayed phenotypic memory of their previous metabolic adaptation.
evidence.notes: Lambert and Kussell 2014, PMID:25255314, PMC4177670; Results / Phenotypic memory in response to sudden environmental changes, not the abstract. Primary text, actual Figure 2 and Text S1 were inspected. Repeated glucose/lactose switches demonstrate history-dependent growth; the paper distinguishes inherited protein persistence from continuing induction after stimulus removal. F3 is an engineered W3110 derivative, not an unmodified natural exemplar. Growth is a chamber-level relative elongation readout. DOI:10.1371/journal.pgen.1004793 corrects author-name typesetting, not the biological claims; the correction was read. Model predictions are not additional experimental replication. Other figures, raw data and equations were not independently reanalyzed.

evidence.snippet: past exposure to an environmental condition can shorten the time needed to adapt when the condition re-occurs
evidence.notes: Cerulus et al. 2018, PMID:30299256, PMC6211830; scientific abstract, confirmed against NCBI full-text XML. Relevant Results, Methods, Discussion, actual Figures 1, 2, 6 and Figure 1 supplement 4 were inspected. Carbon-shift assays separate population lag from single-cell growth resumption; cells not resuming within the observation window are not thereby proved dead. Cross-sugar effects and respiratory perturbations oppose an obligatory same-sugar or sugar-specific protein-inheritance mechanism. The main AN63 series is engineered; the separately reported non-laboratory strains have unreviewed primary provenance here. Publisher article access was challenged; public figure assets were accessible. Raw data and all other supplements were not reanalyzed.

evidence.snippet: This "galactose memory" persists for several generations
evidence.notes: Zacharioudakis et al. 2007, PMID:17997309; directly retrieved, source-qualified MED scientific abstract only. The preceding sentence compares initial GAL activation with rapid reactivation in progeny after intervening glucose growth. This supports the induction endpoint, not a measured growth-rate benefit. Its Gal1 and cytoplasmic-factor interpretation remains assay-specific; the abstract's chromatin conclusion is not universalized. Full text, figures and strain provenance were not inspected. The index links a Comment in, not a correction or independent replication.

discussions.prompt: Retain carbon-source history dependence without conflating its endpoints or neighboring traits.
discussions.rationale: The qualifier carbon-source bounds this curator-defined class. Unqualified cellular, metabolic, phenotypic and transcriptional memory, bistability and hysteresis are not asserted as exact synonyms. Demonstrating the phenotype requires comparing prior histories under matched test conditions and genetic background; a single diauxic transition, persistent reporter fluorescence, gene presence or a different current medium alone is insufficient. Induction kinetics and growth recovery are distinct endpoints, and one must not be substituted for the other. No fixed duration, number of divisions, benefit, particular sugar, or molecular mechanism is required. Genetic adaptation, immune memory, chemotactic temporal sensing, stress priming and stochastic bet hedging are not equivalent. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is a trophic-type class locally framed as the chronic copiotroph/oligotroph axis; diauxic growth denotes sequential nutrient use, and generalist/specialist describe niche breadth. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream hierarchy review. This is not a sequence-feature record or a precomposed uses-carbon-source assertion.

discussions.prompt: Resolve natural strain provenance and assay-specific causal branches before adding exemplars or a graph.
discussions.rationale: The retained observations do not establish a uniform species-wide phenotype or a common protein-resolved mechanism. Canonical taxa require primary provenance and authority-resolved taxon identity; no canonical_examples, causal_graphs or external xrefs are asserted. Source-qualified MED and Crossref records were checked on 2026-10-12. Lambert's linked correction was read and retained in evidence notes; no other linked correction or retraction was exposed by these bounded records. Publisher/full-text access limits are recorded per source, not treated as absence of notices. The pinned and current upstream METPO releases contain no exact memory class found by the ignored/hidden lexical and RDF assessment; the ontology baseline remains unchanged.

label: cell-body contraction
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell actively shortens its body by contraction of intracellular structures.

evidence.snippet: Ca2+ concentrations from 10−6 to 10−2 M in the culture medium could stimulate cell contraction while maintaining the viability of the cell.
evidence.notes: Zhang et al. 2023, PMID:36812318, PMCID:PMC9946354, Results: functional analysis of giant backbone proteins, second paragraph. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The study identified its East Lake, Wuhan isolate as Spirostomum minus using morphology, protargol staining and SSU rDNA, then established clonal cultures at 22 C. Actual Figure 1A shows extended and contracted cell bodies. The quoted treatment maintained viability; 38-to-16 seconds describes intervals between contractions, not contraction duration. Selected Results, Methods and Discussion, actual Figures 1, 6 and 9, and relevant supplement pages were inspected. Figure 9 is a mechanistic schematic. Supplementary Figure 7 shows shortening during death, which is insufficient for this trait. Abnormal-cell counts are in Supplementary Table 2, not Table S1 as cited in the RNAi Results. Rare twisted RNAi phenotypes do not establish contraction loss in every treated cell. The source's superscript exponents mean 10^(-6) to 10^(-2) M; the normalized plain-text quotation does not preserve superscript styling.

Floyd et al. 2023, PMID:37307463, PMCID:PMC10288572, Figure 4 caption, contiguous observed-asymmetry clause. Direct JATS match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The quoted top and bottom ends are those of the imaged Spirostomum cell body in Figure 4A-C, not Vorticella's stalk or simulated springs. The actual panel A contours and panel B solid length trajectory show body shortening; panel C shows the staggered endpoint movements. Dashed model curves are separate from observations. The 15-word caption span replaces the data-presentation excerpt rejected in #1935; historical source receipts remain in the sidecar. Actual Figures 1A and 2A-B show Spirostomum body shortening and experimental trajectories separately from fitted curves. Methods used commercially sourced cultures and high-speed imaging without compressing cells; no species identity is inferred. Supplementary Figure S3 measures length along the central backbone curve, with increasing width. Supplementary Figure S6 states that repeated contractions of the same organism were not distinguished from contractions of different organisms: five traces are not five established biological replicates. Vorticella panels measure stalk contraction, not the body endpoint. Calcium-wave and energy models are not universal molecular proof. Selected experimental sections, actual Figures 1-2 and supplementary pages 3 and 5 were inspected; raw videos and the complete model were not reanalyzed.
evidence.snippet: Asymmetric contraction can be observed as the top end begins contracting before the bottom end
Living Vorticella showed a graded shrinkage of the cell body when Ca2+ buffer was injected into the cell body
evidence.notes: Katoh and Naitoh 1994, PMID:9317557, scientific Abstract item 3, first clause. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED abstract match and native VERIFIED. The same sentence contrasts graded cell-body shrinkage with all-or-nothing stalk coiling. Triton-extracted preparations in other abstract items are not the living-cell injection assay. Calcium-release causality is presented as an assumption, not direct molecular proof. Publisher HTML and PDF requests returned 403; full Methods, figures and strain provenance were not accessed. No species-wide example, quantitative threshold or universal trigger is inferred.

The axopodial record's broader cellular-contractility parent question is not resolved by this body-specific class; do not reparent it here. label: cell body or cytoplasmic projection contraction
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell actively contracts its body or a cytoplasmic projection, reducing its length or extension.

evidence.snippet: Living Vorticella showed a graded shrinkage of the cell body when Ca2+ buffer was injected into the cell body
evidence.notes: Katoh and Naitoh 1994, PMID:9317557, scientific Abstract item 3, first clause. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED match; native VERIFIED. The same sentence contrasts graded cell-body shrinkage with all-or-nothing stalk coiling. This supports the curator-synthesized body/projection-shortening parent, not a universal calcium threshold. Other abstract items use Triton-extracted preparations, not the living-cell injection assay. Calcium-induced calcium release is an assumption, not direct molecular proof. Publisher requests returned 403; full Methods, figures and strain provenance were not accessed.

evidence.snippet: Axopodial contraction of the centrohelid heliozoon Raphidiophrys contractilis was induced by mechanical or electrical stimulation.
evidence.notes: Khan et al. 2003, PMID:14624035, scientific Abstract opening sentence. Direct namespace-qualified Europe PMC MED match; native VERIFIED. This supports stimulated shortening of a cytoplasmic projection rather than whole-cell locomotion. Reported calcium dependence and speed apply to this assay, not every member of the parent class. Non-detection of other filaments after fixation is not proof of their absence. Full Methods and figures were not accessed; the publisher's HTTP 200 response was an access challenge, not readable article content. Current taxonomic and culture identities remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Both recording techniques showed that the rapid contraction involves 80% of the total cell length.
evidence.notes: Febvre-Chevalier and Febvre 1992, PMID:1639845, PMCID:PMC2289557, Results, Kinetics of the Contraction, printed page 588, right column. Direct extracted-PDF match with the typeset passage visually checked; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The primary PDF was retrieved from its Semantic Scholar mirror after official PDF attempts failed. Selected Methods/Results and actual Figures 1 and 3-6 were inspected. Length was measured from head top to stalk base, not isolated cell-body length; graph axes use stalk length. The percentage is study-specific. Natural-seawater responses differ from artificially slowed responses. The specimens were collected near Villefranche and cultured at 14-18 C; current taxonomic identity is not verified. The n=20 initial-length sample is not asserted as independent contraction replication. Microtubule disassembly accompanies shortening, but this study expressly does not establish force production. Its disassembly half-time is not automatically contraction duration. The accessible JATS contains an abstract and PDF pointer, not the complete experimental text.

discussions.prompt: Review the shortening-defined parent without equating all contractility endpoints.
discussions.rationale: Require active reduction of cell-body length or the extension of a cytoplasmic projection. Generic force production or isometric contractility alone is insufficient. Extracellular pilus retraction, injection-system contraction, contractile-vacuole cycling and cytokinetic constriction alone do not establish this endpoint. Neither passive osmotic shrinkage, death-associated shortening nor static short-cell morphology suffices. The existing body and rapid axopodial traits are narrower children; stalk contraction traitmech:000730 is now a narrower child, defined by active reduction of stalk end-to-end extension. This does not require shortening of the stalk contour or make its sheath cytoplasm. Motility METPO:1000701 and motile METPO:1000702 concern locomotion, not necessarily shortening. Active denotes the cellular response, not demonstrated ATP-driven motor action. No universal speed, fractional shortening, trigger, calcium threshold, ATP dependence, ecological role, exact synonym for generic contractility or organism-level disjointness is asserted.

label: functional cellular rejuvenation
definition: A physiological phenotype in which age-associated loss of cellular performance or replicative potential is reversed in a microbial cell or reset in its descendants.

evidence.snippet: This is the first description of the restoration of a senescent defect by microinjection of young cytoplasmic components into Paramecium.
evidence.notes: Haga and Karino 1986, PMID:3654779; scientific abstract, directly read in the MED record. Young-cell cytoplasm restored sexual activity in senescent cells (about 700 fissions); recovery persisted for up to 20 fissions. Division rate and fertility after self-conjugation did not improve. This supports endpoint-specific recovery in treated old cells, not whole-cell or permanent rejuvenation. Full methods and figures were unavailable.

evidence.snippet: As this convergence was now downwards, doubling times decreased with each generation.
evidence.notes: Proenca et al. 2018, PMID:30213942, PMC6137065; Results, Stable equilibria are connected by aging and rejuvenation (Sec6), directly checked in primary XML. Actual Figure 4d was visually inspected: new-daughter lineages from the old-cell equilibrium converge toward faster growth over successive generations. These doubling times are derived from elongation rates, not direct interdivision intervals. Recovery is in descendants, not the same old mother. The tested MG1655 conditions do not establish all-environment recovery or a universal damage mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Gametes (spores) generated by aged cells show the same replicative potential as gametes generated by young cells.
evidence.notes: Unal et al. 2011, PMID:21700873, PMC3923466; scientific abstract, directly checked in MED and an MIT-hosted author manuscript. Main text and Figure 1 support gamete replicative-potential reset. Figure 4 concerns the separate vegetative lifespan-extension experiment. Transient NDT80-dependent vegetative lifespan extension is a separate result and does not establish reversal of every aged-cell defect. Supplements and strain tables were not assessed. The retrieved PDF identifies the article but differs in size and checksum from MIT bitstream metadata; original deposited-byte identity remains unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The cloned immaturin gene induces sexual rejuvenation in both mature and senescent cells by microinjection.
evidence.notes: Haga 2023, PMID:36677375, PMC9865852; scientific abstract, directly checked in primary XML and PMC text. Results 3.1 uses rejuvenation for suppression of mating in mature cells: that maturation-state reset alone is outside this functional trait. Results 3.2 reports recovery of old-cell mating activity after transformation. Figure 6C measures total cell counts over four days, not direct division times, and lacks a young-cell growth comparator. Engineered treatment is not a natural canonical taxon example; inferred chemistry is not a proven mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Some cells rejuvenated immediately, even after extended starvation, but others only restarted growth after a delay or not at all.
evidence.notes: Cesar et al. 2022, PMID:35243217, PMC8858994; scientific abstract, directly checked against MED and primary XML. Boundary evidence: culture duration during stationary phase is not individual replicative age. Immediate regrowth can reflect preserved function, not recovery from a demonstrated deficit. Regrowth classes use area-derived growth rates; nongrowth during the observation window is not proof of irreversible death. Results 2.1 and 2.3, Discussion, limitations and classification methods were read; figures and raw data were not independently assessed.

discussions.prompt: Assess the functional qualifier and distinguish same-cell recovery from descendant reset.
discussions.rationale: Require an age-linked deficit and a measured recovery or replicative-potential reset, retaining the endpoint, age axis, comparison group, treated unit, conditions and persistence. Recovery of one function need not restore all functions, be permanent or extend lifespan. Descendant recovery must not be reported as repair of the old mother. Marker changes, lifespan extension alone, prevention without prior loss and sexual immaturity alone are insufficient. Bare cellular rejuvenation has broader source usages and is not an exact synonym. Autogamy, gametogenesis and dormancy exit are not themselves this phenotype; neither is replicative aging with functional decline. Culture age is not interchangeable with lineage age. METPO:1000059 phenotype is a conservative parent, with no reparenting of existing records or asserted external equivalence.

discussions.prompt: Resolve strain provenance and endpoint-specific mechanisms before adding examples or causal edges.
discussions.rationale: This is a reusable physiological outcome, not a gene, protein, sequence feature or intervention. No canonical example or protein-resolved graph is asserted pending strain provenance and mechanistic review. Bacterial model-derived damage and fluorescent aggregates are not direct proof of a universal rejuvenation chemistry. Studies need not share a mechanism. The 2011 PDF/metadata byte mismatch is retained, not explained away by its added cover. MED/Crossref notice fields and accessible primary pages were checked on 2026-10-12; incomplete publisher access prevents an exhaustive notice-absence claim. Ignored/hidden local and pending-source searches plus pinned and current released METPO found no exact term in the inspected scope. No ontology upgrade or discovery-exhaustion claim follows.

Under the PATHWAY-vs-BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS rule, one node_id means one thing corpus-wide (issue 356): fermentation is typed BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS. label: chemokinesis
definition: A motile phenotype in which swimming speed changes in response to chemical concentration, without requiring directional bias along a chemical gradient.

evidence.snippet: chemokinesis is the ability to change swimming speed in response to a change in chemical concentration.
evidence.notes: Discussion, page 1005, visually checked in the author-hosted published PDF at https://stockerlab.ethz.ch/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/49.-Garren_etal_ISME_2014.pdf. This bacterial usage defines chemokinesis by speed, in contrast to chemotactic directional bias. The two responses can coexist. This citation supports identity; no independent reanalysis of its supplementary assays is claimed.

evidence.snippet: Chemokinesis was also observed in the absence of a chemical gradient
evidence.notes: SI Text, Chemokinesis, page 3 of 9; full article and SI inspected at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4978249/. Figure S5 and its caption were visually checked in the author PDF at https://stockerlab.ethz.ch/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/89._Son_atall.pdf (SI page 7 of 9). The uniform-serine assay supports a speed response without a gradient. Model block removals are in silico mutants, not biological gene deletions. YM4 cells were harvested in late exponential phase and resuspended in TMN motility medium, pH 7.5; Figure S5 uses uniform 5 micromolar serine at 600 mM sodium. YM4 is a laboratory mutant deficient in lateral flagella, as documented separately by DOI:10.7717/peerj.17126; it is retained as qualified experimental evidence, not a natural canonical example.

evidence.snippet: Thus, we hypothesize that the metabolism of mucus substrate stimulates Na+-NQR activity, which in turn enables sustained chemokinesis.
evidence.notes: Discussion, page 3677, visually checked at https://stockerlab.ethz.ch/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/141.-Cherry-Gao_Coral-Muscus.pdf. The plus is superscript in the typeset sodium notation and plain text in extraction. The following sentence requires experimental testing of this hypothesis. Transcript associations do not establish a causal protein pathway; no supplementary gene-level result is curated here.

evidence.snippet: two strains showing defects in the lateral flagellum (VIO5 and YM4)
evidence.notes: Abstract, PMID:38515459. This primary genomic study identifies YM4 as a laboratory strain with defective lateral flagellation. It supplies strain provenance, not a chemokinesis measurement. The Son observation must not be generalized to unperturbed Vibrio alginolyticus. Canonical examples are deferred pending separate verification of a natural exemplar (issue #1653).

discussions.prompt: Preserve the source-defined speed response and its distinction from taxis.
discussions.rationale: This record follows the swimming-speed usage in Garren, Son and Gao. Chemotaxis (traitmech:000086) concerns directional bias. No equivalence, disjointness or parent-child relation between them is asserted. A speed response can occur with or without chemotaxis and need not always be an increase. Existing research also uses chemokinesis more broadly for changes in turning frequency. Reconcile that broader usage, orthokinesis and klinokinesis before adding synonyms, narrower terms or xrefs; do not equate a turning-only response with this speed definition.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish observed behavior from model ablations and molecular hypotheses.
discussions.rationale: Son's computational removal of functional blocks is not a gene-knockout experiment. Gao's Na+-NQR explanation is explicitly hypothetical, with further experimental work requested. A mechanistic graph is deferred pending source-backed causal edges and eligible taxon-paired protein examples. Do not borrow the enterobacterial Che pathway from chemotaxis, infer causality from transcript changes, or use NONMECHANISTIC to bypass the protein-coverage requirement. No universal receptor is asserted.

Under the PATHWAY-vs-BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS rule, one node_id means one thing corpus-wide (issue 356): fermentation is typed BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS. PATHWAY is a named, conventionally enumerable multi-step route; BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS is everything else. A CLASS of routes rather than one route -- fermentation names a mode of energy conservation with many distinct implementations, so its steps cannot be enumerated without picking one. Was 3 BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS to 2 before this tranche. label: chemotropism
definition: A phenotype in which polarized growth is directionally biased in response to a spatial chemical gradient.

evidence.snippet: Notably, many hyphae changed direction near the boundary, opting to remain in the pH 6.5 layer (Fig 3B).
evidence.notes: Results, Chemotropism to low pH; exact span in Europe PMC full text PMC11288418 (PMID:39078817), published 2024-07-30. The compared layers are pH 6.5 and 8. Figure 3 was visually inspected: tip trajectories support directional growth, not only greater biomass. Main Results and the primary abstract describe lower-pH preference in these comparisons; the separate summary abstract's acidic-pH avoidance wording conflicts with them. Growth inhibition at pH 3 and carbon-source growth differences confound those comparisons. The nitrogen Results separately report negative chemotropism. S1 Table (10.1371/journal.pbio.3002726.s002), inspected as PDF text and image, lists engineered backgrounds including TH122; no natural canonical strain is inferred. Other supplements and movies were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: They respond to changes in their environment by directing hyphal growth towards or away from a range of chemical stimuli.
evidence.notes: Introduction, first paragraph; They refers to filamentous fungi. Exact span in Europe PMC full text PMC7329813 (PMID:32612109). This supports the polarity-neutral growth definition. The first Results subsection reports directional growth of Fusarium graminearum towards methionine, while rapid growth with other tested nitrogen compounds was not significantly directional. Table 1 identifies GZ-3639 as wild type, but natural provenance and an exact NCBI identity were not independently verified. Figures and supplements were not visually inspected. The paper's receptor and infection findings are not transferred into a universal chemotropism mechanism or canonical example.

discussions.prompt: Preserve direction, growth-rate and source-summary distinctions.
discussions.rationale: This class covers positive and negative chemical-gradient responses of polarized growth, not whole-cell locomotion. Use phenotype rather than motile as the parent. Neither increased biomass, faster extension nor asymmetric branching alone establishes directed growth. Keep chemotaxis, contact guidance and electric-field growth distinct. The Yamamoto summary abstract conflicts with the main Results on the pH-response direction; retain the inspected Results and Figure 3 context rather than silently harmonizing them. External equivalences and lexical variants require separate authority and scope checks.

discussions.prompt: Resolve natural strain provenance and accession-level mechanism evidence.
discussions.rationale: Keep laboratory-strain observations as qualified evidence. Verify natural provenance and NCBI identities before adding canonical examples; wild-type labels and no-auxotrophy controls do not establish an unengineered strain. The Aspergillus PmaA perturbation also affects growth and acid tolerance, so it does not isolate a dedicated chemical sensor. Inspect remaining figures and supplements and resolve taxon-paired protein accessions before adding a causal graph. Do not generalize stimulus-specific perturbations into a universal pathway or use a NONMECHANISTIC graph to bypass missing molecular evidence.

label: coccolith production
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell produces the calcitic cell-covering elements known as coccoliths.

evidence.snippet: Coccoliths are calcitic particles produced inside the cells of unicellular marine algae known as coccolithophores.
evidence.notes: Sviben et al. 2016, PMID:27075521, PMC4834641. Scientific Abstract and full article text directly read in Europe PMC XML on 2026-10-10; actual Figures 1 and 3 inspected. Calcium resupply to depleted AWI1516 cultures supports new calcite formation; imaging distinguishes forming coccoliths from a separate calcium-rich compartment. Its necessity, direct precursor identity and transfer route are not established. Figure 3's detector-panel caption repeats c in two pairs; no panel-specific detector assignment is imported. Other figures and supplements were not visually inspected. Historical Emiliania huxleyi is retained as the source name, not a current taxonomic or culture-collection phenotype assertion.

evidence.snippet: The continued production of malformed coccoliths could be observed on successive days
evidence.notes: Walker et al. 2018, PMID:29916209, PMC6175242, Results, time-lapse observations associated with Figure 8. Full article text and actual Figures 5 and 8 directly inspected on 2026-10-10; supplements and movies unread. This passage concerns Ge-treated Coccolithus braarudii PLY182g, not normal morphology. Production persists despite defective coccosphere integrity. Growth responses differ from the assayed E. huxleyi CCMP1516; neither growth dependence nor photosynthetic benefit is generalized. Preserve source discrepancies: Methods time-lapse stage 17 C versus Figure 5's 16 C; Methods/Results HEDP 50 micromolar versus Figure 1's 5 micromolar; Results low-Si threshold below 0.2 micromolar versus Discussion below 0.1. No unqualified quantitative claim depends on choosing between them.

discussions.prompt: Resolve broader biomineralization placement without conflating endpoints.
discussions.rationale: Use phenotype METPO:1000059 pending a source-backed broader biomineralization phenotype. Coccolith production is not mere possession, secretion or arrangement of preformed elements into a coccosphere. Defective elements still count as production; a complete covering is not required. It is not equivalent to generic calcification, urease-associated calcium carbonate precipitation, siliceous scale production, or magnetosome/ferrosome possession. The physiological trait is distinct from a material coccolith, its vesicle and a process-level ontology term. No exact synonyms, xrefs, common molecular pathway or organism-level disjointness are asserted.
discussions.resolution_note: Added biomineralization traitmech:000690 as the direct broader phenotype. Production of the mineral elements specified by this record entails mineral formation; this is a definition-based hierarchy inference, not a new child experiment. Phenotype METPO:1000059 remains an ancestor. The historical rationale and endpoint distinctions are preserved; the separate exemplar and mechanism gap remains OPEN. The v566 proposal requests the additional child axiom without rewriting the historical proposal cohort.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile assay strains, life stages and production-specific mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: No canonical examples are assigned pending joint strain-provenance and current-taxonomy verification. Skeffington et al., DOI:10.1111/jpy.12942, p. 239, explicitly derives calcifying AWI1516 from CCMP1516; this does not make all descendants equivalent. The current collection https://ncma.bigelow.org/CCMP1516, read 2026-10-10, labels it Gephyrocapsa huxleyi and reports lost coccolith production. Keep historical assay observations separate from this current catalog state; loss alone does not establish engineering. PLY182g provenance remains unresolved here. No universal silicon requirement, ploidy restriction, growth dependence or protective function is inferred. Separate mineral deposition, transport, secretion and covering integrity before adding causal edges. A protein mechanism needs direct functional evidence and taxon-paired accessions; sequence features alone are insufficient. Mechanism is deferred, not claimed absent.

label: contact-dependent outer membrane exchange
definition: A physiological phenotype in which microbial cells exchange outer-membrane lipids and proteins with other cells through direct intercellular contact.

evidence.snippet: transient contacts between two cells are sufficient to transfer OM materials, proteins and lipids, at high efficiency.
evidence.notes: PMID:23898400, PMC3721248. Scientific Abstract span directly read in Europe PMC XML, not the eLife digest. Selected Results s2-1 to s2-4 and Methods s4-1 to s4-4 were read; actual Figures 2 and 4 were visually inspected with their captions. Engineered Myxococcus xanthus DZ2 reporters and DiO assays distinguish OM material transfer from inner-membrane reporter exchange. Contact and traA controls support the observed endpoint. Dye continuity through some tubes does not establish significant protein transfer through them, which was not detected. Membrane fusion is the authors' mechanistic interpretation; not every contact transfers material. Videos and remaining supplementary panels were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: By use of a lipophilic fluorescent dye, we also discovered that OM lipids are exchanged.
evidence.notes: PMID:22511878, PMC3325183. Scientific Abstract directly read in Europe PMC XML; Results s2c/s2d and Methods s4a/s4e/s4f also read. Reporter and DiD experiments in M. xanthus support TraA/TraB dependence in donors and recipients under the tested surface-growth conditions. Liquid and nonmotile-pair controls limit inference from dye labeling alone. Similar domain architecture in mxan_4924 did not yield an overt transfer defect when disrupted; sequence resemblance is not sufficient phenotype evidence. Proposed adhesion, fusion and social roles are not all directly established by this study. Actual panels and strain-table provenance remain uninspected.

evidence.snippet: Thus, genetic and environmental conditions that promote OMT production are incongruent with OM exchange.
evidence.notes: PMID:24391054, PMC4011004. Scientific abstract directly retrieved through the Europe PMC core API. Full-text XML retrieval failed, so no full-text or panel verification is claimed. The abstract reports abundant OM tubes in traA/traB mutants and liquid conditions that do not permit transfer. Tube abundance alone is therefore insufficient for this trait; this does not negate the specific dye-conducting connections imaged in 2013. This paper shares investigators with the 2012 study and is not independent-laboratory replication.

evidence.snippet: Collectively, our results suggest that most mechanisms of interference competition and inter-colony kin discrimination in natural populations of myxobacteria do not require OME.
evidence.notes: PMID:31774841, PMC6880969. Scientific Abstract and Results sec012/sec014 directly read in Europe PMC XML. In the tested natural-isolate pairs, traA disruption or the A60 deletion did not remove colony-merger incompatibility. This is a boundary on ecological-function claims, not evidence that membrane exchange never occurs. The GJV1 control uses swarm inhibition as an inferred OME-dependent toxin readout, not direct fluorescent membrane transfer in every isolate. The directly read correction DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0228697 (PMID:31999808, PMC6991971) concerns Table 3 typesetting; no Table 3 numerical claim is used here. Actual panels were not visually inspected.

discussions.prompt: Keep membrane-component exchange distinct from its possible consequences.
discussions.rationale: The endpoint is contact-dependent exchange of outer-membrane material between cells. It is not cytoplasmic fusion, conjugative DNA transfer, all contact-dependent toxin delivery, or a generic secretion phenotype. Exocytosis traitmech:000637 concerns intracellular-compartment fusion-pore discharge; extracellular membrane vesicle production traitmech:000649 concerns extracellular particles. Neither is an exact parent. Cell-free vesicle transfer and slime-trail deposition do not alone demonstrate this contact-qualified class. The traits may coexist; no organism-level disjointness is asserted. Do not require equal bidirectional flux, transfer of every cargo at every contact, cooperation, killing, kin discrimination or fruiting-body development. Retain phenotype METPO:1000059 pending human hierarchy and external-mapping review; no unqualified exact synonym or external equivalence is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Ground strain-specific transfer machinery beyond sequence predictions.
discussions.rationale: TraA/TraB dependence and live material transfer are supported, but no accession-resolved universal fusogen pathway is asserted. Before adding causal graphs, resolve protein accessions, inspect remaining supplements and distinguish measured transfer, binding and fusion-model steps. PA14/MYXO-CTERM/OmpA-like sequence features or a traAB annotation alone do not establish the phenotype. Reporter-bearing and deletion strains remain qualified evidence, not unqualified natural exemplars. Natural provenance and direct positive transfer evidence must be paired before adding canonical examples; the 2019 negative kin-discrimination result cannot supply that positive anchor. These are outstanding grounding tasks, not a claim that no mechanism is known.

label: cue-triggered environmental anticipation
definition: A physiological phenotype in which exposure to an environmental cue induces changes that prepare a microorganism for a distinct, temporally associated environmental condition before that condition occurs.

evidence.snippet: early stimuli pre-induce genes that would be needed for later ones, yet later stimuli only induce genes needed to cope with them.
evidence.notes: Mitchell et al. 2009, PMID:19536156; scientific abstract, checked against publisher and source-qualified MED text. Main Figures 2-3 and supplementary Figures 3 and 6 were visually inspected, with their relevant Methods and control explanations. MG1655 sugar-switch assays distinguish early induction from subsequent growth; glycerol normalization and residual-sugar controls matter. Loss of the association in laboratory-evolved strains concerns selection across generations, not cognitive learning. Ecological explanations remain author interpretations. Not all raw data were reanalyzed.

evidence.snippet: Here, we identify a metabolic adaptation that is triggered upon entry into hypoxia-induced quiescence but facilitates subsequent cell cycle re-entry.
evidence.notes: Eoh et al. 2017, PMID:28530656, PMC5540153; scientific abstract, checked against publisher and source-qualified MED text. The abstract and qualitative main-text framing support metabolically encoded preparation, with hypoxia preceding re-aeration in the studied Mycobacterium tuberculosis system. This is not evidence for a universal transcriptional mechanism or an in-vivo demonstration of anticipation. Figures, supplements and raw data were not independently assessed; no molecular causal edges are asserted.

discussions.prompt: Retain cue-dependent preparation without conflating neighboring temporal-response traits.
discussions.rationale: The cue-triggered qualifier is deliberate: solely clock-driven preparation or constitutive readiness is insufficient. Evidence must link the preceding cue to preparation for a different later condition; correlated expression or cross-protection alone does not establish that interpretation. Generic stress response, stochastic bet hedging, carbon-source memory and diauxic growth are not exact synonyms, although particular observations can overlap. Neither cognition nor learning within an individual's lifetime is required; evolutionary regulatory wiring is compatible. No universal benefit, fixed delay, asymmetric response or single mechanism is required. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is locally framed as chronic copiotroph/oligotroph trophic adaptation, not this cue-to-future-condition phenotype. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream hierarchy review. This is an organismal disposition, not a sequence feature, regulatory site or precomposed chemical-use assertion.

discussions.prompt: Resolve assay-specific mechanisms, natural strain provenance and broader terminology before extending the record.
discussions.rationale: No canonical_examples, causal_graphs, exact synonyms or xrefs are asserted. The studies do not establish a uniform species-wide phenotype or a common protein mechanism; strain provenance and authority-resolved taxa require further review. Source-qualified MED, Crossref and visible publisher notice links were checked on 2026-10-12; their commentary/review links are not corrections or independent experiments. No correction or retraction was exposed for the two retained papers in these bounded checks. The separate Tagkopoulos 2008 lead (DOI:10.1126/science.1154456) is not counted evidence: its main PMC text was readable, but the indexed 9 June 2008 supplement correction could not be directly inspected. Broad environmental anticipation and adaptive prediction are not assumed exactly equivalent to this qualified class. No exact candidate was found in the pinned/current METPO RDF and ignored/hidden novelty searches; the pinned ontology remains unchanged.

label: cytogamy
definition: A sexual-reproduction phenotype in which a paired cell self-fertilizes by fusion of its own gametic nuclei without exchanging gametic nuclei with its partner.

evidence.snippet: Cytogamy is a process of internal self-fertilization in animals which appear to conjugate, but which in fact do not exchange nuclei
evidence.notes: Nobili and Luporini (1967), PMID:4964874, p.39 parenthetical before the Wichterman citation, checked in the typeset PDF. This directly read definition supports paired-cell internal self-fertilization without nuclear exchange. The surrounding Results and Table 2 offer cytogamy as an explanation for three mating-type outlier clones; they do not directly demonstrate cytogamy in those clones. The paper's primary experiments concern autogamy in Euplotes minuta. Do not count this terminology passage as independent experimental replication or turn its proposed explanation into a canonical taxon example. The cited 1940 original was not read beyond bibliographic metadata.

evidence.snippet: In fact, the conjugation process seems to be one of double autogamy (cytogamy), rather than of reciprocal gametic interchange.
evidence.notes: Diller (1958), scientific abstract directly read on the Wiley publisher page. The qualifier seems is retained. Paired Paramecium polycaryum cultures collected at Annamalainagar, South India, showed nuclear behavior resembling autogamy in singles. Breakdown of the paroral cones permitting micronuclear passage was not observed; this is not a genetic exclusion of exchange. The abstract also describes fertilization and postzygotic nuclear reorganization. Double autogamy is source-attributed terminology, not equivalence with our unpaired-cell autogamy class. Full text, actual figures and tables were not inspected; the tentative observation is not an unqualified canonical example.

evidence.snippet: cytogamy generates exconjugant clones that derive their entire genetic information from a single meiotic product of their cytoplasmic parent.
evidence.notes: Orias and Hamilton (1979), PMID:17248904, PMC1216858, scientific abstract clause after By analogy to Paramecium, directly checked in Europe PMC core metadata and NCBI PMC EFetch front-matter XML. The abstract reports hyperosmotic-shock-induced cytogamy in tested Tetrahymena thermophila strains and high fertility in most progeny. Its whole-genome-homozygote interpretation is source-specific, not a universal definition requirement or a genome-sequencing result established here. Other rare transmission abnormalities were not characterized in that abstract. The full text, Methods, actual figures and tables remain unread: PMC EFetch withholds body XML, and attempted public PDF retrieval did not yield a readable PDF. Strain provenance is unresolved; no natural canonical example or protein-level causal mechanism is inferred from this abstract.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish paired-cell self-fertilization from unpaired autogamy.
discussions.rationale: Pairing with internal gametic-nuclear fusion and no gametic-nuclear exchange distinguishes this class from ordinary conjugation with exchange and from operationally unpaired autogamy traitmech:000622. Diller (1958) calls the tentative observation double autogamy; preserve that broader source usage without silently making cytogamy a child or exact synonym of the unpaired class. This is not all selfing or a literal mating locus. No universal hyperosmotic trigger, whole-genome homozygosity, nuclear count or inability to outcross is imposed. Do not infer species-level disjointness between reproductive modes. The parent gap is resolved by automixis traitmech:000625, whose single-meiotic-cell nuclear origin includes this operational scope. The broader terminology and mapping questions keep this discussion OPEN. Verify external equivalences and synonym scope before adding mappings.

discussions.prompt: Resolve original cytology, strain provenance and molecular mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: The 1967 definitional passage is not a direct cytogamy experiment, the 1958 observation is tentative, and the 1979 evidence here is limited to its scientific abstract. Retrieve the original primary study DOI:10.1002/jmor.1050660303 (Wichterman, 1940) and the remaining experimental material before stronger cytological or natural-strain claims. That 1940 DOI is a metadata-verified research lead, not counted trait evidence. No canonical example is assigned from unresolved provenance or tentative marker explanations. Induced transmission outcomes do not identify a molecular causal pathway; graphs and protein accessions remain deferred. Retain actual snippet-resolver outcomes separately from direct source checks.

label: diatom frustule production
definition: A biomineralization phenotype in which a diatom forms the siliceous valve and girdle-band elements of its cell wall (frustule).

evidence.snippet: The basic stages of frustule morphogenesis characteristic of raphid pennate diatoms have been traced
evidence.notes: Bedoshvili et al., journal issue May 2018, online 2017-12-21, PMID:29270874. Scientific Abstract directly read at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29270874/ and in Europe PMC CORE on 2026-10-10 using EXT_ID:29270874 AND SRC:MED; exact ID, source, title and DOI checked together. The abstract defines frustule components as silica valves and girdle bands and reports microscopy of morphogenesis in Encyonema ventricosum under the source name. This supports formation, not just an isolated shell's presence. Cytoskeletal proximity is not functional necessity. Full text, Methods, actual figures and supplements were not inspected; no canonical taxon or universal membrane-release mechanism is inferred.

evidence.snippet: A diatom cell wall consists of two types of building blocks: two plate-shaped valves and several ring-shaped girdle bands.
evidence.notes: Aram et al. 2024, PMID:39251596, PMC11385223, Introduction. Scientific Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion and Methods directly read in official Europe PMC full-text XML on 2026-10-10; actual Figure 2 inspected, other actual figures and supplements unread. Source-qualified CORE lookup EXT_ID:39251596 AND SRC:MED confirmed ID, source, title and DOI. Silicon-starved CCMP1335 cultures were resupplied and imaged during valve formation. Figure 2 orders different cells by inferred maturation, not a live-cell time series. The paper retains historical Thalassiosira pseudonana naming while noting Cyclotella nana; this is not a current taxonomy assignment. Structural correlations support a membrane-mold hypothesis, not proven contact-site function or a universal molecular mechanism. The quote defines wall elements; the Results provide the production observations.

discussions.prompt: Keep frustule-element formation distinct from possession and other silica traits.
discussions.rationale: Use biomineralization traitmech:000690 as the broader phenotype because this endpoint entails formation of mineral cell-wall elements. It is not a material frustule, generic silicification, silica uptake, retention of an inherited valve or adsorption of preformed silica. Production of new wall elements does not require both valves to be synthesized anew in one cell cycle or every element to be formed simultaneously. Keep valve/girdle formation distinct from silica scales, auxospore coverings and setae; their observation alone does not establish this endpoint. The existing scale-production scope note distinguishes these phenotypes and is not an unresolved exact grounding. Do not infer organism-level disjointness or a universal geometry, cell-cycle schedule or fitness effect. Exact synonyms and external phenotype mappings remain unasserted pending authority review; process and material terms are not exact equivalents.

discussions.prompt: Resolve assay-strain provenance and production-specific causal evidence.
discussions.rationale: No canonical examples are assigned before reconciling study strains, collection provenance and current taxonomy. The two studies support wall-element formation but do not establish a conserved protein mechanism. The contact-site transport model and actin-associated expansion in Aram et al. remain proposals; unobserved vesicle fusion is not proof of its absence. Separate silica deposition, shaping, exocytosis and wall assembly when evaluating perturbation evidence. Functional evidence and taxon-paired accessions are required for protein edges; sequence features alone are insufficient. Mechanism is deferred, not claimed absent, and no universal intracellular route is imposed on all diatom silica structures.

label: diatom perizonium production
definition: A biomineralization phenotype in which a diatom produces the siliceous band system called the perizonium in an auxospore wall.

evidence.snippet: The deposition of the primary TP band became evident when the auxospore center attained a slim and rigid appearance.
evidence.notes: Kaczmarska et al. 2022, PMID:36067191, PMC9447881, Results: Epizonium and perizonium. TP means transverse perizonium. Scientific Abstract, Introduction, Methods, early Results, this subsection and Discussion: Auxospore structure and development read in official Europe PMC XML on 2026-10-10; actual Figure 11 inspected. Other actual figures and S1 Appendix unread. EXT_ID:36067191 AND SRC:MED confirmed ID, title, DOI and scientific abstract. Clone HK328 (= ECT3902) originated from Florida Bay material in 2011; atypical morphology and prolonged cultivation limit canonical assignment. PDMPO labels silica deposited after addition. SEM resolves inner TP/LP bands apart from initial valves; fixed images do not establish live kinetics. Authors leave some epizonium/perizonium layer boundaries uncertain.
