label: diauxic growth
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial population exhibits two successive growth phases associated with a switch from preferential use of one nutrient source to use of another as the first becomes limiting.

evidence.snippet: However, a significant fraction of cells maintains a high rate of elongation and displays no detectable growth lag during the shift.
evidence.notes: Boulineau et al. 2013, PMID:23637881, PMC3640066; scientific abstract. Introduction defines diauxic growth by sequential carbon-source use, supporting the definition's nutrient-switching differentia. Relevant Results, Discussion, Methods, actual Figure 2 and Text S1 prose were inspected. AB460 is an engineered MG1655 derivative; single-cell medium exchange is not the same assay as mixed-substrate batch growth. Population lag does not imply arrest of every cell. Contaminant-supported growth and model assumptions remain relevant. Text S1 DOC extraction loses embedded equations; no equation was visually verified or used as a curated mechanistic claim.

evidence.snippet: Azotobacter vinelandii exhibited diauxie when grown in a medium containing both acetate and glucose as carbon sources.
evidence.notes: George et al. 1985, PMID:3863813, PMC214331; directly retrieved source-qualified MED abstract only. Acetate preference in this experiment contradicts a universal glucose-first requirement and supports the lexical name diauxie. Full paper and figures were not inspected; a full-text XML endpoint returned HTTP 500. This access failure is not evidence that full text does not exist.

evidence.snippet: Following recovery of growth on the alternative carbon or nitrogen source, RpoS protein concentrations declined rapidly to a basal level.
evidence.notes: Sandercock and Page 2008, PMID:18055600, PMC2223558; scientific abstract. Relevant Methods/Results and actual Figure 3 support UW batch-culture acetate/glucose and ammonium/N2 transitions. This supports nutrient-source scope rather than sugars or carbon alone. Ammonium augmentation addresses an oxygen-limitation alternative for the stress response. RpoS dynamics are not a universal causal mechanism of diauxie; later PHB consumption was explicitly unmeasured. Publisher text and Figure 3 were accessible despite requests HTML 403 and Europe PMC XML 500 responses.

evidence.snippet: many natural isolates of Saccharomyces cerevisiae display short or nonexistent diauxic lags when grown in mixtures of glucose (preferred) and galactose.
evidence.notes: Wang et al. 2015, PMID:25626068, PMC4308108; scientific abstract, not the XML's preceding TOC teaser or separate Author Summary. Relevant Results, growth-curve Methods, actual Figure 1 and S1 EPS were inspected. Operational zero lag means the smoothed growth-rate curve has no local minimum, not simultaneous equal use of both substrates. Natural-origin growth panels and engineered reporter derivatives require separate provenance. Figure 1 caption says eleven strains but the image has twelve labels; no strain count is inferred here. The observations oppose mandatory positive lag.

evidence.snippet: Once glucose is depleted, the cells consume the earlier produced ethanol
evidence.notes: Zampar et al. 2013, PMID:23549479, PMC3693829; Introduction, second paragraph, not an abstract quote. Relevant Results, culture and measurement Methods and actual Figure 1 were inspected. FY4 was initially supplied glucose and later consumed produced ethanol; the definition therefore does not require both nutrients to be supplied initially. Figure 1 distinguishes concentration observations from fitted rates. Intracellular flux ranges are model-constrained, not direct flux measurements; raw supplemental data and the full mechanistic analysis were not reanalyzed.

discussions.prompt: Retain sequential nutrient use without imposing a universal lag or regulatory mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Boulineau's Introduction defines sequential carbon use, while lag-emphasizing accounts operationalize a narrower growth-curve pattern. Wang reports short or nonexistent lags; Sandercock and Page extend the observed scope to nitrogen-source transitions. The present definition uses the nutrient-switching sense and does not require glucose preference, a positive minimum lag, complete arrest of every cell or strictly zero secondary-substrate use. An arbitrary biphasic growth curve without nutrient-switching evidence is insufficient. Diauxic shift denotes the transition; polyauxie and unqualified diphasic growth are not exact synonyms. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is a trophic-type class whose local record operationalizes chronic copiotroph/oligotroph nutrient regimes, not this temporal pattern. Phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream hierarchy review. Generalist and specialist denote niche breadth; dormancy, carbon catabolite repression and generic resource-use predicates are not exact equivalents.

discussions.prompt: Ground conditional examples and taxon-specific mechanisms before adding canonical taxa or a graph.
discussions.rationale: The studies include laboratory strains and engineered reporter derivatives. No natural canonical example is asserted without primary strain provenance and authority-resolved taxon identity. No shared universal molecular mechanism or taxon-paired protein branch is established here. Gene presence, lac-locus annotation, RpoS expression or predicted flux alone cannot establish observed diauxic growth. It is conditional on culture and nutrients, not a fixed species identity or sequence-feature trait. Qualified MED and Crossref metadata for all five sources exposed no linked correction or retraction at the 2026-10-11 check; available primary pages were also inspected. This bounded check does not guarantee absence of notices; Wang's preprint link is not a correction. Canonical examples, causal graphs and external equivalences remain unasserted rather than being inferred from these observations.

label: diversifying bet hedging
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a clonal microbial lineage reversibly interconverts between alternative cell states independently of the prevailing environment and before environmental change, spreading risk across unpredictable environmental changes through state-specific survival or reproductive trade-offs.

evidence.snippet: Here we report the de novo evolution of bet hedging in experimental bacterial populations.
evidence.notes: Beaumont et al. 2009, PMID:19890329; scientific abstract, directly checked against publisher and source-qualified MED text, not the publisher's Editorial Summary. Supports experimentally evolved risk spreading by rapid phenotype switching under a changing selection regime. Mutational evolution of a switching genotype is not the same claim as mutations generating each alternative cell state. Main figures, supplements and raw data were not independently assessed; no gene-level mechanism or natural canonical exemplar is asserted.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that yeast bet hedging results from multiple epigenetic growth states determined by a combination of stochastic and deterministic factors.
evidence.notes: Levy, Ziv and Siegal 2012, PMID:22589700, PMC3348152; scientific abstract, directly checked against publisher, MED and full-text XML, separately from the Author Summary. Box 1 supplies the definition framework and explicitly leaves adaptive origin untested in this yeast study. The record preserves that limit: reversible state variation and differential stress survival do not alone establish evolutionary optimization. Binary states and a purely stochastic mechanism are not required.

evidence.snippet: Mobile cells grow faster but are stress-sensitive, while non-mobile cells prioritise stress resistance over growth.
evidence.notes: Tang et al. 2024, PMID:38453919; scientific abstract, directly checked against publisher and source-qualified MED text. The Introduction and Discussion distinguish early diversification of Haematococcus pluvialis cultures from later stress-induced conversion. Growth and survival are fitness proxies, not a demonstration of optimized long-term geometric mean fitness. Figures, supplements and raw data were not independently assessed; proposed transcriptional explanations are not encoded as causal edges.

discussions.prompt: Retain lineage-level risk spreading without equating all cellular heterogeneity with bet hedging.
discussions.rationale: The diversifying qualifier restricts this class to alternative states within a clonal microbial lineage; it does not cover every use of unqualified bet hedging. Heterogeneity, noisy gene expression or switching alone is insufficient: reversible states must precede the relevant environmental shift and differ in survival or reproductive performance across conditions. Generic stress-induced change, carbon-source memory, cue-triggered environmental anticipation, genetic resistance and ecological generalist/specialist niche breadth are not exact synonyms. Particular observations can overlap without making these classes equivalent or disjoint. Dormancy and persister formation can participate in risk spreading, but their presence alone does not establish it, so neither existing record is reparented. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream review of this lineage-level physiological disposition. This is not a sequence feature, individual assay result or mixed-species community property. Following Levy et al. Box 1, the relevant state interconversion must be independent of the prevailing environment; temporal precedence alone does not establish this criterion. Cue-triggered preparation before a later change is not sufficient. Deterministic age-related variation can qualify, so environmental independence does not require a purely stochastic switching mechanism.

discussions.prompt: Assess adaptive origin, natural exemplars and molecular mechanisms separately from the operational phenotype.
discussions.rationale: This first-pass class does not assert that every cited system was selected for diversification or has a measured long-term fitness advantage. Levy et al. Box 1 distinguishes those stronger claims from its operational usage; testing arithmetic and geometric mean fitness requires an explicit environmental distribution and comparison strategy. No fixed switching rate, binary state space or universal protein mechanism is asserted. Canonical taxa await strain-provenance and taxonomy checks; causal_graphs, xrefs and synonyms are omitted. MED, Crossref and visible publisher links checked on 2026-10-12 exposed no correction or retraction for the three retained papers; commentary, review and preprint links are not independent experiments. This bounded check does not exclude every possible notice. Pinned/current METPO RDF and ignored/hidden novelty searches found no exact active or deprecated term; earlier research mentions remain leads, not primary records. The pinned ontology is unchanged.

label: dormancy
definition: A reversible physiological state of greatly reduced metabolic activity that allows a cell to survive unfavorable conditions and later resuscitate, generating a microbial seed bank.

evidence.notes: Lennon & Jones review microbial seed banks and the mechanisms by which microorganisms enter and exit dormancy; parent of VBNC and persister sub-variants.
Lewis links dormancy to persister-cell survival and infectious disease.

canonical_examples.note: Paradigm of bacterial dormancy/non-replicating persistence (latent infection; DosR regulon).
Strain-level dormancy model paired to reviewed RpfB, one member of the resuscitation-promoting-factor family.

causal_graphs.title: Reversible dormancy and resuscitation
causal_graphs.description: Evidence-backed causal sketch linking unfavorable conditions to a reversible dormant state forming a microbial seed bank.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This graph combines several bacterial dormancy modules rather than asserting one universal pathway. The H37Rv RpfB example anchors the resuscitation branch and is one Rpf-family protein, not a stand-in for toxin-antitoxin or ribosome-hibernation systems.

label: durotaxis
definition: A motile phenotype in which active migration is directionally biased in response to a spatial gradient in substrate stiffness.

evidence.snippet: Dictyostelium also displayed stiff-side directed motility when seeded on the gradient gel
evidence.notes: Kang et al., Version of Record (v4), 2024-12-13, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.96821.4; full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11643633/ (PMID:39671466). Exact Results paragraph span in Amoeboid durotaxis is evolutionarily conserved, not an abstract quote. Figure 4 was visually inspected: confined Dictyostelium cells on polyacrylamide stiffness gradients had greater directional migration than uniform-gel controls, without a significant velocity difference. Blebbistatin reduced directionality and speed; Rho activator II increased them. These pharmacological results do not isolate a dedicated stiffness sensor. Supplementary file 1 contains simulation parameters; the MDAR checklist refers to cell-culture methods but does not resolve the assayed Dictyostelium strain. Mammalian NMIIA localization and knockdown results are not direct microbial protein evidence.

evidence.snippet: Our findings reveal directional persistence and strong polarization of the plasmodia towards regions of stiffer substrates, indicating a guided migration response.
evidence.notes: Filipinas and Confesor, published online 2025-02-27. Exact abstract span in the publisher-deposited Crossref record, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1088/1361-6463/adb6b8. The authors report tracking Physarum polycephalum plasmodial nodes on agar stiffness gradients. This is independent microbial support for stiffness-directed migration, not merely a simulation prediction. Full methods, figures and supplements were not inspected; strain provenance, gradient controls and the distinction between node migration and growth remain to be assessed before adding a canonical example or mechanistic graph. The abstract's simulation-supported gradient-independence claim is not generalized to all microbes.

evidence.snippet: Our results identify the molecular mechanism driving context-dependent positive or negative durotaxis, determined by a cell's contractile and adhesive machinery.
evidence.notes: Isomursu et al., published 2022-07-11, PMID:35817964. Exact final abstract sentence in the Europe PMC MED record, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/35817964; the publisher's abstract corroborates positive and negative durotaxis usage. This mammalian cell study supports polarity-neutral terminology only, not an additional microbial observation. Its mechanism claim is not transferred to microbes. Full methods, figures and supplements were not inspected for this terminology check. The two microbial studies above report stiff-side migration; negative microbial durotaxis is not established by these sources.

discussions.prompt: Keep stiffness-directed migration distinct from other mechanical responses.
discussions.rationale: The class is polarity-neutral: positive and negative responses are directions along the stiffness gradient, not different stimuli. Isomursu et al. (DOI:10.1038/s41563-022-01294-2) support this terminology in mammalian cells, not negative microbial durotaxis. Both microbial studies here report stiff-side migration; no opposite microbial response is inferred. Speed changes on uniform substrates, passive displacement and differential growth alone are insufficient. Contact-guided polarized growth in thigmotropism (traitmech:000594) is a different response. Do not infer durotaxis from a friction gradient, surface topography or remote substrate deformation without direct evidence for stiffness-directed migration. Mechanotaxis is broader, not an exact synonym. QuickGO returned zero durotaxis hits on 2026-10-04; other external equivalences remain unverified. No xref or synonym is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Resolve experimental strains and microbial protein evidence before graphing.
discussions.rationale: Kang's methods cite Li et al. (DOI:10.3389/fcell.2022.835185), whose cell-culture methods describe Ax2-derived cells and expression constructs. That citation does not uniquely identify the cells used for Kang's Figure 4 or establish natural-strain provenance. Resolve that identity and inspect the Physarum full methods before adding NCBI-grounded canonical examples. Dictyostelium inhibitor/activator responses support a contractility-related interpretation, not a resolved protein-level sensing pathway. Do not transfer mammalian NMIIA polarization or knockdown effects to an unverified microbial accession, or treat the active gel model as a biological perturbation. Mechanistic graphs are deferred pending taxon-paired proteins and bounded causal evidence; NONMECHANISTIC is not a workaround.

label: endocytosis
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell takes up extracellular material or plasma-membrane components into intracellular membrane-bound compartments by remodeling and internalizing its plasma membrane.

evidence.snippet: After an additional 20-40 min, the PM and cytoplasmic punctate staining disappeared concomitant with staining of the vacuolar membrane.
evidence.notes: PMID:7533169, PMC2120394. Scientific Abstract quote verified in Europe PMC XML; full-text OCR, including Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, was read at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC2120394/fullTextXML. FM 4-64 tracks plasma-membrane-to-vacuole transport in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Early experiments used BHY10.5, a CPY-invertase reporter background, not the SEY6210 control in later mutant comparisons. Endosome identity is qualified as likely. Mutant effects on vacuolar delivery are not necessarily initial-internalization defects; in vitro ATP/cytosol dependence concerns later transport. Marker-specific results do not establish a universal route. PDF/figures were unavailable and were not visually audited.

evidence.snippet: This report presents direct evidence for alpha-factor-induced internalization of cell surface receptors.
evidence.notes: PMID:7935439, PMC359259. Scientific Abstract directly read in NCBI PubMed XML and Europe PMC metadata, which agree on this DOI. Density fractionation and extracellular-protease protection support receptor internalization in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The abstract distinguishes receptor signaling, internalization and subsequent vacuolar degradation. No fixed transit time or universal receptor requirement is imposed. Full text and figures were unavailable: the Europe PMC full-text endpoint returned HTTP 500 and the indexed PDF mirror returned 404. Strain provenance and unread assay details are not inferred.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish membrane-bound uptake from neighboring capabilities.
discussions.rationale: This is the microbial cell's uptake phenotype, not a host response, a sequence feature or intracellular trafficking alone. Surface adsorption, passive diffusion, transporter entry, open membrane invaginations and autophagy alone are insufficient. Pinocytosis traitmech:000635 and phagocytosis traitmech:000627 entail this scope; macropinocytosis traitmech:000634 remains below pinocytosis. No fixed size, clathrin/actin dependence, nutritional assimilation or degradation is required. Trogocytosis traitmech:000633 describes removal and uptake of living-cell portions without universally specifying membrane-bound enclosure. Myzocytosis traitmech:000631 describes prey-content aspiration. Its cited 2023 Discussion (DOI:10.3390/microorganisms11081945) calls myzocytosis a form of endocytosis in the studied Colpodella system; that source-attributed umbrella usage is retained, not treated as proof that every aspiration phenotype meets this operational membrane-bound scope. Their broader parent decisions remain unresolved, not exclusions or disjointness claims. Nutritional phagotrophy is not an equivalent. Review process-level ontology mappings separately; no unverified synonyms or xrefs are asserted.

No complete molecular mechanism, protein accessions or causal graph are inferred from tracer behavior or abstracts. Obtain taxon-paired functional and strain-provenance evidence before adding those fields.

label: energy taxis
definition: A motile phenotype in which directional locomotion is regulated by sensing changes in the electron transport system associated with cellular energy generation.

evidence.snippet: behavioral responses to most stimuli in A. brasilense are triggered by changes in the electron transport system.
evidence.notes: Abstract exact-matched at Europe PMC (PMID:11029423). Publisher Methods, Results and Discussion also inspected. label: enhanced transcriptional reactivation memory
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell or lineage retains a non-genetic state from prior inducing conditions that enhances the rate or magnitude of later transcriptional activation after intervening repression.

evidence.snippet: Upon Anchor Away of Opi1, reactivation was faster than activation
evidence.notes: Sump et al. 2022, PMID:35579426, PMC9129879; Results s2-1, paragraph 2, contiguous in primary XML and publisher Version of Record HTML. Figure 1D uses synthetic Opi1 Anchor Away to bypass upstream induction control; enhancement is lost in mrs and nup100 mutants. Ordinary-starvation INO1 reactivation in Figure 1B is not clearly faster than activation. Figure 1 supplement 1C separately measures CHO1/ACT1 after three-hour repression; its generic statistical-comparator caption is ambiguous. Figure 1 supplement 2E measures 18-hour peripheral localization, not that duration of enhanced transcription; the main Results mispoints to supplement 1. Figure 1G competitive fitness is a different endpoint, not proof of transcriptional causality. Selected Results, Methods, scientific abstract, actual figures and strain-table rows were inspected. RT-qPCR mRNA kinetics are not direct measurements of initiation rate. Native abstract lookup returns NOT_IN_ABSTRACT; direct full-text matching supports the quotation, not a native VERIFIED verdict.

evidence.snippet: Cells with prior NaCl exposure have a faster gene-expression response to H2O2.
evidence.notes: Guan et al. 2012, PMID:22851651, PMC3454879; complete opening sentence of the Figure 4 caption, contiguous in publisher HTML with chemical subscripts retained as text. BY4741-background laboratory yeast received 0.7 M NaCl for 60 minutes, washing and 240 minutes of stress-free YPD recovery (two generations in Results), then 0.5 mM H2O2, compared with mock-treated cells. No significant pre-challenge expression difference at FDR 0.05 does not prove identical baselines. Figure 4 includes induced and repressed genes; only the enhanced-induction subset supports this activation phenotype. The 449-gene count is not a count of induced genes. Methods and Figure 4A sample through 40 minutes, whereas Results describes a 60-minute response. Figure 5 shows TSA2 mRNA kinetics by qPCR; nup42 deletion reduces the priming benefit, while nup100 naive and primed responses are both fast, not simple evidence of a universal mechanism. Four-to-five generation resistance persistence is a different endpoint. Relevant Results, Methods, scientific abstract and actual Figures 4 and 5 were inspected; raw data were not reanalyzed. Native abstract-verifier results are retained separately in the source sidecar; exact publisher full-text matching supports this caption quotation.

discussions.prompt: Preserve enhanced reactivation after repression as the defining endpoint.
discussions.rationale: Compare induced transcript responses under matched later test conditions and genetic backgrounds, after intervening repression. Continued expression, transcript or reporter persistence, a chromatin mark, peripheral localization or a gene alone does not establish this phenotype. Transcript abundance does not by itself distinguish synthesis from degradation. No identical first and second stimulus, prior production of a particular transcript, fixed duration, universal mitotic inheritance or shared chromatin mechanism is required. Carbon-source memory (traitmech:000706) spans growth and induction endpoints and is not reparented wholesale. Memory of acquired stress resistance (traitmech:000712) concerns retained resistance, not faster transcription. Anticipation and bet hedging are also not exact equivalents. Unqualified transcriptional memory, epigenetic memory and priming are not asserted as exact synonyms. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending hierarchy review; existing records are unchanged.

label: ER-phagy
definition: An autophagy phenotype in which a microbial cell selectively degrades portions of its endoplasmic reticulum by delivering them to lysosomal or vacuolar compartments.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we provide evidence that ER-phagy degrades excess ER membrane, suggesting that it contributes to cell homeostasis by controlling organelle size.
evidence.notes: PMID:25052096, PMC4163648. Scientific Abstract directly read in Europe PMC core metadata with matching DOI. XML Results s2c/s2e and Methods s4b/s4f were read. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ER-targeted Pho8 reporters distinguish selective turnover from cytosolic and mitochondrial cargo; Atg7 and vacuolar-protease controls distinguish routes and reporter activation. ER whorls enter the vacuole by microautophagy. DTT and tunicamycin interfere with vacuolar proteolysis, so stress-induced whorl accumulation alone is not completed degradation. Untreated opi1 mutants show partly disintegrated vacuolar whorls, unlike opi1 pep4 prb1 mutants; membrane expansion can elicit this response without misfolded-protein stress. The strains derive from W303, but independent natural provenance was not verified. Figure 5/7 captions were read; actual figures, supplements and complete Methods were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: Atg40 is enriched in the cortical and cytoplasmic ER, and loads these ER subdomains into autophagosomes.
evidence.notes: PMID:26040717. Scientific Abstract directly read in Europe PMC core metadata with matching DOI. This Saccharomyces cerevisiae study explicitly restricts its use of autophagy to macroautophagy. Atg40 targets cortical/cytoplasmic ER, whereas Atg39 targets perinuclear ER and nuclear material. These source-specific subdomain assignments do not make ER-phagy and nucleophagy synonyms or restrict all ER-phagy to the macro route. The proposed mammalian FAM134B functional counterpart is qualified as probable, not experimentally universal. Full text, actual figures, supplements and strain provenance were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: Third, we demonstrate that macro- and micro-ER-phagy are parallel pathways with distinct molecular requirements.
evidence.notes: PMID:31802527, PMC6960443. Scientific Abstract directly read in Europe PMC core metadata with matching DOI. XML Results embj2019102586-sec-0005 and Methods sec-0011/sec-0018/sec-0019 were read. This yeast study explicitly includes macro- and microautophagic ER turnover. Their contributions depend on the trigger; do not universalize measured proportions. Nem1-Spo7 and ESCRTs contribute to micro-ER-phagy, but ESCRT mutants also impair nonselective autophagy and vacuolar function, so their defects are not micro-ER-phagy-specific absence tests. Atg40 is dispensable for the Atg7-independent micro route. Pho8 assays require background correction; the Sec63-GFP assay quantifies Pep4-dependent, Atg7-independent cleavage products using unsaturated exposures. Uptake or membrane scission alone does not prove complete degradation. Actual figures, supplements, complete Methods and independent strain provenance were not inspected.

discussions.prompt: Review route-inclusive scope and cargo-selective degradative flux.
discussions.rationale: Use autophagy traitmech:000638 as parent. The 2014 microautophagy study and the 2019 online/2020 issue ESCRT paper support a route-inclusive phenotype, whereas Mochida et al. 2015 use autophagy specifically for macroautophagy. GO:0061709 reticulophagy, resolved at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/GO%3A0061709, is a nonobsolete biological process whose definition specifies autophagosomes and whose exact synonyms include ER-phagy. That route restriction and the process-to-phenotype shift prevent an exact xref here; retain the source-attributed difference for human review without silently narrowing the microbial phenotype. No synonyms or SSSOM mapping are asserted. ER stress, unfolded-protein responses, ER-associated protein degradation outside the lysosome/vacuole, bulk cytoplasmic turnover, gene presence, puncta or accumulated whorls alone are insufficient. Nuclear-envelope cargo can overlap nucleophagy without making the two traits equivalent.

discussions.prompt: Resolve natural exemplars and route-specific protein mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Canonical examples remain unset because natural strain provenance has not been independently verified for the laboratory reporter and perturbation strains. Do not infer natural or engineered origin from a mutant label. The yeast doing the degradation carries this phenotype; a bacterium eliciting an animal-host response does not. Resolve native taxon-paired protein accessions and direct functional evidence before adding a causal graph. Neither Atg39/Atg40 nor Nem1-Spo7/ESCRT dependence is an unconditional definition of ER-phagy across all routes and microbial taxa. Keep reduced rates, residual turnover and complete absence distinct, and do not equate impaired vacuolar function with selective loss of this phenotype.

label: eukaryotic flagellar autotomy
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial eukaryote sheds its cilia or flagella by regulated severing of their axonemes near the base.

evidence.snippet: fla10 cells lose flagella by deflagellation at 33 degrees C.
evidence.notes: Parker and Quarmby 2003, PMID:12930563, PMCID:PMC194436, scientific abstract Results, second sentence. Direct MED text match; native VERIFIED applies to that text, not the PDF degree-symbol typography. Background distinguishes basal axonemal severing from resorption. The quoted response concerns source-named Chlamydomonas fla10 in calcium-containing medium, not reference strain WTB214. Released flagella were counted per 100 cells, with the initial count subtracted; lengths are a separate endpoint. Low calcium is not calcium-free, and buffer exchange is a confound. All twelve main PDF pages and eight figures were inspected. No universal IFT or calcium requirement follows.

evidence.snippet: Wild-type cells deflagellate completely in response to pH shock or dibucaine, regardless of the temperature
evidence.notes: Hilton et al. 2016, PMID:27520959, PMCID:PMC5068960.1, page 3416, Results and Discussion subsection ADF2 and ADF4 remain unassigned, first paragraph and Figure 4A. Contiguous JATS and typeset match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The comparison is 21 versus 33 degrees C after six hours, not every temperature. The assay scores the control-normalized decrease in biflagellate cells per 100 cells, not a direct count of released flagella or proof that every responding cell loses both. Figure 4A reports three independent experiments with SD. All ten main pages, four figures and three tables were inspected; supplements remain unread. Phototaxis screening alone is not the shedding endpoint.

discussions.prompt: Review the basal axonemal shedding endpoint and its phenotype parent.
discussions.rationale: This organism-level phenotype concerns regulated release of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum, not possession, arrangement, assembly failure or nonmotility. Resorption, retained-organelle disassembly, passive breakage, distal vesicle release and premitotic basal-body release alone do not establish the endpoint. Bacterial flagellar ejection or resorption involves a different apparatus and is outside this qualified class. The phenotype parent METPO:1000059 is a definition-based inference; motility is not a required parent. Palmelloid formation traitmech:000654 does not require flagellar loss. No exact synonyms, organism-level disjointness or universal stimulus threshold are asserted.

discussions.prompt: Review current ontology scope without reviving obsolete morphology identifiers.
discussions.rationale: The inspected pinned and current METPO release/editor/template scope has no active exact shedding class. Historical METPO:0000089 and METPO:000090 are deprecated with OMO:0001000; METPO:1000381 is deprecated with IAO:0000226. All point to METPO:1000704, which denotes locomotory flagellar possession, not autotomy. Deprecated ciliated METPO:0000093 and METPO:000094 carry OMO:0001000, while METPO:1000385 carries IAO:0000226; no replacement or consider annotation was observed for these or deprecated flagellum METPO:1000123, whose recorded reason is OMO:0001000. Those historical morphology terms are not exact xrefs and are not reactivated. METPO issue https://github.com/berkeleybop/metpo/issues/521 records unresolved reason-code interpretation. Current upstream describes a bacterial/archaeal focus, so adoption of this microbial-eukaryote proposal requires maintainer review. The ontology pin stays unchanged. Proposal v607 reserves METPO:1068400 within 1068400-1068499; no upstream release or human sign-off is implied.

discussions.rationale: A protein-resolved graph requires taxon-paired authority-checked accessions and edge-specific experiments. Domain, motif, gene or mutant names alone do not establish the organismal phenotype. The p60 study constrains a proposed universal severing mechanism; it does not establish dispensability of every katanin function. No universal FA1, FA2, TRP15, IFT or calcium requirement is asserted. Mechanisms are deferred, not claimed absent.

label: eukaryotic flagellar axoneme internalization
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial eukaryote internalizes the intact axoneme of its own cilium or flagellum into its cell body.

evidence.snippet: axonemes remain intact during internalization
evidence.notes: Venard et al. 2020, PMID:33103844, PMCID:PMC7944584, Results 2.2, TEM interpretation paragraph following Figure 2. Contiguous span checked in direct PMC HTML; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. Live phase microscopy, fixed immunofluorescence and TEM concern Rhizoclosmatium globosum JEL800 and Spizellomyces punctatus DAOM BR117. Internalized cross-sections retain 9+2 architecture without a surrounding ciliary membrane; fixed TEM is not continuous same-cell tracking. Figure 1's 23 and 32 cells are selected retraction events, not biological-culture counts. Methods time zero is plating, whereas Figure 2's TEM caption says post-retraction; retain that timing discrepancy. Table 1 labels length/diameter with rate units unlike Table 2; no numerical conversion or rate is asserted here. Main text and all five actual main figures were inspected. The main PDF and actual supplemental PDFs/videos remain unread. Subsequent degradation is a separate phase, not a requirement for this internalization phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Bd zoospores retracting their flagella by coiling the entire axoneme into the cell body
evidence.notes: Fritz-Laylin et al. 2017, PMID:28473602, PMCID:PMC5461030.1, Discussion JATS s11, printed page 1681, PDF page 9. Direct normalized JATS and typeset passage checked; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. Bd denotes Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis, source strain JEL423, with synchronized zoospores observed under the described confinement preparation. Results s10, Discussion s11 and Methods s20 were read, along with selected PDF pages. Video 5 was inspected through 16 sampled frames and one enlarged frame, not continuous playback or every-frame analysis. File metadata reports 10.1 seconds at nominal 10 fps, burned-in labels span 0-20 seconds, and the caption states 0.1-second acquisition with 20-fps playback. These are not silently reconciled; no retraction rate or replicate count is inferred. The paper's WASP/SCAR pseudopod experiments do not establish an axoneme-internalization mechanism.

discussions.prompt: Review intact withdrawal separately from later axonemal disassembly.
discussions.rationale: The defining endpoint is internalization of the cell's own intact eukaryotic axoneme. Static internal localization, uptake of another cell's material, external coiling, failed assembly, motor arrest, passive breakage or shedding alone do not establish it. Venard et al. 2020 place internalization within a broader cilium-disassembly program while distinguishing subsequent degradation. The operational resorption record traitmech:000733 requires shortening through axonemal disassembly, not intact withdrawal alone. Later degradation can occur after internalization; no organism-level disjointness or permanently intact internal axoneme is asserted. Autotomy traitmech:000731 and bacterial polar flagellar ejection traitmech:000732 have different endpoints; bacterial periplasmic flagella and type IV pili are different structures. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is a definition-based parent inference, without a locomotion requirement.

Figure 4's caption gives about 4.5-fold expansion, versus 5.5 +/- 0.2 in Results S6 (Supplemental Figure S3A-B); no absolute-size conversion is inferred. Figure 4F counts 16, 3, 26 and 41 sporangia across categories from three to five independent experiments, not retraction events. The two-hour timeline is attributed to 2020, not a new measurement. Other actual main figures, the main PDF and other supplement pages were not visually inspected. The preprint is another version, not another study.

label: eukaryotic flagellar resorption
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial eukaryote shortens previously assembled cilia or flagella through disassembly of their axonemes.

evidence.snippet: Cells under resorption-inducing conditions rapidly shortened their flagella
evidence.notes: L'Hernault and Rosenbaum 1985, PMID:3968171, PMCID:PMC2113451.1, printed page 458, Results, Monitoring of Flagellar Length during In Vivo Labeling, sole paragraph; Figure 2 on page 459. Contiguous typeset and whitespace-normalized OCR match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The XML body is a single OCR preformat block, not a section-structured JATS paragraph. Source-designated wild-type Chlamydomonas reinhardtii 21gr was mechanically deflagellated and pulse-chase labelled during regeneration before resorption was induced with 15 mM sodium pyrophosphate at pH 7.5 plus cycloheximide; HEPES was the control. The shortening concerns regenerated flagella, not failed assembly. Apparent flagellalessness after 90 minutes still permits the reported short stubs. Protein fractionation supports transfer to the cell body, not complete recycling. All six main PDF pages, three figures and Table I were inspected; raw data were not reanalyzed. Figure 1's two determinations and Table I's two gels per sample are not established biological-replicate counts.

evidence.snippet: Acid shock causes resorption of mutants unable to deflagellate.
evidence.notes: Parker and Quarmby 2003, PMID:12930563, PMCID:PMC194436, Figure 7 caption, first sentence, page 9 of 12; JATS F7 under sec9/sec5. Direct caption and typeset match; native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT retained. The acid-shock experiments concern Chlamydomonas fa1, fa2 and adf1 mutants, with coiling and incomplete resorption described; wild-type cells instead shed and regrow their flagella in this comparison. Figure 7 scores the fraction of cells with flagella longer than 7 micrometers, not a resorption rate or count of released organelles. The separate fla10 temperature experiments must not be merged with this assay. Low-calcium HEPES is not calcium-free: Methods retain trace calcium and do not add chelators. The main length measurements count at least 70 cells per time point and use at least three independent cultures. All twelve main PDF pages and eight figures were inspected. Proposed basal disassembly and shared severing machinery are not universal requirements of this class.

discussions.prompt: Review shortening through disassembly without requiring complete disappearance.
discussions.rationale: This physiological phenotype concerns shortening of a previously assembled eukaryotic axoneme. Static short flagella, failed assembly, nonmotility, bending or coiling, passive breakage, or shedding a largely intact organelle alone do not establish it. Neither complete structural disappearance nor complete protein recycling is required. Basal severing and residual transition zones can accompany resorption; the class does not require an intact base or the absence of severing. Eukaryotic flagellar autotomy traitmech:000731 and bacterial polar flagellar ejection traitmech:000732 have different endpoints. Bacterial periplasmic resorption involves a different apparatus. No organism-level disjointness is asserted. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is the definition-based parent; locomotion is not required. Palmelloid formation traitmech:000654 does not require flagellar loss.

evidence.reference_title: Centrioles are freed from cilia by severing prior to mitosis.
evidence.snippet: resorbing flagella of Chlamydomonas leave remnants associated with the mother cell wall.
evidence.explanation: Supports the remnant/scope limitation, not an additional definition citation, a universal severing mechanism or complete recycling.
evidence.notes: Parker et al. 2010, PMID:20506243, PMCID:PMC2897710.1, scientific abstract, JATS paragraph P2, third sentence. Direct JATS and MED scientific-abstract matches; native VERIFIED retained. Main text, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions and three captions were read, not the actual figures, PDF, supplementary video, supplementary legend or raw data. Live pf6 CC1029 observations and wild-type 137c mt- CC124 electron microscopy concern different preparations. Paired spots in daughter-cell clusters are not a flagellar-resorption rate. Remnants may remain in the wall or be expelled; do not universalize this premitotic context to every resorption stimulus.

discussions.prompt: Review microbial-eukaryote scope without reviving obsolete morphology identifiers.
discussions.rationale: The inspected pinned/current METPO releases, editor and templates have no active exact resorption class. Historical METPO:0000089 and METPO:000090 carry OMO:0001000; METPO:1000381 carries IAO:0000226. All are deprecated and point to active METPO:1000704, which denotes locomotory flagellar possession, not resorption. Deprecated ciliated METPO:0000093 and METPO:000094 carry OMO:0001000, while METPO:1000385 carries IAO:0000226; no replacement or consider annotation was observed for those or deprecated flagellum METPO:1000123, whose reason is OMO:0001000. Historical terms are not exact xrefs and are not reactivated. https://github.com/berkeleybop/metpo/issues/521 records unresolved reason-code interpretation. Upstream's bacterial/archaeal focus requires maintainer review of this microbial-eukaryote proposal. The ontology pin stays unchanged. Proposal v609 reserves METPO:1068600 in 1068600-1068699; neither upstream release nor human sign-off is implied.

discussions.prompt: Keep the phenotype separate from universal disassembly or sequence-based mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: The studies discuss different models of axonemal disassembly. Do not require a universal tip-to-base direction, basal severing site, tubulin modification, IFT defect, calcium threshold, stimulus or cell-cycle transition. Induced and mutant observations support the phenotype without becoming natural canonical exemplars. A protein-resolved graph requires taxon-paired authority-checked accessions and edge-specific experiments. A gene, domain, motif or sequence profile alone does not establish organelle resorption. Mechanisms are deferred, not claimed absent. No exact synonyms or mappings are asserted.

label: exocytosis
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell releases material from an intracellular membrane-bounded compartment to the cell exterior through a fusion pore between the compartment membrane and the plasma membrane.

evidence.snippet: The cytoplasm between the two matching membrane sites is squeezed away and the membranes fuse
evidence.notes: PMID:4629881, PMC2108847. Scientific Abstract directly read in Europe PMC XML and PubMed. The quote retains the source's missing terminal punctuation. Freeze-fracture/etch observations in the historically named Tetrahymena pyriformis system connect mucocyst-plasma-membrane fusion, opening enlargement and contents release. Fixation triggers some discharge. Abstract-level evidence does not establish a universal pore size or fusion machinery. The XML has sparse body content and the PDF endpoint returned HTML; full methods, figures and strain provenance were not inspected.

evidence.snippet: Upon returning the cells to the permissive temperature the contents of the accumulated vesicles were secreted.
evidence.notes: PMID:1744905. Scientific Abstract directly read in NCBI PubMed XML and Europe PMC metadata, which agree on the DOI. Constitutive secretion in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is examined using temperature-sensitive sec mutants, accumulated vesicles and blocked protein synthesis. Calcium perturbations did not affect the measured release under these conditions; this does not establish calcium irrelevance in every yeast context. No universal rate or requirement for extracellular stimulation is inferred. Full methods, figures and strain provenance remain unread.

evidence.snippet: This is a detailed characterization of a secretory mutant incapable of releasing secretory contents despite normal exocytotic membrane fusion performance.
evidence.notes: PMID:9681197. Scientific Abstract verified in PubMed XML and Europe PMC metadata. Relevant Methods, Results and Discussion were read in the primary PDF at https://d-nb.info/1107191386/34; pages 349-350 and 354-356, including Figures 6-9, were visually inspected. Paramecium caudatum tnd1 retains condensed cargo despite fusion and extracellular fluorochrome access. Figure 9 shows untriggered mutant cells, not a wildtype experiment. This supports separation of fusion and discharge, not tnd1 as a positive example of completed secretion. Reduced calcium binding is a proposed explanation, not a proven molecular lesion. Other figures and tables were not visually audited.

discussions.prompt: Separate the secretion phenotype from its component steps.
discussions.rationale: This concerns secretion by the microbe, not a host-cell response. Docking, intracellular trafficking or fusion alone does not demonstrate cargo release. Transporter-mediated export, membrane budding, lysis, cell-cell fusion and endocytosis are not equivalents. Constitutive and stimulus-regulated secretion are included; total emptying, permanent vesicle collapse and a shared calcium response are not required. GO:0006887 was resolved at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/GO%3A0006887 and includes partial secretion through transient pores, but denotes a biological process rather than an equivalent organismal phenotype. No xref or synonym is inferred. The obsolete METPO secretion classes are broader, not exact replacements or usable parents. Retain phenotype METPO:1000059 pending human mapping review.

discussions.prompt: Resolve natural strain provenance and route-specific mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Canonical examples remain unset: the historical Tetrahymena strain needs modern taxonomy and provenance review, the yeast experiment uses conditional sec mutants, and the origin of the Paramecium tnd1 mutant has not been independently checked. Do not infer natural or engineered provenance from a mutant label. The fusion-only mutant is boundary evidence, not a positive secretion exemplar. These studies support phenotype scope across experimental systems, not one conserved protein mechanism. Obtain taxon-paired functional evidence and verified accessions before adding protein examples or a causal graph.

label: extracellular membrane vesicle production
definition: A physiological phenotype in which microbial cells give rise to closed, cell-derived lipid-membrane vesicles in the extracellular space.

canonical_examples.note: Type strain PS (= ATCC 35061 = DSM 861). Vesicles were purified from exponentially growing cultures at 37 C in modified DSM 119 medium under H2/CO2 and examined by TEM. The collection record https://www.dsmz.de/collection/catalogue/details/culture/DSM-861 traces PS to a primary sewage digester in Gainesville, not to a human donor; it supplies provenance, not independent vesicle evidence. NCBI Taxonomy resolves this strain to species 2173. This is a culture observation, not direct in-gut vesicle production.

evidence.snippet: Super-resolution microscopy reveals that explosive cell lysis also produces shattered membrane fragments that rapidly form MVs.
evidence.notes: PMID:27075392, PMC4834629. Scientific Abstract, not the editorial teaser, directly read in Europe PMC XML; selected Results and strain/isolation Methods also read. Live super-resolution imaging in Pseudomonas aeruginosa distinguishes vesicles from fragments and supports membrane reassembly after lysis. Lys dependence in biofilms/stress does not extend to ordinary oxic planktonic cultures, where the lys mutant retains comparable MV levels. Reporter/deletion/rescue experiments are qualified observations, not proof of one universal route. Actual panels and supplements were not visually inspected.

evidence.snippet: Through these openings, cytoplasmic membrane material protrudes into the extracellular space and is released as MVs.
evidence.notes: PMID:28883390, PMC5589764. Scientific Abstract, separate from the appended teaser, and selected Results/Methods directly read in Europe PMC XML. The openings are endolysin-associated peptidoglycan holes in Bacillus subtilis. Live imaging and induced strains support extrusion from cells that ultimately die; tomography uses an engineered skinny ponA deletion, not wild-type cells. Static tomographic stages are not a measured time sequence. This route differs from explosive-fragment reassembly. This study and the 2016 paper share investigators; they are not independent-laboratory replications. Actual panels were not visually inspected.

evidence.snippet: Bilayered vesicles with diameters at the 100–300 nm range were found in extracellular fractions from yeast cultures.
evidence.notes: PMID:20559436, PMC2885426. Scientific Abstract and Methods s2a-s2c, Results s3a/s3d directly read in Europe PMC XML. Saccharomyces cerevisiae WT and trafficking mutants yield vesicles after supernatant fractionation and TEM. Heat-killed controls yielded no vesicle-like structures; viability controls were reported without displayed data. SEC/MVB perturbations alter composition and sterol-based release proxies without abolishing production. The abstract's concluding requirement language is not taken as a universal necessity claim. Size is assay-specific; WT denotes laboratory comparators, not verified natural isolates. Actual panels were not visually inspected.

evidence.snippet: The EVs were isolated from exponentially growing M. smithii cultures to limit the contamination of the EV preparations with cell debris.
evidence.notes: PMID:40461479, PMC12134362. Full-text Results Sec3 quote, not an abstract quote, checked in Europe PMC XML. Sec3/Sec7 and Methods Sec10-Sec12 describe PS cultures, density-gradient purification, TEM and particle assays. Instrument detection limits yield different size distributions. Cryo-ET suggests budding and wall passage; the large-vesicle lysis route is hypothesized, not directly demonstrated. DNA/protein cargo annotations do not demonstrate increased methane production. Actual panels and supplements were not visually inspected.

discussions.prompt: Separate vesicle production from particle identity and cargo effects.
discussions.rationale: Include vesicles produced by non-lytic release or membrane reassembly after cell lysis; the producer need not survive. Require evidence for intact extracellular vesicles, not bulk membrane-dye signal, unclosed debris, intracellular organelles, whole daughter cells or virions. Vesicle-associated viral DNA alone does not make a particle a virion. Gas vesicles are proteinaceous intracellular inclusions. Exocytosis traitmech:000637 describes fusion-pore discharge, which need not release an intact vesicle. The yeast source attributes roles to both conventional and unconventional trafficking, so unconventional protein secretion traitmech:000648 is not a universal parent; possible overlap is not disjointness. Outer-membrane vesicles and exosomes are narrower or route-specific usages, not exact synonyms. No universal size, cargo, lipid-bilayer architecture or ecological function is imposed. Retain phenotype METPO:1000059 pending human hierarchy and external mapping review; no exact xref is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Ground separate biogenesis mechanisms without universalizing them.
discussions.rationale: The bacterial sources support distinct endolysin-associated routes; the yeast work supports trafficking contributions; the methanogen's budding and large-vesicle lysis models remain qualified. No common protein apparatus follows from these observations. Before adding route-specific causal graphs, inspect the remaining panels, supplements and strain provenance and resolve the relevant protein accessions with taxon-paired functional evidence. The verified PS exemplar does not ground bacterial Lys or yeast SEC proteins. Do not infer vesicle production from a sequence feature, cargo annotation, membrane blebbing alone or an isolation protocol that mechanically manufactures particles from cells.

label: extracellular-trail-based spatial memory
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microorganism's subsequent spatial exploration is guided by persistent extracellular trails deposited during earlier movement.

evidence.snippet: When one arm contained extracellular slime, 39 of 40 plasmodia chose the blank agar arm
evidence.notes: Reid et al. 2012, PMID:23045640, PMC3491460; Results opening paragraph, printed page 17490 / PDF page 1. Cultured Physarum polycephalum avoided previously deposited slime in a Y maze. Same-stock coatings do not demonstrate individual recognition of one's own trace. In the separate U-trap experiment, 23/24 plasmodia on blank agar versus 8/24 on slime-coated agar reached the target within 120 hours. Coating masks newly informative trails; it does not abolish secretion or lesion internal memory. Success, completion time among successful trials, speed, path length and revisitation are distinct endpoints. No-trap and speed controls do not exclude every environmental confound. Main Methods, Results, Discussion and all four figures were inspected in an author-hosted publisher-formatted PDF bearing a 2012 download stamp, not verified as the current corrected VoR. Supplements and raw data were not assessed. Southern Biological Supplies culture provenance remains unresolved. The contiguous result span was text-matched and visually checked.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that the external memory has an adaptive advantage in ‘open’ and simple bounded environments.
evidence.notes: Smith-Ferguson et al. 2017; scientific abstract, printed page 1 / PDF page 2. This is the authors' interpretation of maze performance, not a measured fitness or natural-selection endpoint. Within 72 hours, blank versus extracellular-slime conditions yielded success in 24/24 versus 9/24 open trials, 12/15 versus 4/12 simple-maze trials and 11/17 versus 11/13 complex-maze trials; the last comparison showed no significant benefit. Completion times conditional on success were not significantly different. Escaped trials were excluded; split decisions used the dominant front. Printed page 6 pairs the same chi-square 0.802 with P=0.004 and P=0.371; this discrepancy is unresolved. Figure 8 is illustrative, not quantified trajectory evidence. Main Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion and all eight figures were inspected; supplements were not. The author-hosted PDF bears a 2017 download stamp, not verified current VoR equivalence. This study shares authors with Reid 2012, not an independent-laboratory replication.

evidence.snippet: In accordance with the literature, we observe that plasmodia generally avoid previously visited areas marked by their slime trail
evidence.notes: Troger et al. 2024, PMID:38517977, PMC10990088; Results, Quantifying Run-and-Tumble and Self-Avoiding Behavior, page 3. The authors report their own Physarum observations, not only a background citation. Actual trajectories, including Figure 2A, are distinct from simulated-model panels. Page 5 describes 14 trajectories divided into groups of nine each; Figure 4 instead gives seven small and seven large. The discrepancy remains unresolved. The 0.65 square-millimeter median is a cohort split, not a universal threshold. Small plasmodia can cross trails; a modeled three-hour forgetting time is not a measured chemical half-life or internal-memory duration. Main text, Methods and all four main figures were inspected in the author-hosted publisher-formatted PDF with a March 2024 download stamp, not verified current corrected VoR equivalence. Publisher supplements and raw data were not reanalyzed. This different laboratory's assay is not a replication of the earlier maze experiments; no universal molecular receptor is established.

discussions.prompt: Keep external trace-guided exploration distinct from internal memory and universal trail avoidance.
discussions.rationale: This operational phenotype concerns spatial information persisting outside the microorganism. It does not require always avoiding a trail, improved navigation in every setting, individual self-recognition, or internal recall. Carbon-source memory (traitmech:000706), acquired stress-resistance memory (traitmech:000712), enhanced transcriptional reactivation memory (traitmech:000713) and behavioral habituation (traitmech:000714) have different endpoints. Negative autotropism (traitmech:000603) concerns germ-tube or hyphal orientation. Collective bacterial predation (traitmech:000701) concerns coordinated killing and feeding, despite a trail mention. Contact-dependent outer membrane exchange (traitmech:000650) concerns actual intercellular exchange. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending hierarchy review; local chemotaxis has a flagellar-specific definition and is not a universal parent. Generic memory, learning, stigmergy and extracellular polymer production are not exact synonyms. Psl-biased visitation and community growth history require separate scope and evidence assessments.

discussions.prompt: Resolve source versions, assay discrepancies and culture provenance before assigning taxa or mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Coated-versus-blank substrates manipulate spatial trace information along with the environment, not exclusively a memory molecule. The 2017 significance-statistic discrepancy and 2024 group-size discrepancy remain visible source gaps. The 2024 arXiv v1 was posted after journal publication; its seven-per-group wording and differing illumination details do not silently correct the publisher-formatted PDF. Supplement illustrations do not establish crossing frequencies. Bounded Crossref/MED and publisher checks do not establish exhaustive absence of notices or corrected-version equivalence. The evidence concerns cultured Physarum, not species-wide possession or all microbes. Natural culture provenance remains unverified. No canonical taxa, exact external mappings, protein examples or molecular causal graph are asserted. Unknown trail components, sensory mechanisms, unread supplements and raw-data reanalysis remain research gaps. Source hashes, access limits and actual native snippet-verifier outcomes are retained in the source-verification sidecar.

discussions.prompt: Retain unresolved historical adaptation and chemotaxis identity without reviving deprecated identifiers.
discussions.rationale: Pinned and inspected current METPO graphs mark METPO:0000248 and METPO:000249 Microbial Adaptation, METPO:1000004 adaptation and METPO:1000062 chemotaxis deprecated. Inspected subjects have no replacement or consider annotations; OMO:0001000 reasons are provisional under open METPO issue 521. Original historical scopes remain unresolved. Neither biological invalidity nor exact equivalence follows from their labels or deprecation reasons. This qualified external-trace phenotype is accepted independently from primary evidence. Ignored and hidden current files, available tracked history, independent copies, pending changes and inspected ontology graphs revealed no exact active record within the documented scope. No historical exact mapping is asserted. Existing records and the pinned ontology remain unchanged; discovery is not exhausted.

label: galvanotaxis
definition: A motile phenotype in which an organism biases its active movement in response to an electric field.

evidence.snippet: movement of a motile organism or cell in direct response to an electric current
evidence.notes: Adler and Shi, publisher's freely accessible Excerpt, https://symposium.cshlp.org/content/53/23.short. The full paywalled paper was not accessed. The disposition requires active motility; passive electrophoretic displacement alone is insufficient.

evidence.snippet: motile Escherichia coli K-12 placed in an electric field swims toward the anode
evidence.notes: Shi, Stocker and Adler, primary abstract (PMID:8576046), verified through Europe PMC. Rough K-12 and smooth Salmonella differ in direction; surface composition and capsules qualify the response. Only the abstract was accessed, not the full paper.

canonical_examples.note: The primary abstract reports anode-directed swimming of motile rough K-12 cells. This is not a claim about every E. coli strain or an invariant direction across surface compositions.

canonical_examples.taxon_label: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. 14028S
canonical_examples.note: Figure 5 and Supplementary Table 1: Green ST is IR715, a nalidixic-acid-resistant 14028S derivative, carrying pGFT/RalFc. These fluorescent cells migrated toward the cathode at 2 V/cm in vitro. Do not substitute the SW473 flagellar mutant or the separate cheB mutant for this behavioral example.

causal_graphs.title: Flagellar motility in electric-field-biased migration
causal_graphs.description: Flagellin supports the motility apparatus used for active galvanotaxis.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The flagellar-motility branch supported in Salmonella 14028S-background cells, not a complete electrical sensing or orientation mechanism. The fliC/fljB double mutant establishes dependence on the flagellar apparatus, not individual FliC necessity or flagellin sufficiency. Host CFTR is outside this microbial graph.

nodes.label: electric field
nodes.description: Applied electrical stimulus, 2 V/cm in the Sun et al. in vitro assay.

nodes.label: flagellin
nodes.description: Flagellin family forming the flagellar filament; not the entire flagellum, its rotary motor or an established electrical sensor.

protein_examples.taxon_label: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. 14028S
protein_examples.role: FliC is one of the two alternative flagellins removed together in SW473; individual FliC necessity was not established.

evidence.snippet: Most of these mutants were non-motile
evidence.notes: Results, flagellar-mutant paragraph and Supplementary Table 1: SW473 is an IR715 fliC/fljB double mutant. The exact 14028S FliC identity, taxon and versions were resolved at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/proteins/api/proteins/A0A0F6B2U2; https://rest.uniprot.org/proteomes/UP000002695.json confirms reference-proteome membership. UniProtKB REST protein requests failed during retrieval; the EBI Proteins API supplied the metadata. This accession anchors the strain background, not an experimentally sequenced SW473 protein.

nodes.label: flagellar motility
nodes.description: Active movement powered by the bacterial flagellar apparatus.

nodes.label: electric-field-biased active migration
nodes.description: Biased active movement, not passive drift of fixed cells.

nodes.label: galvanotaxis
nodes.description: Organismal disposition for electric-field-guided active movement.

edges.subject: galvanotaxis_electric_field
edges.description: An applied electric field biases active migration direction.

evidence.snippet: robustly biased migration of all cells
evidence.notes: Results and Figure 5c-e compare no-field and 2 V/cm conditions. DH5alpha K-12-background cells migrated toward the anode and IR715-background cells toward the cathode. This edge does not prescribe one direction for every microbe.

edges.subject: galvanotaxis_flagellin
edges.description: Flagellin supplies the filament component of the motility apparatus.

evidence.snippet: Flagellin is the subunit protein that polymerises to form the flagella
evidence.notes: InterPro IPR001492 family description, verified through https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/interpro/IPR001492/ on 2026-10-03. This is a family, not merely an N- or C-terminal domain. Filament assembly and the motor are also required; flagellin alone is not sufficient for movement.

edges.subject: galvanotaxis_flagellar_motility
edges.description: Flagellar motility enables active electrical-field-guided migration.

evidence.snippet: flagella are indeed essential for electrical field-guided galvanotaxis
evidence.notes: Results, flagellar-mutant experiment: SW473 cells were mostly non-motile and unresponsive. This establishes a motility requirement, not a specific electrical sensor. Fixed-cell controls distinguish passive drift from live-cell swimming.

edges.subject: galvanotaxis_process
edges.description: Electric-field-guided active movement realizes the galvanotaxis phenotype.

evidence.snippet: migration is toward the cathode or the anode
evidence.notes: Publisher's free Excerpt defines galvanotaxis and allows either pole. Direction depends on organism and context, rather than being a universal part of this trait definition.

discussions.prompt: Resolve electrical orientation mechanisms without equating active motility with passive drift.
discussions.rationale: DOI:10.1128/jb.178.4.1113-1119.1996 proposes differential electrophoretic mobility of the body and flagellar filaments as an orientation model. DOI:10.1038/s41564-024-01778-8 observes flagellar redistribution and a largely non-motile double mutant; it does not establish a universal receptor circuit or separate the individual flagellin contributions. A cheB mutant retains the electrical response. The source's weakly biased B. subtilis assay is not a robust canonical example. Physical orientation can guide powered locomotion, but fixed-cell drift alone is not this phenotype. QuickGO searches for galvanotaxis and electrotaxis found no exact term on 2026-10-03; MeSH Taxis Response is broader and excluded from xrefs. GO:0071973 grounds only the flagellar process.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile directedness signs before importing numerical source-data values.
discussions.rationale: Sun et al., Figure 5d and Results report negative directedness for E. coli and positive for Salmonella. The source workbook's Fig. 5d,e sheet labels Red to anode and Green to cathode but contains opposite-signed cosine values. Direction labels agree with Figure 5c and the 1996 primary abstract; the coordinate conventions need reconciliation. No numerical directedness values are imported and no correction is inferred. label: galvanotropism
definition: A phenotype in which growth is directionally oriented or reoriented in response to an electric field.

evidence.snippet: Field-treated (but not control) Enterobacter cloacae and Escherichia coli cells curved rapidly toward the anode.
evidence.notes: Abstract, exact-matched at Europe PMC (PMID:8300526; PMCID:PMC205108); full text not inspected. Curvature depended on field strength and pH and reversed with field polarity. The authors report controls excluding passive bending and field-induced gradients of tropic substances in their assay. Bacillus subtilis required a higher field threshold. Spatial wall-growth measurements support growth asymmetry, not a resolved universal electrical sensor. The historical actin-absence premise is not adopted as current biology.

label: gravikinesis
definition: A motile phenotype in which the speed of active propulsion is modulated according to orientation relative to gravity.

evidence.snippet: We confirmed the gravikinesis from the analysis on the swimming of single cells.
evidence.notes: Abstract; full publisher PDF inspected at https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/bss/20/2/20_2_44/_pdf. Methods and Results (pages 45-46, Table 1) distinguish active propulsion from passive drift using subsequent 10-18 mM NiCl2 immobilization of the same cell. The drift controls retained contractile-vacuole activity and lacked visible deformation. Curved-swimmer responses reverse in 72% Percoll; straight-swimmer responses were not significant. Results N=55 and Table 1 straight-swimmer N=57 are unreconciled; no aggregate sample count is asserted. Table and method pages were visually checked.

evidence.snippet: The resulting potential-induced modulation of the speed of propulsion is called gravikinesis because it acts to neutralize, fully or in part, sedimentation.
evidence.notes: Publisher abstract and Europe PMC PMID:11536922 checked. Orientation-dependent membrane-potential changes support a physiological component of propulsion control in Paramecium. The sedimentation-opposing response described here is not a universal sign convention or proof of one receptor in all taxa. The subscription full text was not inspected; no strain, channel accession or full-text-only measurement is inferred.

canonical_examples.note: Curved-swimming cells from 14-20-day early-stationary hay-infusion cultures at 24 C, adapted to KCM (pH 7.2) and selected beneath the water surface. Table 1 supports gravity-dependent active propulsion in the control hypo-density medium. Swimming was recorded before nickel immobilization, which supplied only the passive-drift correction. This is not a universal cell-state claim. NCBI identifier is species-level; no strain accession is supplied.

discussions.prompt: Keep propulsion modulation distinct from orientation and passive drift.
discussions.rationale: Observed upward/downward speed differences alone can arise from sedimentation or flotation; the trait concerns the active propulsion component. Gravitaxis (traitmech:000584) denotes directional bias, and gyrotaxis (traitmech:000583) denotes torque-mediated orientation. These can coexist with gravikinesis; no equivalence, disjointness or parent-child relation among them is asserted. The definition does not require faster upward swimming in every medium. Reconcile sign conventions and source-qualified response classes before adding narrower terms or equivalent external mappings.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact protein and taxon anchors for a mechanistic graph.
discussions.rationale: Mechanism evidence exists: Gebauer's abstract links orientation to membrane potential and propulsion, while Takeda discusses mechanosensitive conductances and ciliary control. The inspected sources do not identify a sequence-resolved gravity receptor. Takeda treats hydraulic pressure as a candidate stimulus needing amplification, not a demonstrated complete molecular pathway. A graph is deferred pending eligible taxon-paired protein examples and source-bounded causal edges. label: gravitaxis

evidence.snippet: Predominantly, E. gracilis shows a negative gravitaxis behavior.

Supplementary Figure 5e, not the main text's 5c, measures flagellar length; Supplementary Table 1 reports comparable, not identical, speeds. These controls do not exclude every flagellar defect. evidence.snippet: the ability to swim preferentially upwards (negative gravitaxis) is primarily the result of upwardly curving trajectories
evidence.notes: Summary (PMID:21112996); publisher main-text Methods, Results and Discussion inspected. Curved trajectories agree with a physical shape-orientation model, but shape and orientation rate were not measured simultaneously in the same individual. This is not proof that all protists lack gravity receptors. Gravikinesis concerns orientation-dependent swimming speed, not the directional phenotype. Equation images and supplementary material were not inspected; no equation-derived or supplement-only claim is asserted.

Wild-type cells from one-week-old boiled-hay-infusion cultures. After several hours in the observation chamber, rotation of the chamber revealed upward-curving swimming tracks (Results, Figure 2). NCBI identifier is species-level; the paper does not supply a resolved strain accession.

label: gyrotaxis
definition: A motile phenotype in which the balance of gravitational and viscous torques biases an organism's swimming orientation.

evidence.snippet: The orientational response to the gravity-viscous torque balance is known as gyrotaxis
evidence.notes: Introduction, page 1; definition checked against the publisher-formatted article deposited by the authors at https://api.repository.cam.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/ac9ccafe-f229-477c-9d59-b7a56cd506a0/content (PMID:36219692; PMC9586295). The second of the introduction's three accumulation mechanisms starts 'The second is response to an external field': it describes swimming in still water and gravitational restoration resisted hydrodynamically, then names this response gyrotaxis. This record follows Zeng's broader usage, not a universal requirement or exclusion of imposed shear. Results, Figures 5-7, and Materials and Methods distinguish gravitational reorientation from wall-contact effects in Heterosigma akashiwo GY-H24. Shape asymmetry and density asymmetry are alternatives; bottom-heaviness is not universal. The full main article was read; supplementary material and movies were not inspected. No gravity-sensing receptor is asserted.

evidence.snippet: The swimming direction, θ, is then set by the balance of viscous and gravitactic torques
evidence.notes: Page 1068, left column beneath Figure 2; the typeset theta in the torque-balance sentence was visually checked because PDF extraction substitutes q. This passage concerns imposed shear. Live-cell experiments are on pages 1067-1069 of the full main article at https://stockerlab.ethz.ch/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/17.-DurhamKesslerStocker_Science2009.pdf (PMID:19229037). Chlamydomonas nivalis and Heterosigma akashiwo formed layers in a depth-varying shear chamber; dead cells did not. Gyrotactic trapping is a population consequence under suitable shear, not the definition of the organismal trait or the cause of every oceanic thin layer. Ocean-scale results are model predictions. The supplement and exact culture identities were not verified; no strain or modern C. nivalis taxon identity is inferred.

canonical_examples.note: GY-H24 culture, examined 3-9 hours into the light phase of a 12-hour light/12-hour dark cycle. Figures 5-7 show gravitational reorientation and wall-modified swimming in a sealed, still-fluid microchannel; upward bias is not asserted for every cell or diurnal phase. This example follows Zeng's explicit still-water usage of gyrotaxis; it is not an imposed-shear experiment. The NCBI identifier is species-level, not a resolved GY-H24 strain accession.

label: haptocyst discharge
definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell releases material from haptocysts to the cell exterior.

evidence.snippet: The fine structure of haptocysts, characteristic organelles of most suctorians, is described during the resting state and the discharge after contact with the prey.
evidence.notes: Benwitz 1984, English abstract reproduced at https://www.nies.go.jp/chiiki1/protoz/refere/id4999/4538.htm, read directly on 2026-10-10. Crossref confirms the DOI, title, author and original 1984 publication; later online dates are not the experiment year. In Ephelota gemmipara the abstract reports prey-contact discharge, continuity of the haptocyst membrane with the tentacle plasma membrane, and attachment of internal haptocyst structures to the perforated prey pellicle.
